document.title: Wisconsin's Model Academic Standards for Science

4DF24770DFE80131FC0668A86D17958E.description: Develop a list of issues that citizens must make decisions about and describe a strategy for becoming informed about the science behind these issues

4DF289C0DFE80131FC0768A86D17958E.description: Show how science has contributed to meeting personal needs, including hygiene, nutrition, exercise, safety, and health care

4DF203B0DFE80131FC0568A86D17958E.description: Using the science themes, identify local and state issues that are helped by science and technology and explain how science and technology can also cause a problem

4DF1BF20DFE80131FC0468A86D17958E.description: Describe how science and technology have helped, and in some cases hindered, progress in providing better food, more rapid information, quicker and safer transportation, and more effective health care

4DF17730DFE80131FC0368A86D17958E.description: Students in Wisconsin will use scientific information and skills to make decisions about themselves, Wisconsin, and the world in which they live.

4DF124D0DFE80131FC0268A86D17958E.description: Science in Personal and Social Perspectives

4DEF8090DFE80131FBFD68A86D17958E.description: Ask questions to find answers about how devices and machines were invented and produced

4DF04C70DFE80131FBFF68A86D17958E.description: Identify the combinations of simple machines in a device used in the home, the workplace, or elsewhere in the community, to make or repair things, or to move goods or people

4DF09460DFE80131FC0068A86D17958E.description: Determine what science discoveries have led to changes in technologies that are being used in the workplace by someone employed locally

4DEFFA50DFE80131FBFE68A86D17958E.description: Discover what changes in technology have occurred in a career chosen by a parent, grandparent, or an adult friend over a long period of time

4DF0D820DFE80131FC0168A86D17958E.description: Identify the technology used by someone employed in a job or position in Wisconsin and explain how the technology helps

4DEF31A0DFE80131FBFC68A86D17958E.description: Students in Wisconsin will demonstrate an understanding of the relationship between science and technology and the ways in which that relationship influences human activities.

4DED0DD0DFE80131FBF568A86D17958E.description: Using the science themes, develop explanations for the connections among living and non-living things in various environments

4DEDA0F0DFE80131FBF768A86D17958E.description: Illustrate the different ways that organisms grow through life stages and survive to produce new members of their type

4DEEA6E0DFE80131FBFA68A86D17958E.description: Investigate how organisms, especially plants, respond to both internal cues (the need for water) and external cues (changes in the environment)

4DEE5620DFE80131FBF968A86D17958E.description: Discover how each organism meets its basic needs for water, nutrients, protection, and energy in order to survive

4DEC81C0DFE80131FBF368A86D17958E.description: Students in Wisconsin will demonstrate an understanding of the characteristics and structures of living things, the processes of life, and how living things interact with one another and their environment.

4DEAD3E0DFE80131FBED68A86D17958E.description: Illustrate human resources used in mining, forestry, farming, and manufacturing in Wisconsin and elsewhere in the world

4DEA23D0DFE80131FBEB68A86D17958E.description: Using the science themes, describe resources used in the home, community, and nation as a whole

4DEA83E0DFE80131FBEC68A86D17958E.description: Using the science themes, find patterns and cycles in the earth's daily, yearly, and long-term changes

4DE9D0C0DFE80131FBEA68A86D17958E.description: Describe the weather commonly found in Wisconsin in terms of clouds, temperature, humidity, and forms of precipitation, and the changes that occur over time, including seasonal changes

4DE98B40DFE80131FBE968A86D17958E.description: Changes in the Earth and Sky

4DE94900DFE80131FBE868A86D17958E.description: Identify celestial objects (stars, sun, moon, planets) in the sky, noting changes in patterns of those objects over time

4DEBAB00DFE80131FBF068A86D17958E.description: Develop descriptions of the land and water masses of the earth and of Wisconsin's rocks and minerals, using the common vocabulary of earth and space science

4DEB6A40DFE80131FBEF68A86D17958E.description: Show that earth materials have different physical and chemical properties, including the properties of soils found in Wisconsin

4DEBEB90DFE80131FBF168A86D17958E.description: Investigate that earth materials are composed of rocks and soils and correctly use the vocabulary for rocks, minerals, and soils during these investigations

4DE8AAC0DFE80131FBE668A86D17958E.description: Students in Wisconsin will demonstrate an understanding of the structure and systems of earth and other bodies in the universe and of their interactions.

4DE67160DFE80131FBDE68A86D17958E.description: Ask questions and make observations to discover the differences between substances that can be touched (matter) and substances that cannot be touched (forms of energy, light, heat, electricity, sound, and magnetism)

4DE5E900DFE80131FBDC68A86D17958E.description: Observe and describe physical events involving objects and develop record-keeping systems to follow these events by measuring and describing changes in their properties, including position relative to another object, motion over time, and position due to forces

4DE59800DFE80131FBDB68A86D17958E.description: Observe and describe physical events in objects at rest or in motion

4DE74370DFE80131FBE168A86D17958E.description: Construct simple models of what is happening to materials and substances undergoing change, using simple instruments or tools to aid observations and collect data

4DE6FB30DFE80131FBE068A86D17958E.description: Observe and describe changes in form, temperature, color, speed, and direction of objects and construct explanations for the changes

4DE78680DFE80131FBE268A86D17958E.description: Understand that substances can exist in different states-solid, liquid, gas

4DE7CC80DFE80131FBE368A86D17958E.description: Group and/or classify objects and substances based on the properties of earth materials

4DE80F70DFE80131FBE468A86D17958E.description: Understand that objects are made of more than one substance, by observing, describing and measuring the properties of earth materials, including properties of size, weight, shape, color, temperature, and the ability to react with other substances

4DE4DA40DFE80131FBD968A86D17958E.description: Students in Wisconsin will demonstrate an understanding of the physical and chemical properties of matter, the forms and properties of energy, and the ways in which matter and energy interact.

4DE2D7F0DFE80131FBD268A86D17958E.description: Ask additional questions that might help focus or further an investigation

4DE27BA0DFE80131FBD168A86D17958E.description: Support their conclusions with logical arguments

4DE328D0DFE80131FBD368A86D17958E.description: Communicate the results of their investigations in ways their audiences will understand by using charts, graphs, drawings, written descriptions, and various other means, to display their answers

4DE41130DFE80131FBD668A86D17958E.description: Use data they have collected to develop explanations and answer questions generated by investigations

4DE38700DFE80131FBD468A86D17958E.description: Use simple science equipment safely and effectively, including rulers, balances, graduated cylinders, hand lenses, thermometers, and computers, to collect data relevant to questions and investigations

4DE3CCE0DFE80131FBD568A86D17958E.description: Select multiple sources of information to help answer questions selected for classroom investigations

4DE45520DFE80131FBD768A86D17958E.description: Use the science content being learned to ask questions, plan investigations, make observations, make predictions, and offer explanations

4DE22580DFE80131FBD068A86D17958E.description: Use the vocabulary of the unifying themes to ask questions about objects, organisms, and events being studied

4DE1E120DFE80131FBCF68A86D17958E.description: Students in Wisconsin will investigate questions using scientific methods and tools, revise their personal understanding to accommodate knowledge, and communicate these understandings to others.

4DE0C2E0DFE80131FBCB68A86D17958E.description: Show how the major developments of scientific knowledge in the earth and space, life and environmental, and physical sciences have changed over time

4DE14BC0DFE80131FBCD68A86D17958E.description: Acquire information about people who have contributed to the development of major ideas in the sciences and learn about the cultures in which these people lived and worked

4DE108C0DFE80131FBCC68A86D17958E.description: Use encyclopedias, source books, texts, computers, teachers, parents, other adults, journals, popular press, and various other sources, to help answer science-related questions and plan investigations

4DE08240DFE80131FBCA68A86D17958E.description: Students in Wisconsin will understand that science is ongoing and inventive, and that scientific understandings have changed over time as new evidence is found.

4DDFB6E0DFE80131FBC768A86D17958E.description: When studying a science-related problem, decide what changes over time are occurring or have occurred

4DDF2110DFE80131FBC568A86D17958E.description: When studying science-related problems, decide which of the science themes are important

4DDFFF10DFE80131FBC868A86D17958E.description: When investigating a science-related problem, decide what data can be collected to determine the most useful explanations

4DDED760DFE80131FBC468A86D17958E.description: When faced with a science-related problem, decide what evidence, models, or explanations previously studied can be used to better understand what is happening now

4DDF68D0DFE80131FBC668A86D17958E.description: When conducting science investigations, ask and answer questions that will help decide the general areas of science being addressed

4DDE7160DFE80131FBC368A86D17958E.description: Students in Wisconsin will understand that there are unifying themes: systems, order, organization, and interactions; evidence, models, and explanations; constancy, change, and measurement; evolution, equilibrium, and energy; form and function among scientific disciplines.

419F63D0DFE80131E75868A86D17958E.description: Create a dance video using technology to enhance the mood of the dance

419DE650DFE80131E75368A86D17958E.description: Add to a video portfolio of dance studies and performances

419BF390DFE80131E74D68A86D17958E.description: Students in Wisconsin will make connections between dance and healthful living.

419B6520DFE80131E74B68A86D17958E.description: Respond to a dance using another discipline (such as create a dance based on a historical event)

419B0DF0DFE80131E74A68A86D17958E.description: Create a dance project illustrating a concept shared with another discipline (such as the idea of positive and negative space, a concept shared by art and dance)

419AC0D0DFE80131E74968A86D17958E.description: Learn from resources in their community (such as people, books, or videos) a folk dance of a different culture or a social dance of a different time period, study the cultural and historical context of that dance, and effectively share the dance and its context with their peers

419A7B00DFE80131E74868A86D17958E.description: Students in Wisconsin will dance to build bridges to other disciplines and cultures.

4199CA20DFE80131E74668A86D17958E.description: Keep a journal of personal responses to dance experiences

41997C00DFE80131E74568A86D17958E.description: Research influential dancers, choreographers, and styles (such as modern, ballet, square, Ghanaian, Middle Eastern)

4198ECE0DFE80131E74368A86D17958E.description: Students in Wisconsin will reflect upon and appreciate dance as an art form past and present.

41981CF0DFE80131E74068A86D17958E.description: Use and explain how different accompaniments (such as sound, music, and spoken text) can affect the meaning of a dance

41974CA0DFE80131E73D68A86D17958E.description: Differentiate between functional and expressive movement

41959CD0DFE80131E73768A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate appropriate audience behavior while watching dance performances, and discuss their opinions about the dances with their peers in a supportive and constructive way

419502E0DFE80131E73568A86D17958E.description: Students in Wisconsin will develop critical and creative thinking through their dance experience.

41929DB0DFE80131E72D68A86D17958E.description: Analyze and discuss the relationship among the arts and other disciplines.

41922050DFE80131E72B68A86D17958E.description: Realize the potential of improvisation as a tool for the enrichment of individual and group expression

4191DD50DFE80131E72A68A86D17958E.description: Respond to various motivational resources such as music, props, costumes, and scenic elements through improvisation

41918610DFE80131E72968A86D17958E.description: Improvise spontaneous dances that range from free-form to structured studies

41911B90DFE80131E72868A86D17958E.description: Use improvisation to explore, discover, and invent movement and to solve movement problems

4190D2A0DFE80131E72768A86D17958E.description: Students in Wisconsin will improvise using movement elements, themes, personal experience, and imagination.

419057C0DFE80131E72568A86D17958E.description: Continue to develop and value a positive body image

418F7A30DFE80131E72268A86D17958E.description: Exhibit control and efficiency while moving

418F3BF0DFE80131E72168A86D17958E.description: Recognize and apply the laws of motion in challenging movement problems, such as acceleration and deceleration, and turning and balancing in asymmetrical shapes

418EFC40DFE80131E72068A86D17958E.description: Students in Wisconsin will use the body as the instrument of expression and use movement as the medium to develop kinesthetic awareness.

418E7AC0DFE80131E71E68A86D17958E.description: Continue to observe and describe movement elements in creative dance studies using appropriate movement/dance vocabulary

418E38E0DFE80131E71D68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate increasing kinesthetic awareness, concentration, and focus in performing movement skills

418DACD0DFE80131E71B68A86D17958E.description: Respond to rhythmic patterns with accuracy

491BD520DFE80131F45B68A86D17958E.description: Intercultural Experiences: Students will travel to communities where the language studied is spoken and/or host someone from a country where the language studied is spoken

491B8C00DFE80131F45A68A86D17958E.description: Further learning: Students will look for opportunities to learn more about languages and cultures

491B2D30DFE80131F45968A86D17958E.description: Understanding: Students will deepen their understanding of other cultures through various avenues; such as cuisine, sports, theatre, dance, and art

491AD8E0DFE80131F45868A86D17958E.description: Careers: Students will investigate careers where skills in another language and/or cross-cultural understanding are needed

491A82A0DFE80131F45768A86D17958E.description: Media: Students will use various media in the language studied for study, work, or pleasure

491A34A0DFE80131F45668A86D17958E.description: Students in Wisconsin will show evidence of becoming life-long learners by using the language for personal enjoyment and enrichment.
comments: Students who study another language are better prepared to be responsible members of their communities because of their global perspective. They have expanded their employment opportunities both at home and abroad and have access to a wider variety of resources where they can pursue topics of personal interest.

4919A1E0DFE80131F45468A86D17958E.description: Communication: Students will exchange information with people locally and around the world through avenues such as penpals, e-mail, videos, speeches, and publications

49194BE0DFE80131F45368A86D17958E.description: Outreach: Students will participate in activities where the ability to communicate in a second language may be beneficial, including business internships, exchange programs, and sister city projects

49190340DFE80131F45268A86D17958E.description: Service: Students will provide service to their school and community through such activities as tutoring, teaching, translating, interpreting, and assisting speakers of other languages

4918BA80DFE80131F45168A86D17958E.description: Students in Wisconsin will use the language both within and beyond the school setting.
comments: As businesses expand domestic and international markets, and as people of the world meet each other more often through face-to-face encounters and/or the use of technology, the need for students to be proficient in other languages becomes critical in order for the United States to maintain international respect and economic competitiveness.

4917C740DFE80131F44E68A86D17958E.description: Characteristics of culture: Students will understand the concept of culture as they compare other cultures to their own

491760C0DFE80131F44D68A86D17958E.description: Comparisons: Students will compare the form, meaning, and importance of certain perspectives, products, and practices in different cultures

49171820DFE80131F44C68A86D17958E.description: Cultural variations: Students will discuss the meaning of perspectives, products, and practices in different cultures

4916CFC0DFE80131F44B68A86D17958E.description: Students in Wisconsin will demonstrate understanding of the concept of culture through comparisons of the cultures studied and their own.
comments: Students who study more than one language continuously compare and contrast the practices of people in different cultures. This helps students understand themselves better and builds understanding of different responses to similar situations.

49163830DFE80131F44968A86D17958E.description: Phonetics: Students will compare the sound-symbol association of English to that of the language studied

4915DDD0DFE80131F44868A86D17958E.description: Cultural characteristics: Students will identify cultural characteristics of language such as formalities, levels of politeness, informal and formal language

49157C60DFE80131F44768A86D17958E.description: Translation: Students will identify words and expressions that have no equivalent in another language

49152960DFE80131F44668A86D17958E.description: Idioms: Students will identify expressions that cannot be translated word for word in order to derive meaning

4914CC70DFE80131F44568A86D17958E.description: Structures: Students will identify cognates (words similar to English), word roots, prefixes, suffixes, and sentence structure to derive meaning

comments: Students who study more than one language gain insight into the nature of their own language and can analyze the power of word choice. They can compare how different language systems express meaning and reflect culture.
49148050DFE80131F44468A86D17958E.description: Students in Wisconsin will demonstrate understanding of the nature of language through comparisons of the language studied and their own.

49138EC0DFE80131F44168A86D17958E.description: Accessing resources: Students will access information in the language studied in order to gain greater insight about other cultures and/or their own

49133FB0DFE80131F44068A86D17958E.description: Popular media: Students will read, view, listen to, and talk about subjects contained in popular media from other countries in order to gain a perspective on other cultures

4912E690DFE80131F43F68A86D17958E.description: Students in Wisconsin will acquire information and recognize the distinctive viewpoints that are available only through a language and its cultures.
comments: Being able to access information in more than one language gives students a much richer base of knowledge. Not only is there a greater choice of resources, but there is also the opportunity to analyze a topic from another culture's perspective, providing students with unique insights.

491239B0DFE80131F43D68A86D17958E.description: Accessing resources: Students will access resources in the language studied on topics being discussed or researched in other classes

4911ECB0DFE80131F43C68A86D17958E.description: Reading and listening: Students will read material, listen to and/or watch programs in the language studies on topics from other classes

49119BF0DFE80131F43B68A86D17958E.description: Speaking and writing: Students will use topics and skills from other school subjects to discuss and/or write in the language studied

491151D0DFE80131F43A68A86D17958E.description: Students in Wisconsin will reinforce and further their knowledge of other disciplines through a language other than English.
comments: The conscious effort to connect the study of languages with other disciplines opens doors to information and experiences that enrich students' entire lives. Students can use information and skills learned in other classes to practice their new language. Conversely, language classes provide additional information to enhance what students learn in other disciplines.

491078C0DFE80131F43768A86D17958E.description: Geography: Students will evaluate the target country's geography with respect to the impact on politics, economics, and history

49102AD0DFE80131F43668A86D17958E.description: Mutual influences: Students will explain the impact of a culture's views on what is happening and could happen in the world today

490FCF90DFE80131F43568A86D17958E.description: Contributions: Students will examine the role and significance of other cultures on the target culture

490F80C0DFE80131F43468A86D17958E.description: Objects and symbols: Students will connect objects and symbols of other cultures to the underlying beliefs and perspectives

490EED00DFE80131F43268A86D17958E.description: Geography: Students will explain the impact of the target country's geography on the people's beliefs, perspectives, and attitudes

490EA460DFE80131F43168A86D17958E.description: Mutual influences: Students will discuss how historical and contemporary influences from other cultures shape people's views of the world and their own attitudes toward issues facing the world

490E52E0DFE80131F43068A86D17958E.description: Contributions: Students will examine the role and significance of the contributions of other cultures in today's world

490DFD50DFE80131F42F68A86D17958E.description: Objects and symbols: Students will research the historic background of objects and symbols and how they came to represent certain cultures

490D6CF0DFE80131F42D68A86D17958E.description: Geography: Students will explain the impact of the target country's geography on daily life

490D2370DFE80131F42C68A86D17958E.description: Mutual influences: Students will identify some historical and contemporary influences from other cultures that impact today's society such as the democratic form of government and environmental concerns

490CD7B0DFE80131F42B68A86D17958E.description: Contributions: Students will identify major contributions and historical figures from the culture studied that are significant in the target cultures

490C8080DFE80131F42A68A86D17958E.description: Objects and symbols: Students will compare objects and symbols, such as flags or currency, from other cultures to those found in their own culture

490BDAE0DFE80131F42868A86D17958E.description: Geography: Students will identify countries, regions, and geographic features where the target language is spoken

490B8A60DFE80131F42768A86D17958E.description: Mutual influences: Students will identify some historical and contemporary influences from other cultures that are significant in their own culture such as explorers and settlers, music, and sports

490B33B0DFE80131F42668A86D17958E.description: Contributions: Students will identify some major contributions and historical figures from the cultures studied that are significant in the target culture

490AD960DFE80131F42568A86D17958E.description: Objects and symbols: Students will identify objects and symbols, such as flags or currency, that are used day-to-day and represent other cultures

490A2960DFE80131F42368A86D17958E.description: Students in Wisconsin will demonstrate an understanding of the relationship between the products and perspectives of the cultures studied.
comments: To respect and appreciate the diversity of their world, students need to learn about the contribution of other cultures to the world and the solutions they offer to problems confronting them. Awareness of these contributions helps students understand how their views and other people's views of the world have been influenced.

49096DD0DFE80131F42168A86D17958E.description: Historical influences: Students can discuss historical and philosophical backgrounds that have influenced a culture's patterns of interaction

490920B0DFE80131F42068A86D17958E.description: Beliefs and attitudes: Students will explain how beliefs, perspectives, and attitudes affect the target countries' position on global issues

4908C900DFE80131F41F68A86D17958E.description: Cultural activities: Students will examine the role and importance of various social activities within the cultures studied (such as religious celebrations, historical events, rites of passage)

49088280DFE80131F41E68A86D17958E.description: Patterns of interaction: Students will interact in a variety of cultural contexts (formal/informal, social/work) with sensitivity and respect

4907F400DFE80131F41C68A86D17958E.description: Historical influences: Students will exhibit broader and deeper knowledge of historical and philosophical backgrounds that explain patterns of interaction

4907A1A0DFE80131F41B68A86D17958E.description: Beliefs and attitudes: Students will discuss and compare beliefs and attitudes within the cultures studied and their own in relation to home, school, community and nation

49074C20DFE80131F41A68A86D17958E.description: Cultural activities: Students will compare and contrast activities from other cultures to their own in relation to home, school, community, and nation

4906C4C0DFE80131F41968A86D17958E.description: Patterns of interaction: Students will interact with respect according to the social and cultural requirements of most social and some formal contexts

49061F40DFE80131F41768A86D17958E.description: Historical influences: Students will begin to be able to explain historical and philosophical reasons for different patterns of interaction

4905C890DFE80131F41668A86D17958E.description: Beliefs and attitudes: Students will identify some common beliefs and attitudes within the cultures studied and compare them to their own beliefs and attitudes

49057240DFE80131F41568A86D17958E.description: Cultural activities: Students will experience cultural and social activities common to students of similar age in the target cultures (such as holiday celebrations, school life, and pastimes)

49052290DFE80131F41468A86D17958E.description: Patterns of interaction: Students will interact with respect using culturally appropriate patterns of behavior in everyday informal and social situations

49048190DFE80131F41268A86D17958E.description: Historical influences: Students will identify reasons for different patterns of interaction

490418F0DFE80131F41168A86D17958E.description: Beliefs and attitudes: Students will identify some common beliefs and attitudes within the cultures studied such as social etiquette or the role of the family

4903B940DFE80131F41068A86D17958E.description: Cultural activities: Students will participate in and learn about age-appropriate cultural activities (such as games, songs, and holiday celebrations)

49036D90DFE80131F40F68A86D17958E.description: Patterns of interaction: Students will observe and imitate appropriate patterns of behavior (such as greetings or gestures) used with friends and family in the cultures studied

4902CF30DFE80131F40D68A86D17958E.description: Students in Wisconsin will demonstrate an understanding of the relationship between the practices and perspectives of the cultures studied.
comments: To fully understand another culture, students need to develop an awareness of another people's way of life, of the patterns of behavior that order their world, and of the traditional ideas, attitudes, and perspectives that guide their behaviors.

4901F410DFE80131F40A68A86D17958E.description: Forms of writing: Students will write formal compositions, research papers, and letters for a variety of purposes

490199F0DFE80131F40968A86D17958E.description: Recounting events: Students will recount a long story with a wide variety of details and descriptions

49013F70DFE80131F40868A86D17958E.description: Directions: Students will give a series of detailed instructions to someone with suggestions in how best to complete the task

4900E6A0DFE80131F40768A86D17958E.description: Speeches: Students will write and present a speech on a topic that has been researched

49008E70DFE80131F40668A86D17958E.description: Oral presentations: Students will present student-created works and authentic literature

48FFEC90DFE80131F40468A86D17958E.description: Forms of writing: Students will write formal compositions and letters for a variety of purposes

48FF98E0DFE80131F40368A86D17958E.description: Recounting events: Students will recount a story with substantive description and detail

48FF4AA0DFE80131F40268A86D17958E.description: Directions: Students will give a series of directions to someone, coaching the person in order to complete the task

48FEFEC0DFE80131F40168A86D17958E.description: Speeches: Students will write and deliver a short speech on a topic of personal interest

48FEA490DFE80131F40068A86D17958E.description: Oral presentations: Students will present student-created works and excerpts of authentic literature

48FDD430DFE80131F3FE68A86D17958E.description: Forms of writing: Students will write short compositions and letters

48FD8EB0DFE80131F3FD68A86D17958E.description: Recounting events: Students will tell a story incorporating some description and detail

48FD4850DFE80131F3FC68A86D17958E.description: Directions: Students will give simple directions to someone in order to complete a multi-step task

48FD0070DFE80131F3FB68A86D17958E.description: Speeches: Students will write and deliver a short presentation about their school or community

48FCB4E0DFE80131F3FA68A86D17958E.description: Oral presentations: Students will present student-created and/or authentic short plays, stories, skits, poems, and songs

48FC14F0DFE80131F3F868A86D17958E.description: Forms of writing: Students will write personal journals and/or brief messages to friends (postcard, letter, or e-mail)

48FBCB40DFE80131F3F768A86D17958E.description: Recounting events: Students will tell a simple story

48FB7F00DFE80131F3F668A86D17958E.description: Directions: Students will give simple commands and make requests of another person or group

48FB3440DFE80131F3F568A86D17958E.description: Speeches: Students will write and present a short narrative about themselves

48FAEA50DFE80131F3F468A86D17958E.description: Oral presentations: Students will dramatize student-created and/or authentic songs, short poems, skits, or dialogues

48FA48B0DFE80131F3F268A86D17958E.description: Students in Wisconsin will present information, concepts, and ideas to an audience of listeners or readers on a variety of topics in a language other than their own.
comments: Students must develop strong speaking and writing skills to communicate their thoughts, concepts, and opinions effectively to members of other cultures. This standard focuses on presenting information in a way that is appropriate for the audience.

48F9B510DFE80131F3F068A86D17958E.description: Strategies: In addition, students will analyze the author's use of language to understand a written text

48F96290DFE80131F3EF68A86D17958E.description: Reading: Students will comprehend the main idea and supporting ideas, and make inferences in a wide variety of authentic written materials

48F90A30DFE80131F3EE68A86D17958E.description: Reading: Students will understand written materials on a wide variety of topics and in a wide variety of formats

48F89850DFE80131F3ED68A86D17958E.description: Listening: Students will comprehend the main idea and supporting ideas of oral presentations and authentic spoken materials

48F82470DFE80131F3EC68A86D17958E.description: Listening: Students will understand spoken language on a wide variety of topics

48F76690DFE80131F3EA68A86D17958E.description: Strategies: In addition, students will use the dictionary to look up words that cannot be deciphered via previously learned strategies

48F71690DFE80131F3E968A86D17958E.description: Reading: Students will comprehend the main idea and key supporting ideas, and begin to make inferences in selected authentic written materials

48F6BE70DFE80131F3E868A86D17958E.description: Reading: Students will understand more complex written materials on a variety of topics and formats

48F67690DFE80131F3E768A86D17958E.description: Listening: Students will comprehend the main ideas and supporting ideas of oral presentations and selected authentic materials including videos, and radio and television broadcasts

48F62CF0DFE80131F3E668A86D17958E.description: Listening: Students will understand spoken language that incorporates more advanced vocabulary and structures

48F59600DFE80131F3E468A86D17958E.description: Strategies: In addition, students will begin to derive meaning through use of prediction, prefixes, suffixes, root words, words similar to English, contextual clues, and word order

48F545D0DFE80131F3E368A86D17958E.description: Reading: Students will comprehend the main idea and some supporting ideas of selected authentic written materials

48F4F360DFE80131F3E268A86D17958E.description: Reading: Students will understand selected written materials on topics of personal interest

48F4A530DFE80131F3E168A86D17958E.description: Listening: Students will comprehend the main idea and some supporting ideas of selected authentic materials including recordings, broadcasts, and videos

48F44AA0DFE80131F3E068A86D17958E.description: Listening: Students will understand spoken language that incorporates familiar vocabulary and structures

48F38840DFE80131F3DE68A86D17958E.description: Strategies: Students will use previous classroom experience with the language to understand its spoken and written forms

48F33310DFE80131F3DD68A86D17958E.description: Reading: Students will comprehend the main idea of selected, short authentic written materials

48F270B0DFE80131F3DB68A86D17958E.description: Listening: Students will comprehend simple daily conversations on familiar topics and selected, age-appropriate authentic recordings, broadcasts, and videos

48F21070DFE80131F3DA68A86D17958E.description: Listening: Students will understand spoken language on familiar topics that has strong visual support

comments: Students must develop strong listening and reading skills to interpret the concepts, ideas, and opinions expressed by members of other cultures through their media and their literatures. This standard focuses on increasing the level of understanding as students listen to, read, or view materials in a new language.
48F16BE0DFE80131F3D868A86D17958E.description: Students in Wisconsin will understand and interpret a language other than their own in its written and spoken form on a variety of topics.

48F0DEF0DFE80131F3D668A86D17958E.description: Comprehension: Students will ask for clarification and be able to paraphrase to ensure understanding

48F096E0DFE80131F3D568A86D17958E.description: Problem-solving: Students will discuss options and negotiate to solve a problem

48F04BF0DFE80131F3D468A86D17958E.description: Opinions: Students will defend personal preferences, feelings, and opinions with substantive arguments

48EFF860DFE80131F3D368A86D17958E.description: Questions: Students will ask and answer a variety of questions that require elaboration and substantiation of opinions

48EF9D20DFE80131F3D268A86D17958E.description: Conversations: Students will discuss or debate a wide variety of topics from the local to the international level, hypothesizing, convincing, persuading, and negotiating to reach a conclusion

48EEF100DFE80131F3D068A86D17958E.description: Comprehension: Students will ask for clarification and suggest alternative words to ensure understanding

48EE9680DFE80131F3CF68A86D17958E.description: Problem-solving: Students will suggest options for solving problems related to personal needs and needs of others

48EE4330DFE80131F3CE68A86D17958E.description: Opinions: Students will defend personal preferences, feelings, and opinions with more complete explanation

48EDED70DFE80131F3CD68A86D17958E.description: Questions: Students will ask and answer a variety of questions that require followup questions and responses for more information

48EDA4D0DFE80131F3CC68A86D17958E.description: Conversations: Students will discuss and defend an option on selected topics from the local to the international level

48ED09B0DFE80131F3CA68A86D17958E.description: Comprehension: Students will ask for simplification and clarification.

48ECBBB0DFE80131F3C968A86D17958E.description: Problem-solving: Students will give possible solutions to a problem related to a personal need

48EC6E30DFE80131F3C868A86D17958E.description: Opinions: Students will state personal preferences and feelings with some explanation

48EC1D20DFE80131F3C768A86D17958E.description: Questions: Students will ask and answer a variety of questions, giving reasons for their answers

48EBD0C0DFE80131F3C668A86D17958E.description: Conversations: Students will sustain a conversation including descriptions on selected topics about themselves and their state or country

48EB42F0DFE80131F3C468A86D17958E.description: Comprehension: Students will ask for repetition and repeat to ensure understanding

48EAFC30DFE80131F3C368A86D17958E.description: Problem-solving: Students will express personal needs

48EAB000DFE80131F3C268A86D17958E.description: Opinions: Students will state personal preferences and feelings

48EA5920DFE80131F3C168A86D17958E.description: Questions: Students will ask and answer questions, including biographical information

48EA1340DFE80131F3C068A86D17958E.description: Conversations: Students will carry on a short conversation about personal interests, including what they have done, are doing, and are planning to do

48E982F0DFE80131F3BE68A86D17958E.description: Students in Wisconsin will engage in conversations, provide and obtain information, express feelings and emotions, and exchange opinions in a language other than their own.
comments: Students must know how to use the language effectively in order to exchange ideas and information with other people in a culturally appropriate manner. This standard focuses on the goal of learning to engage in conversations.

434D89D0DFE80131E9AB68A86D17958E.description: Listen to and identify, by genre or style, examples of music from various historical periods and world cultures

434D3510DFE80131E9AA68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate audience behavior appropriate for the context and style of music performed

434CE450DFE80131E9A968A86D17958E.description: Students in Wisconsin will relate music to history and culture.

434C48A0DFE80131E9A768A86D17958E.description: Recognize the relationship of music to principles in other disciplines

434C0800DFE80131E9A668A86D17958E.description: Identify terms common in the arts, such as texture, color, form, and movement

434BC6B0DFE80131E9A568A86D17958E.description: Identify ways in which the principles and subject matter of other disciplines taught in the school are interrelated with those of music

434B8440DFE80131E9A468A86D17958E.description: Identify similarities and differences in the meanings of common terms used in the various arts

434B4310DFE80131E9A368A86D17958E.description: Students in Wisconsin will relate music to the other arts and disciplines outside the arts.

434A2620DFE80131E99F68A86D17958E.description: Evaluate the quality of their own performance and the performance of others

4349DF30DFE80131E99E68A86D17958E.description: Evaluate the quality of their own and others' performances and offer constructive suggestions for improvement

434994D0DFE80131E99D68A86D17958E.description: Explain, using appropriate music terminology, personal preferences for specific musical works and styles

43494070DFE80131E99C68A86D17958E.description: Devise criteria for evaluating performances and compositions

4348EBC0DFE80131E99B68A86D17958E.description: Students in Wisconsin will evaluate music and music performances.

43483D30DFE80131E99968A86D17958E.description: Identify simple musical devices, such as form, contrast, and texture

4347F810DFE80131E99868A86D17958E.description: Identify sounds of various band and orchestra instruments

4347B0E0DFE80131E99768A86D17958E.description: Respond through purposeful physical movement to selected prominent music characteristics or to specific music events while listening to music

434762D0DFE80131E99668A86D17958E.description: Identify the sounds of a variety of instruments, including many orchestra and band instruments and instruments from various cultures, as well as male and female adult voices

4346F810DFE80131E99568A86D17958E.description: Use appropriate terminology in explaining music, music notation, music instruments and voices, and music performances

43469C00DFE80131E99468A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate perceptual skills by listening to, answering questions about, and describing music of various styles representing diverse cultures

43465040DFE80131E99368A86D17958E.description: Identify simple music forms upon listening to a given example

434605F0DFE80131E99268A86D17958E.description: Identify phrases and sections of music that are the same, similar, and/or different

4345C140DFE80131E99168A86D17958E.description: Students in Wisconsin will analyze and describe music.

4344DCC0DFE80131E98E68A86D17958E.description: Recognize standard musical symbols of pitch, rhythm, dynamics, and articulation

43449110DFE80131E98D68A86D17958E.description: Read whole, half, quarter, and eighth notes in 2/4, 3/4, 4/4 meter signatures

43443D40DFE80131E98C68A86D17958E.description: Invent a system of nontraditional music notation

4343F020DFE80131E98B68A86D17958E.description: Use standard symbols to notate meter, rhythm, pitch, and dynamics in pattern and/or song

43439920DFE80131E98A68A86D17958E.description: Identify symbols and traditional terms referring to dynamics, tempo, and articulation and interpret them correctly when performing

434346C0DFE80131E98968A86D17958E.description: Use a system (syllables, numbers, or letters) to read simple pitch notation in the treble clef in major keys

4342E820DFE80131E98868A86D17958E.description: Read whole, half, quarter, eighth, and dotted notes and rests in 2/4, 3/4, and 4/4 meter signatures

4342A0A0DFE80131E98768A86D17958E.description: Students in Wisconsin will read and notate music.

4341C620DFE80131E98468A86D17958E.description: Compose simple melodies for their own instrument

43417240DFE80131E98368A86D17958E.description: Explore, in large group settings, compositional devices using sound effects

43410960DFE80131E98268A86D17958E.description: Use a variety of sound sources when composing and arranging

4340C470DFE80131E98168A86D17958E.description: Create and arrange short songs and instrumental pieces within specified guidelines

43407EA0DFE80131E98068A86D17958E.description: Create and arrange music to accompany readings and dramatizations

43403820DFE80131E97F68A86D17958E.description: Students in Wisconsin will compose and arrange music.

433FABF0DFE80131E97D68A86D17958E.description: Play and embellish simple melodies by ear

433F5AE0DFE80131E97C68A86D17958E.description: Echo simple rhythmic and melodic patterns

433F0AE0DFE80131E97B68A86D17958E.description: Improvise short songs and instrumental pieces, using a variety of sound sources, including traditional sounds, sounds available in the classroom, body sounds, and sounds produced by electronic means

433EB6F0DFE80131E97A68A86D17958E.description: Improvise simple rhythmic variations and melodic embellishments on given pentatonic melodies

433E5EC0DFE80131E97968A86D17958E.description: Improvise simple rhythmic and melodic ostinato accompaniments

433E15B0DFE80131E97868A86D17958E.description: Improvise in the same style answers to given rhythmic and melodic questions

433DC800DFE80131E97768A86D17958E.description: Students in Wisconsin will improvise music.

433CEF40DFE80131E97468A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate basic characteristic tone on their instrument

433C6650DFE80131E97268A86D17958E.description: Perform a repertoire of instrumental literature with a level of difficulty of one on a scale of one to six, using dynamic control and demonstrating a basic understanding of key and time signatures

433C18F0DFE80131E97168A86D17958E.description: Perform on at least one instrument, alone and in small groups and large ensembles, with correct posture and playing position

433BB410DFE80131E97068A86D17958E.description: Play independent instrumental parts while other students sing or play contrasting parts

433B6730DFE80131E96F68A86D17958E.description: Play in groups, blending instrumental timbres, matching dynamic levels, and responding to the cues of a conductor

433B1EE0DFE80131E96E68A86D17958E.description: Echo short rhythmic and melodic patterns

433ADC40DFE80131E96D68A86D17958E.description: Play expressively a varied repertoire of music representing diverse genres and styles

433A97B0DFE80131E96C68A86D17958E.description: Play easy rhythmic, melodic, and chordal patterns accurately and independently on rhythmic, melodic, and harmonic classroom instruments

433A48E0DFE80131E96B68A86D17958E.description: Play on pitch, in rhythm, with appropriate dynamics and timbre, and maintain a steady tempo

433A0170DFE80131E96A68A86D17958E.description: Students in Wisconsin will play, alone and with others, a varied repertoire of music on instruments.

43393900DFE80131E96768A86D17958E.description: Sing on pitch using neutral syllables, note names, or solfege

4338F1D0DFE80131E96668A86D17958E.description: Sing in groups, blending vocal timbres, matching dynamic levels, and responding to the cues of the conductor

4338A770DFE80131E96568A86D17958E.description: Sing ostinati, partner songs, and rounds

43385060DFE80131E96468A86D17958E.description: Sing from memory a varied repertoire of songs representing genres and styles from diverse cultures

433806A0DFE80131E96368A86D17958E.description: Sing expressively with appropriate dynamics, phrasing, and interpretation

4337B8A0DFE80131E96268A86D17958E.description: Sing independently, on pitch, and in rhythm with appropriate timbre, diction, and posture, and maintain a steady tempo

433771A0DFE80131E96168A86D17958E.description: Students in Wisconsin will sing, alone and with others, a varied repertoire of music.

document.title: Wisconsin Standards for Physical Education

4F164F70DFE80131FDAB68A86D17958E.description: Describes the impact of physical activity and the result of improved fitness and performance on self-confidence and self-esteem.

4F160BC0DFE80131FDAA68A86D17958E.description: Recognizes physical activity as an opportunity for social and group interaction and to form new relationships.

4F15C5A0DFE80131FDA968A86D17958E.description: Describes the mental benefits of physical activity (e.g., improved concentration, creativity, alertness, etc.).

4F157F70DFE80131FDA868A86D17958E.description: Describes the ways to use body and movement to communicate ideas and feelings in creative dance.

4F1534F0DFE80131FDA768A86D17958E.description: Appreciates the aesthetic and creative aspects of skilled performance.

4F14DE80DFE80131FDA668A86D17958E.description: Seeks personally-challenging experiences in physical activity settings.

4F149920DFE80131FDA568A86D17958E.description: Recognizes the importance of physical activity to keep body systems working together efficiently.

4F145430DFE80131FDA468A86D17958E.description: Recognizes the value of physical activity to reduce stress and improve mood.

4F140FD0DFE80131FDA368A86D17958E.description: Recognizes that participation in regular physical activity reduces the risk of disease (e.g., heart disease, osteoporosis, diabetes, etc.) and injury.

4F13C820DFE80131FDA268A86D17958E.description: Analyzes selected physical experiences for social, emotional, mental, and physical health benefits.

4F136EC0DFE80131FDA168A86D17958E.description: Recognizes that regular physical activity improves the student's fitness level in both skill-related and health-related fitness components.

4F131DF0DFE80131FDA068A86D17958E.description: Values the benefits of physical activity physically, mentally, emotionally, and socially.

4F12CE60DFE80131FD9F68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrates an awareness of the intrinsic values and benefits of participation in physical activity that provides personal meaning.

4F127B60DFE80131FD9E68A86D17958E.description: Values physical activity for health, enjoyment, challenge, self-expression, and/or social interaction.

4F1226D0DFE80131FD9D68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrates cooperation skills needed to accomplish group/team goals in both cooperative and competitive activities.

4F11D210DFE80131FD9C68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrates respect and concern for the safety of others (e.g., physical, emotional, environmental) in word and actions (e.g., using and replacing equipment properly, following safety guidelines/rules of an activity etc.) in adventure and team building activities.

4F1174C0DFE80131FD9B68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrates positive social interaction while in a physical activity setting (e.g., the student gives another student a high five after making a great shot in basketball).

4F112890DFE80131FD9A68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrates appropriate etiquette in activity settings (e.g., while playing golf the student waits for the ball to be played that is farthest from the hole).

4F10E360DFE80131FD9968A86D17958E.description: Demonstrates cooperation and support of students of different gender, race, ethnicity, and ability in a physical activity setting.

4F109EE0DFE80131FD9868A86D17958E.description: Handles situations in an appropriate manner (e.g., calls by officials, boundary lines, etc.) when participating in team sports.

4F0FBB40DFE80131FD9568A86D17958E.description: Demonstrates self-control during conflict (e.g., peer conflicts or an official's decision).

4F0F7410DFE80131FD9468A86D17958E.description: Communicates to teacher and/or peers when problems are observed and uses the problem-solving model to solve or find a solution.

4F0F3030DFE80131FD9368A86D17958E.description: Follows and listens to all directions and asks for help when needed.

4F0EEBE0DFE80131FD9268A86D17958E.description: Makes responsible decisions for personal safety regarding appropriate dress for weather and/or physical activity, use of equipment, and any health concerns (allergies, asthma, etc.).

4F0EA490DFE80131FD9168A86D17958E.description: Identifies the importance of following class and procedures.

4F0E5900DFE80131FD9068A86D17958E.description: Uses time wisely when given the opportunity to work on skill or fitness development without close teacher monitoring.

4F0DBEE0DFE80131FD8E68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrates safe practices, follows rules, etiquette, cooperation and teamwork, ethical behavior, and positive social interaction.

4F0D7030DFE80131FD8D68A86D17958E.description: Exhibits responsible personal and social behavior that respects self and others in physical activity settings.

4F0D20A0DFE80131FD8C68A86D17958E.description: Completes a total body stretching routine with safe stretching techniques.

4F0CC910DFE80131FD8B68A86D17958E.description: Completes a total body resistance training workout with safe lifting procedures (e.g., large muscles first, proper form and balance, correct amount of resistance, rest day, etc.).

4F0C6F90DFE80131FD8A68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrates appropriate training principles and exercise techniques during participation in activities designed to improve physical fitness.

4F0C1FB0DFE80131FD8968A86D17958E.description: Assesses (manually or mechanically with heart rate monitors) and maintains their heart rate in a target heart rate zone for the recommended time while participating in aerobic physical activity.

4F0BBC30DFE80131FD8868A86D17958E.description: Documents individual physical activity in relation to all the health-related components of fitness.

4F0B6210DFE80131FD8768A86D17958E.description: Participates in activities designed to improve or maintain all health-related fitness components both during and outside of school.

4F0B1A10DFE80131FD8668A86D17958E.description: Develops fitness as it relates to aerobic fitness/body composition, muscular fitness, and flexibility.

4F0ACEC0DFE80131FD8568A86D17958E.description: Demonstrates knowledge of all major muscle groups.

4F0A5FD0DFE80131FD8468A86D17958E.description: Demonstrates knowledge of current guidelines for physical activity (60 minutes daily).

4F0A18D0DFE80131FD8368A86D17958E.description: States the differences between moderate and vigorous physical activity as it relates to perceived exertion.

4F09D260DFE80131FD8268A86D17958E.description: Develops, with teacher assistance, an individual plan for improving fitness levels.

4F098DF0DFE80131FD8168A86D17958E.description: Formulates meaningful personal fitness goals based on fitness test results.

4F094780DFE80131FD8068A86D17958E.description: Performs physical fitness test with correct form and/or technique.

4F08FAF0DFE80131FD7F68A86D17958E.description: Defines health-related fitness terminology (e.g., physical fitness, aerobic fitness, body composition, muscle strength, muscle endurance, flexibility).

4F08A3D0DFE80131FD7E68A86D17958E.description: Explains the FITT guidelines as they apply to a training program (e.g., frequency, intensity, time, and type of exercise).

4F084CD0DFE80131FD7D68A86D17958E.description: Knows the various principles of training (threshold, overload, progression, etc.) and how these principles are applied.

4F07A560DFE80131FD7B68A86D17958E.description: Acquires and applies knowledge of the fitness components for overall fitness.

4F075D30DFE80131FD7A68A86D17958E.description: Achieves and maintains a health enhancing level of physical fitness.

4F071770DFE80131FD7968A86D17958E.description: Regulates physical activity behavior by using appropriate practice procedures and training principles.

4F06CB40DFE80131FD7868A86D17958E.description: Documents practice time as specified by their physical education teacher.

4F067C50DFE80131FD7768A86D17958E.description: Maintains a physical activity log documenting progress toward attaining their personal goals.

4F0613B0DFE80131FD7668A86D17958E.description: Maintains a pedometer log for a minimum of two weekdays and one weekend day.

4F05AB20DFE80131FD7568A86D17958E.description: Participates regularly in moderate to vigorous physical activity in and out of school.

4F0556B0DFE80131FD7468A86D17958E.description: Develops a physical activity plan using practice procedures and training principles appropriate to their personal goals, as well as the physical activity pyramid guidelines.

4F050530DFE80131FD7368A86D17958E.description: Sets realistic activity goals of his or her choosing based on interests as well as fitness assessment results.

4F04BEA0DFE80131FD7268A86D17958E.description: Completes a survey to determine personal interests and increase awareness of a broad range of opportunities existing within the community.

4F047A20DFE80131FD7168A86D17958E.description: Plans for physical activity based on personal goals and interests.

4F043350DFE80131FD7068A86D17958E.description: Develops and implements an individual physical activity plan.

4F039B70DFE80131FD6E68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrates an understanding of team play in invasion sports (e.g., basketball, soccer, handball, etc.) by proper positioning, team communication, and team support.

4F033740DFE80131FD6D68A86D17958E.description: Identifies similarities in body position when receiving a serve (e.g., volleyball, badminton, tennis, etc.) and when defending a player (e.g., basketball, soccer, ultimate, etc.) and reasons why they are similar.

4F02E7C0DFE80131FD6C68A86D17958E.description: Explains at least two game tactics involved in invasion sports (e.g., soccer, basketball, handball, etc.).

4F029980DFE80131FD6B68A86D17958E.description: Explains at least two game tactics involved in playing net/wall sports (e.g., tennis, badminton, volleyball, etc.).

4F024F70DFE80131FD6A68A86D17958E.description: Applies cognitive understanding and application to game play as it relates to strategies and tactics.

4F020930DFE80131FD6968A86D17958E.description: Devises and performs a skill after explaining the significance of a biomechanical principle that enhances performance.

4F01BE60DFE80131FD6868A86D17958E.description: Explains force application and how it affects flight path of object.

4F016EA0DFE80131FD6768A86D17958E.description: Detects and corrects errors in alignment in target sports (e.g., archery, golf) based on knowledge of results.

4F012540DFE80131FD6668A86D17958E.description: Describes the critical elements of a sport-specific skill (e.g., basketball free throw, forearm pass, etc.).

4F00DBA0DFE80131FD6568A86D17958E.description: Identifies proper warm-up and cool down procedures as they affect performance and injury prevention.

4F008750DFE80131FD6468A86D17958E.description: Describes basic principles of conditioning (e.g., overload, progression, specificity, regularity, etc.) and how they improve fitness and performance.

4F001690DFE80131FD6368A86D17958E.description: Selects appropriate practice procedures to learn and master skills and movement patterns.

4EFFC670DFE80131FD6268A86D17958E.description: Applies cognitive understanding and application to skill development: Principles of practice, critical elements of skills, and error correction.

4EFF84B0DFE80131FD6168A86D17958E.description: Applies cognitive understanding to improve motor skill development and performance.

4EFF40A0DFE80131FD6068A86D17958E.description: Demonstrates understanding of movement concepts, principles, strategies, and tactics as they apply to the learning and performance of physical activities.

4EFEFD10DFE80131FD5F68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrates correct position in both net/wall and invasion sports for effective defense and offensive coverage.

4EFEB770DFE80131FD5E68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrates technique to place the ball away from an opponent in net/wall sports (e.g., volleyball, tennis, etc.).

4EFE6D10DFE80131FD5D68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrates correct application of force to control distance of object in a target sport (e.g., golf putt, curling, etc.).

4EFE1CE0DFE80131FD5C68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrates a return to base position in net/wall sports (e.g., tennis, badminton, etc.).

4EFDD820DFE80131FD5B68A86D17958E.description: Applies skill application to successful use of skills and sports tactics.

4EFD9020DFE80131FD5A68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrates use of technology (e.g., compass and GPS) in outdoor pursuits such as hiking, backpacking, and snowshoeing.

4EFD4810DFE80131FD5968A86D17958E.description: Demonstrates correct balance techniques (e.g., static and dynamic) in a variety of activities (yoga, Pilates, gymnastics, cooperative activities, etc.).

4EFCFF80DFE80131FD5868A86D17958E.description: Demonstrates the ability to do a one-foot glide and controlled stop while rollerblading.

4EFCAC90DFE80131FD5768A86D17958E.description: Designs and performs dance (or gymnastic) sequences that combine traveling, rolling, balancing, and weight transfer into a smooth, flowing sequence with intentional changes in direction, speed, and flow.

4EFC5780DFE80131FD5668A86D17958E.description: Demonstrates correct alignment in form in a target sport (e.g., archery, golf, curling, etc.) to control direction.

4EFC1050DFE80131FD5568A86D17958E.description: Dribbles a ball while preventing an opponent from stealing the ball in invasion sports (e.g., basketball, soccer).

4EFBBEE0DFE80131FD5468A86D17958E.description: Serves a ball underhand in net/wall sports (e.g., volleyball, pickle ball) using mature form (e.g., stands with feet apart, eyes on ball, pulls arm and shifts weight backward, swings arm and shifts weight forward, contacts ball, and follows through).

4EFB6D70DFE80131FD5368A86D17958E.description: Achieves skill development in modified sport, dance, gymnastics, and outdoor activities.

4EFAF0A0DFE80131FD5268A86D17958E.description: Demonstrates basic and specialized skills, as well as applies those skills tactically, in increasingly complex environments and in combination with other skills.

4EF40610DFE80131FD5168A86D17958E.description: Demonstrates competency in motor skills and movement patterns needed to perform a variety of physical activities.

document.title: Wisconsin's Model Academic Standards for Art and Design Education

426F5990DFE80131E88268A86D17958E.description: Understand that art is created by people of different cultures, expresses different ideas and concepts, and changes over time

426F0030DFE80131E88168A86D17958E.description: Study ways that artists develop personal style that reflects who they are

426EB980DFE80131E88068A86D17958E.description: Understand that nature and other designs can be sources for new ideas

426E76F0DFE80131E87F68A86D17958E.description: Understand the role that personal traits, such as independent thinking, courage, integrity, insight, dedication and patience, play in creating quality art and design

426E31E0DFE80131E87E68A86D17958E.description: Develop a base of knowledge and skills from which to create new ideas

426DEBA0DFE80131E87D68A86D17958E.description: Use their knowledge, intuition, and experiences to develop ideas for artwork

426DA030DFE80131E87C68A86D17958E.description: Students in Wisconsin will use their imaginations and creativity to develop multiple solutions to problems, expand their minds, and create ideas for original works of art and design.

426D08A0DFE80131E87A68A86D17958E.description: Explore the similarities and differences of world cultures by studying their fine arts: music, dance, theatre, literature, and architecture

426CC320DFE80131E87968A86D17958E.description: Know about a range of art activities, such as museum curation, historic preservation, collecting, and writing about art and design

426C7B80DFE80131E87868A86D17958E.description: Use a variety of tools, such as words, numbers, sounds, movements, images, objects, emotions, technology, and spaces, to help understand and communicate about the visual world

426C31E0DFE80131E87768A86D17958E.description: Apply what they know about the nature of life, nature, the physical world, and the human condition to their understanding and creation of art

426BE180DFE80131E87668A86D17958E.description: Invent new artistic forms to communicate ideas and solutions to problems

426B9900DFE80131E87568A86D17958E.description: Connect their knowledge and skills in art to other areas, such as the humanities, sciences, social studies, and technology

426B4FA0DFE80131E87468A86D17958E.description: Students in Wisconsin will make connections among the arts, other disciplines, other cultures, and the world of work.

426A4410DFE80131E87168A86D17958E.description: Develop the ability to reflect and talk about works of art

4269F840DFE80131E87068A86D17958E.description: Understand the difference between original artworks, reproductions, and copies

4269AE40DFE80131E86F68A86D17958E.description: Explore different cultures' concepts of beauty

42694620DFE80131E86E68A86D17958E.description: Learn to use art criticism and aesthetic knowledge in art and design

4268DA80DFE80131E86D68A86D17958E.description: Learn the value of art as a basic part of being human

42688EC0DFE80131E86C68A86D17958E.description: Explore their own ideas about the purposes and meanings of art

42683D10DFE80131E86B68A86D17958E.description: Learn ways philosophers think about art

4267F8E0DFE80131E86A68A86D17958E.description: Learn ways different cultures think about art

4267B210DFE80131E86968A86D17958E.description: Understand how the choice of materials and techniques influences the expressive quality of art

42676AD0DFE80131E86868A86D17958E.description: Begin to understand the purposes and functions of art

42672410DFE80131E86768A86D17958E.description: Students in Wisconsin will reflect upon the nature of art and design and meaning in art and culture.

42668740DFE80131E86568A86D17958E.description: Work independently and collaboratively to produce ideas and works of art

42663B30DFE80131E86468A86D17958E.description: Understand how creating or looking at art brings out feelings

4265CE80DFE80131E86368A86D17958E.description: Understand that art reflects the time and place in which it was created

42657ED0DFE80131E86268A86D17958E.description: Recognize that their own feelings affect how they look at art

42651820DFE80131E86168A86D17958E.description: Talk or write about feelings in a variety of works of art

4264D0C0DFE80131E86068A86D17958E.description: Make art that reflects different feelings

42648DC0DFE80131E85F68A86D17958E.description: Use art to understand their own emotions

42644910DFE80131E85E68A86D17958E.description: Students in Wisconsin will use their senses and emotions through art and design to develop their minds and to improve social relationships.

426364F0DFE80131E85B68A86D17958E.description: Make and interpret photographs and videos

42631410DFE80131E85A68A86D17958E.description: Be able to read complex maps, charts, and plans

42628ED0DFE80131E85868A86D17958E.description: Be able to draw, paint, and sculpt from life

42624B80DFE80131E85768A86D17958E.description: Know how light, shadow, color, distance, and angle of viewing affect sight

426204B0DFE80131E85668A86D17958E.description: Look at things using different methods and tools, such as through a microscope

4261B660DFE80131E85568A86D17958E.description: Students in Wisconsin will develop perception, visual discrimination, and media literacy skills to become visually educated people.

42610360DFE80131E85368A86D17958E.description: Create works of art that have meanings

4260B400DFE80131E85268A86D17958E.description: Analyze the meanings of artworks and design

42605E70DFE80131E85168A86D17958E.description: Know how to find the meanings in artwork

425FFD60DFE80131E85068A86D17958E.description: Know that visual images are important tools for thinking and communicating

425FA260DFE80131E84F68A86D17958E.description: Students in Wisconsin will interpret visual experiences, such as artwork, designed objects, architecture, movies, television, and multimedia images, using a range of subject matter, symbols, and ideas.

425ECB20DFE80131E84C68A86D17958E.description: Revise media productions based on personal reflection

425E7DC0DFE80131E84B68A86D17958E.description: Develop a working knowledge of media production systems

425458F0DFE80131E82A68A86D17958E.description: Know the elements and principles of design

document.title: Wisconsin's Model Academic Standards for Nutrition Education

495DA310DFE80131F4B268A86D17958E.description: List the basic food groups, give examples from each group and use the food groups to plan a meal and snack

495D5800DFE80131F4B168A86D17958E.description: Identify processed foods by source (plants and animal products) and explain how food may change during processing

495D1060DFE80131F4B068A86D17958E.description: Use descriptive words and sensory characteristics to evaluate and classify foods

495CB710DFE80131F4AF68A86D17958E.description: Identify foods by food group and nutrient contributions

comments: Foods are classified in many ways. Awareness of the variety and types of foods available may increase willingness to try unfamiliar foods. Identifying and trying new foods is one of the first steps leading to knowledge of foods. Students who understand why foods are processed, and how foods change during processing establish a foundation for understanding how nutritional content can change with changes in form of a food.
495C65A0DFE80131F4AE68A86D17958E.description: Students in Wisconsin will be able to appreciate and classify foods. They will also demonstrate an interest and appreciation for a variety of foods.

495BC370DFE80131F4AC68A86D17958E.description: Discuss different dietary needs related to food allergies and medical conditions

495B8520DFE80131F4AB68A86D17958E.description: Describe the food customs and habits, or various cultures, and recognize that our culture, ethnicity and health status may impact our food choices

495B44F0DFE80131F4AA68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate respect for others body weight, size, shape, and abilities and identify factors that contribute to differences in people (genetics, lifestyle behaviors, age)

495B01B0DFE80131F4A968A86D17958E.description: Locate supplier(s), source(s) or retail outlet(s) for ethnic foods within the community

495AA6B0DFE80131F4A868A86D17958E.description: Students in Wisconsin will understand that nutritional status and health can be impacted by many factors, and healthy eating must be individualized to meet personal preferences and characteristics.
comments: The Wisconsin population is growing more diverse. Nutritional status is affected by the food choices available and the nutritional adequacy and appropriateness of the food available. In addition, diversity in body size and shape, economic resources and racial and ethnic background may influence and impact food choices.

495A07E0DFE80131F4A668A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of health promotion concepts

4959CAF0DFE80131F4A568A86D17958E.description: Identify key nutrients from each food group and list ways nutrients can promote health and prevent of chronic disease

49598D60DFE80131F4A468A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate the ability to influence and support others in making positive eating and physical activity choices

49594DD0DFE80131F4A368A86D17958E.description: Describe the relationship between food choices and health problems, such as dental caries, osteoporosis, diabetes, obesity, and blood pressure

495908D0DFE80131F4A268A86D17958E.description: Identify avenues of support for eating disorders, and where to go with concerns

4958C770DFE80131F4A168A86D17958E.description: Define the concepts of balance, and moderation as part of a healthy diet

49588350DFE80131F4A068A86D17958E.description: Students in Wisconsin will understand concepts related to personal health promotion and disease prevention, and will practice behaviors to promote health, prevent disease, and reduce health risks.
comments: Making nutritious food choices is a cornerstone of healthy behaviors. Knowledge of nutrition concepts will assist students in making informed choices regarding their lifestyles.

49582D60DFE80131F49F68A86D17958E.description: Nutrition for Health Promotion of Healthy Behaviors

4957C2C0DFE80131F49E68A86D17958E.description: Identify reliable sources of nutrition information

49577860DFE80131F49D68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate how to use food labels to make healthier choices

49573930DFE80131F49C68A86D17958E.description: Differentiate between hunger and non-hunger cues to eating

4956F960DFE80131F49B68A86D17958E.description: Identify examples of how the food companies, advertising, and the media encourage people to buy and use different foods

4956ADC0DFE80131F49A68A86D17958E.description: Plan snacks and/or meals that are consistent with the Food Guidance System

49564E30DFE80131F49968A86D17958E.description: Assess eating habits (meals and snacks), set a personal nutrition goal, and track progress toward achieving this goal

495607C0DFE80131F49868A86D17958E.description: Identify the consequences of consuming too much or too little food

4955CAE0DFE80131F49768A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate the ability to apply a decision-making process to food choices at home and away from home

49558A70DFE80131F49668A86D17958E.description: Students in Wisconsin will understand and use critical thinking and practical reasoning skills to address food choices, nutrition, and health concerns
comments: Critical thinking and practical reasoning are used in everyday problem solving. Students who develop these skills are more likely to approach everyday problem solving more deliberately, with greater flexibility, and increased open-mindedness.

49550580DFE80131F49468A86D17958E.description: Identify points in food preparation where hand washing is needed

49547730DFE80131F49268A86D17958E.description: Describe factors associated with a safe food supply (food handling, production, storage, and preparation techniques)

49543A60DFE80131F49168A86D17958E.description: Explain the relationship between food safety practices and health

4953FD70DFE80131F49068A86D17958E.description: Verbalize how to safely prepare/pack foods

4953BE40DFE80131F48F68A86D17958E.description: Identify and explain the importance of key food safety messages (clean, cook, chill, avoid cross-contamination)

49537BC0DFE80131F48E68A86D17958E.description: Students in Wisconsin will understand/know how to keep food safe for consumption and how to prepare food safely.
comments: Food borne illness is a common and serious consequence of poor hygiene, unsafe food handling and improper food preparation.

4952DC90DFE80131F48C68A86D17958E.description: Describe how factors such as age, physical activity and gender affect nutritional requirements

49529760DFE80131F48B68A86D17958E.description: Compare portion and serving sizes and demonstrate an awareness of the amount of food consumed and the calories and other nutrients consumed as compared to recommended or label amounts

49524DB0DFE80131F48A68A86D17958E.description: Identify recommended amounts of foods from each food group using the food guidance system

49520810DFE80131F48968A86D17958E.description: Explain the concepts of variety, moderation, and balance, and balancing caloric intake and energy expenditure

4951BB70DFE80131F48868A86D17958E.description: Students in Wisconsin will understand the concepts related to and the connections between food choices, eating habits, activity, and healthy growth.
comments: Nutritional needs vary across the lifecycle. Growth and energy are dependent on healthy eating and nutrition. Students who understand the personal relationship of food choices to energy and growth may be more likely to maintain or improve health.

document.title: Common Core State Standards for English Language Arts

4514BD00DFE80131ED1C68A86D17958E.description: Acquire and use accurately grade-appropriate conversational, general academic, and domain-specific words and phrases, including those that signal spatial and temporal relationships (e.g., After dinner that night we went looking for them).
