45140B50DFE80131ED1A68A86D17958E.description: Identify real-life connections between words and their use (e.g., describe people who are friendly or helpful).

4513AD90DFE80131ED1968A86D17958E.description: Distinguish the literal and nonliteral meanings of words and phrases in context (e.g., take steps).

45135730DFE80131ED1868A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of word relationships and nuances in word meanings.

45130A20DFE80131ED1768A86D17958E.description: Use glossaries or beginning dictionaries, both print and digital, to determine or clarify the precise meaning of key words and phrases.

4512BDD0DFE80131ED1668A86D17958E.description: Use a known root word as a clue to the meaning of an unknown word with the same root (e.g., company, companion).

45126D00DFE80131ED1568A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of the new word formed when a known affix is added to a known word (e.g., agreeable/disagreeable, comfortable/uncomfortable, care/careless, heat/preheat).

45120F60DFE80131ED1468A86D17958E.description: Use sentence-level context as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

4511B870DFE80131ED1368A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning word and phrases based on grade 3 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.

45112330DFE80131ED1168A86D17958E.description: Recognize and observe differences between the conventions of spoken and written standard English.

4510D8B0DFE80131ED1068A86D17958E.description: Choose words and phrases for effect.

45108650DFE80131ED0F68A86D17958E.description: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening.

450FD6C0DFE80131ED0D68A86D17958E.description: Consult reference materials, including beginning dictionaries, as needed to check and correct spellings.

450F8860DFE80131ED0C68A86D17958E.description: Use spelling patterns and generalizations (e.g., word families, position-based spellings, syllable patterns, ending rules, meaningful word parts) in writing words.

450F2F20DFE80131ED0B68A86D17958E.description: Use conventional spelling for high-frequency and other studied words and for adding suffixes to base words (e.g., sitting, smiled, cries, happiness).

450E6C70DFE80131ED0968A86D17958E.description: Use commas and quotation marks in dialogue.

450D8A40DFE80131ED0668A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

450D4110DFE80131ED0568A86D17958E.description: Produce simple, compound, and complex sentences.

450C9830DFE80131ED0368A86D17958E.description: Form and use comparative and superlative adjectives and adverbs, and choose between them depending on what is to be modified.

450BF9C0DFE80131ED0168A86D17958E.description: Form and use the simple (e.g., I walked; I walk; I will walk) verb tenses.

450BB0C0DFE80131ED0068A86D17958E.description: Form and use regular and irregular verbs.

450B1460DFE80131ECFE68A86D17958E.description: Form and use regular and irregular plural nouns.

450ACB00DFE80131ECFD68A86D17958E.description: Explain the function of nouns, pronouns, verbs, adjectives, and adverbs in general and their functions in particular sentences.

450A7FC0DFE80131ECFC68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

450963E0DFE80131ECF968A86D17958E.description: Acquire and use accurately a range of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases sufficient for reading, writing, speaking, and listening at the college and career readiness level; demonstrate independence in gathering vocabulary knowledge when encountering an unknown term important to comprehension or expression.

45090360DFE80131ECF868A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

4508B630DFE80131ECF768A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases by using context clues, analyzing meaningful word parts, and consulting general and specialized reference materials, as appropriate.

45080F60DFE80131ECF568A86D17958E.description: Apply knowledge of language to understand how language functions in different contexts, to make effective choices for meaning or style, and to comprehend more fully when reading or listening.

45077420DFE80131ECF368A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

45072890DFE80131ECF268A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

45067230DFE80131ECF068A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Language

45060DF0DFE80131ECEF68A86D17958E.description: Speak in complete sentences when appropriate to task and situation in order to provide requested detail or clarification.

4505BC00DFE80131ECEE68A86D17958E.description: Create engaging audio recordings of stories or poems that demonstrate fluid reading at an understandable pace; add visual displays when appropriate to emphasize or enhance certain facts or details.

450574E0DFE80131ECED68A86D17958E.description: Report on a topic or text, tell a story, or recount an experience with appropriate facts and relevant, descriptive details, speaking clearly at an understandable pace.

45044510DFE80131ECE968A86D17958E.description: Explain their own ideas and understanding in light of the discussion.

45020FB0DFE80131ECE268A86D17958E.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and communicative tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate.

4501B7E0DFE80131ECE168A86D17958E.description: Make strategic use of digital media and visual displays of data to express information and enhance understanding of presentations.

450164A0DFE80131ECE068A86D17958E.description: Present information, findings, and supporting evidence such that listeners can follow the line of reasoning and the organization, development, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

45009590DFE80131ECDE68A86D17958E.description: Evaluate a speaker's point of view, reasoning, and use of evidence and rhetoric.

45004BF0DFE80131ECDD68A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.

44FFFFE0DFE80131ECDC68A86D17958E.description: Prepare for and participate effectively in a range of conversations and collaborations with diverse partners, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly and persuasively.

44FF67D0DFE80131ECDA68A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Speaking and Listening

44FF0950DFE80131ECD968A86D17958E.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of discipline-specific tasks, purposes, and audiences.

44FDE4B0DFE80131ECD568A86D17958E.description: Conduct short research projects that build knowledge about a topic.

44FD3A10DFE80131ECD368A86D17958E.description: With guidance and support from adults, use technology to produce and publish writing (using keyboarding skills) as well as to interact and collaborate with others.

44FCE900DFE80131ECD268A86D17958E.description: With guidance and support from peers and adults, develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, and editing.

44FC9420DFE80131ECD168A86D17958E.description: With guidance and support from adults, produce writing in which the development and organization are appropriate to task and purpose.
comments: (Grade-specific expectations for writing types are defined in standards 1—3 above.)

44FB9BC0DFE80131ECCE68A86D17958E.description: Use temporal words and phrases to signal event order.

44FB46A0DFE80131ECCD68A86D17958E.description: Use dialogue and descriptions of actions, thoughts, and feelings to develop experiences and events or show the response of characters to situations.

44FACD10DFE80131ECCC68A86D17958E.description: Establish a situation and introduce a narrator and/or characters; organize an event sequence that unfolds naturally.

44FA78A0DFE80131ECCB68A86D17958E.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, descriptive details, and clear event sequences.

44FA2690DFE80131ECCA68A86D17958E.description: Provide a concluding statement or section.

44F9BA20DFE80131ECC968A86D17958E.description: Use linking words and phrases (e.g., also, another, and, more, but) to connect ideas within categories of information.

44F96F30DFE80131ECC868A86D17958E.description: Develop the topic with facts, definitions, and details.

44F922A0DFE80131ECC768A86D17958E.description: Introduce a topic and group related information together; include illustrations when useful to aiding comprehension.

44F8D9E0DFE80131ECC668A86D17958E.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine a topic and convey ideas and information clearly.

44F89040DFE80131ECC568A86D17958E.description: Provide a concluding statement or section.

44F83B00DFE80131ECC468A86D17958E.description: Use linking words and phrases (e.g., because, therefore, since, for example) to connect opinion and reasons.

44F7DA00DFE80131ECC368A86D17958E.description: Provide reasons that support the opinion.

44F780E0DFE80131ECC268A86D17958E.description: Introduce the topic or text they are writing about, state an opinion, and create an organizational structure that lists reasons.

44F73330DFE80131ECC168A86D17958E.description: Write opinion pieces on topics or texts, supporting a point of view with reasons.

44F64400DFE80131ECBE68A86D17958E.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of tasks, purposes, and audiences.

44F5A380DFE80131ECBC68A86D17958E.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

44F54EE0DFE80131ECBB68A86D17958E.description: Gather relevant information from multiple print and digital sources, assess the credibility and accuracy of each source, and integrate the information while avoiding plagiarism.

44F502C0DFE80131ECBA68A86D17958E.description: Conduct short as well as more sustained research projects based on focused questions, demonstrating understanding of the subject under investigation.

44F4BB50DFE80131ECB968A86D17958E.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

46A1EEF0DFE80131F02468A86D17958E.description: Analyze in detail the structure of a specific paragraph in a text, including the role of particular sentences in developing and refining a key concept.

46A17D60DFE80131F02368A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including figurative, connotative, and technical meanings; analyze the impact of specific word choices on meaning and tone, including analogies or allusions to other texts.

46A0D4C0DFE80131F02168A86D17958E.description: Analyze how a text makes connections among and distinctions between individuals, ideas, or events (e.g., through comparisons, analogies, or categories).

46A07D30DFE80131F02068A86D17958E.description: Determine a central idea of a text and analyze its development over the course of the text, including its relationship to supporting ideas; provide an objective summary of the text.

46A024B0DFE80131F01F68A86D17958E.description: Cite the textual evidence that most strongly supports an analysis of what the text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text.

469F1190DFE80131F01C68A86D17958E.description: By the end of the year, read and comprehend literature, including stories, dramas, and poems, at the high end of grades 6—8 text complexity band independently and proficiently.

469EBD70DFE80131F01B68A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

469E6940DFE80131F01A68A86D17958E.description: Analyze how a modern work of fiction draws on themes, patterns of events, or character types from myths, traditional stories, or religious works such as the Bible, including describing how the material is rendered new.

469E1440DFE80131F01968A86D17958E.description: Analyze the extent to which a filmed or live production of a story or drama stays faithful to or departs from the text or script, evaluating the choices made by the director or actors.

469CFF00DFE80131F01668A86D17958E.description: Analyze how differences in the points of view of the characters and the audience or reader (e.g., created through the use of dramatic irony) create such effects as suspense or humor.

469C9E20DFE80131F01568A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast the structure of two or more texts and analyze how the differing structure of each text contributes to its meaning and style.

469C2BA0DFE80131F01468A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including figurative and connotative meanings; analyze the impact of specific word choices on meaning and tone, including analogies or allusions to other texts.

469B7E10DFE80131F01268A86D17958E.description: Analyze how particular lines of dialogue or incidents in a story or drama propel the action, reveal aspects of a character, or provoke a decision.

469B2F50DFE80131F01168A86D17958E.description: Determine a theme or central idea of a text and analyze its development over the course of the text, including its relationship to the characters, setting, and plot; provide an objective summary of the text.

469AE180DFE80131F01068A86D17958E.description: Cite the textual evidence that most strongly supports an analysis of what the text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text.

4699BE80DFE80131F00D68A86D17958E.description: Read and comprehend complex literary and informational texts independently and proficiently.

46996F90DFE80131F00C68A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

46991F30DFE80131F00B68A86D17958E.description: Analyze how two or more texts address similar themes or topics in order to build knowledge or to compare the approaches the authors take.

4698CED0DFE80131F00A68A86D17958E.description: Delineate and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, including the validity of the reasoning as well as the relevance and sufficiency of the evidence.

46987A90DFE80131F00968A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate content presented in diverse media and formats, including visually and quantitatively, as well as in words.

document.title: Wisconsin's Model Academic Standards for Theatre

42BBF610DFE80131E91268A86D17958E.description: Rehearse and perform a scene or play for peers and invited guests

42BBAB50DFE80131E91168A86D17958E.description: Make decisions regarding the scene's visual elements (such as where doors are located or where the audience will sit)

42BB70D0DFE80131E91068A86D17958E.description: Create publicity for a dramatic presentation

42BB3630DFE80131E90F68A86D17958E.description: Explain their choices for setting, characters, and other artistic elements

42BAFAD0DFE80131E90E68A86D17958E.description: Use props or furniture to create an environment for drama and create a character with costume pieces

42BABE60DFE80131E90D68A86D17958E.description: Create a scene or play based on a story, another piece of literature, or an idea, with a beginning, middle, and end

42BA7F10DFE80131E90C68A86D17958E.description: Students will think and work as playwrights, designers, managers, and/or directors to create and interpret improvised and scripted scenes.

42B9EBF0DFE80131E90A68A86D17958E.description: Share their comments constructively and supportively within the group

document.title: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics

4C106790DFE80131F88868A86D17958E.description: Compare two decimals to hundredths by reasoning about their size. Recognize that comparisons are valid only when the two decimals refer to the same whole. Record the results of comparisons with the symbols >, =, or <, and justify the conclusions, e.g., by using a visual model.

4C1023B0DFE80131F88768A86D17958E.description: Use decimal notation for fractions with denominators 10 or 100.
comments: For example, rewrite 0.62 as 62/100; describe a length as 0.62 meters; locate 0.62 on a number line diagram.

Students who can generate equivalent fractions can develop strategies for adding fractions with unlike denominators in general. But addition and subtraction with unlike denominators in general is not a requirement at this grade.
For example, express 3/10 as 30/100, and add 3/10 + 4/100 = 34/100.
4C0FD9B0DFE80131F88668A86D17958E.description: Express a fraction with denominator 10 as an equivalent fraction with denominator 100, and use this technique to add two fractions with respective denominators 10 and 100.

4C0F85F0DFE80131F88568A86D17958E.description: Understand decimal notation for fractions, and compare decimal fractions.

4C0F1E90DFE80131F88468A86D17958E.description: Solve word problems involving multiplication of a fraction by a whole number, e.g., by using visual fraction models and equations to represent the problem.
comments: For example, if each person at a party will eat 3/8 of a pound of roast beef, and there will be 5 people at the party, how many pounds of roast beef will be needed? Between what two whole numbers does your answer lie?

4C0ED680DFE80131F88368A86D17958E.description: Understand a multiple of a/b as a multiple of 1/b, and use this understanding to multiply a fraction by a whole number.
comments: For example, use a visual fraction model to express 3 × (2/5) as 6 × (1/5), recognizing this product as 6/5. (In general, n × (a/b) = (n × a)/b.)

4C0E8AB0DFE80131F88268A86D17958E.description: Understand a fraction a/b as a multiple of 1/b.
comments: For example, use a visual fraction model to represent 5/4 as the product 5 × (1/4), recording the conclusion by the equation 5/4 = 5 × (1/4).

4C0E3470DFE80131F88168A86D17958E.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication to multiply a fraction by a whole number.

4C0DD390DFE80131F88068A86D17958E.description: Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions referring to the same whole and having like denominators, e.g., by using visual fraction models and equations to represent the problem.

4C0D75E0DFE80131F87F68A86D17958E.description: Add and subtract mixed numbers with like denominators, e.g., by replacing each mixed number with an equivalent fraction, and/or by using properties of operations and the relationship between addition and subtraction.

4C0D22D0DFE80131F87E68A86D17958E.description: Decompose a fraction into a sum of fractions with the same denominator in more than one way, recording each decomposition by an equation. Justify decompositions, e.g., by using a visual fraction model.

4C0CDA80DFE80131F87D68A86D17958E.description: Understand addition and subtraction of fractions as joining and separating parts referring to the same whole.

4C0C94D0DFE80131F87C68A86D17958E.description: Understand a fraction a/b with a > 1 as a sum of fractions 1/b.

4C0C2B10DFE80131F87B68A86D17958E.description: Build fractions from unit fractions by applying and extending previous understandings of operations on whole numbers.

4C0BDA10DFE80131F87A68A86D17958E.description: Compare two fractions with different numerators and different denominators, e.g., by creating common denominators or numerators, or by comparing to a benchmark fraction such as 1/2. Recognize that comparisons are valid only when the two fractions refer to the same whole. Record the results of comparisons with symbols >, =, or <, and justify the conclusions, e.g., by using a visual fraction model.

4C0B7E40DFE80131F87968A86D17958E.description: Explain why a fraction a/b is equivalent to a fraction (n × a)/(n × b) by using visual fraction models, with attention to how the number and size of the parts differ even though the two fractions themselves are the same size. Use this principle to recognize and generate equivalent fractions.

4C0B3940DFE80131F87868A86D17958E.description: Extend understanding of fraction equivalence and ordering.

comments: Grade 3 expectations in this domain are limited to fractions with denominators 2, 3, 4, 6, and 8.
Grade 4 expectations in this domain are limited to fractions with denominators 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12, and 100

4C0AB120DFE80131F87668A86D17958E.description: Recognize a line of symmetry for a two-dimensional figure as a line across the figure such that the figure can be folded along the line into matching parts. Identify line-symmetric figures and draw lines of symmetry.

4C0A66B0DFE80131F87568A86D17958E.description: Classify two-dimensional figures based on the presence or absence of parallel or perpendicular lines, or the presence or absence of angles of a specified size. Recognize right triangles as a category, and identify right triangles.

4C0A18C0DFE80131F87468A86D17958E.description: Draw points, lines, line segments, rays, angles (right, acute, obtuse), and perpendicular and parallel lines. Identify these in two-dimensional figures.

4C09C2F0DFE80131F87368A86D17958E.description: Draw and identify lines and angles, and classify shapes by properties of their lines and angles.

4C092C30DFE80131F87168A86D17958E.description: Recognize angle measure as additive. When an angle is decomposed into non-overlapping parts, the angle measure of the whole is the sum of the angle measures of the parts. Solve addition and subtraction problems to find unknown angles on a diagram in real world and mathematical problems, e.g., by using an equation with a symbol for the unknown angle measure.

4C08E9E0DFE80131F87068A86D17958E.description: Measure angles in whole-number degrees using a protractor. Sketch angles of specified measure.

4C089E40DFE80131F86F68A86D17958E.description: An angle that turns through n one-degree angles is said to have an angle measure of n degrees.

4C084BF0DFE80131F86E68A86D17958E.description: An angle is measured with reference to a circle with its center at the common endpoint of the rays, by considering the fraction of the circular arc between the points where the two rays intersect the circle. An angle that turns through 1/360 of a circle is called a "one-degree angle," and can be used to measure angles.

4C07EE90DFE80131F86D68A86D17958E.description: Recognize angles as geometric shapes that are formed wherever two rays share a common endpoint, and understand concepts of angle measurement:

4C07A9C0DFE80131F86C68A86D17958E.description: Geometric measurement: understand concepts of angle and measure angles.

comments: For example, from a line plot find and interpret the difference in length between the longest and shortest specimens in an insect collection.
4C064830DFE80131F86768A86D17958E.description: Make a line plot to display a data set of measurements in fractions of a unit (1/2, 1/4, 1/8). Solve problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions by using information presented in line plots.

4C0767D0DFE80131F86B68A86D17958E.description: Apply the area and perimeter formulas for rectangles in real world and mathematical problems.
comments: For example, find the width of a rectangular room given the area of the flooring and the length, by viewing the area formula as a multiplication equation with an unknown factor.

4C072530DFE80131F86A68A86D17958E.description: Use the four operations to solve word problems involving distances, intervals of time, liquid volumes, masses of objects, and money, including problems involving simple fractions or decimals, and problems that require expressing measurements given in a larger unit in terms of a smaller unit. Represent measurement quantities using diagrams such as number line diagrams that feature a measurement scale.

4C06DFF0DFE80131F86968A86D17958E.description: Know relative sizes of measurement units within one system of units including km, m, cm; kg, g; lb, oz.; l, ml; hr, min, sec. Within a single system of measurement, express measurements in a larger unit in terms of a smaller unit. Record measurement equivalents in a two column table.
comments: For example, know that 1 ft is 12 times as long as 1 in. Express the length of a 4 ft snake as 48 in. Generate a conversion table for feet and inches listing the number pairs (1, 12), (2, 24), (3, 36), …

4C069BC0DFE80131F86868A86D17958E.description: Solve problems involving measurement and conversion of measurements from a larger unit to a smaller unit.

4C042B00DFE80131F86068A86D17958E.description: Find whole-number quotients and remainders with up to four-digit dividends and one-digit divisors, using strategies based on place value, the properties of operations, and/or the relationship between multiplication and division. Illustrate and explain the calculation by using equations, rectangular arrays, and/or area models.

4C03DE80DFE80131F85F68A86D17958E.description: Multiply a whole number of up to four digits by a one-digit whole number, and multiply two two-digit numbers, using strategies based on place value and the properties of operations. Illustrate and explain the calculation by using equations, rectangular arrays, and/or area models.

4C038FC0DFE80131F85E68A86D17958E.description: Fluently add and subtract multi-digit whole numbers using the standard algorithm.

4C033EE0DFE80131F85D68A86D17958E.description: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to perform multi-digit arithmetic.

4C054CC0DFE80131F86468A86D17958E.description: Use place value understanding to round multi-digit whole numbers to any place.

4C0508D0DFE80131F86368A86D17958E.description: Read and write multi-digit whole numbers using base-ten numerals, number names, and expanded form. Compare two multi-digit numbers based on meanings of the digits in each place, using >, =, and < symbols to record the results of comparisons.

comments: For example, recognize that 700 ÷ 70 = 10 by applying concepts of place value and division.
4C04BF60DFE80131F86268A86D17958E.description: Recognize that in a multi-digit whole number, a digit in one place represents ten times what it represents in the place to its right.

4C047110DFE80131F86168A86D17958E.description: Generalize place value understanding for multi-digit whole numbers.

4C02D8E0DFE80131F85C68A86D17958E.description: Number and Operations in Base Ten
comments: Grade 4 expectations in this domain are limited to whole numbers less than or equal to 1,000,000.

For example, given the rule "Add 3" and the starting number 1, generate terms in the resulting sequence and observe that the terms appear to alternate between odd and even numbers. Explain informally why the numbers will continue to alternate in this way.
4C028E70DFE80131F85B68A86D17958E.description: Generate a number or shape pattern that follows a given rule. Identify apparent features of the pattern that were not explicit in the rule itself.

4C020CF0DFE80131F85968A86D17958E.description: Find all factor pairs for a whole number in the range 1—100. Recognize that a whole number is a multiple of each of its factors. Determine whether a given whole number in the range 1—100 is a multiple of a given one-digit number. Determine whether a given whole number in the range 1—100 is prime or composite.

4C01CBE0DFE80131F85868A86D17958E.description: Gain familiarity with factors and multiples.

4C0187A0DFE80131F85768A86D17958E.description: Solve multistep word problems posed with whole numbers and having whole-number answers using the four operations, including problems in which remainders must be interpreted. Represent these problems using equations with a letter standing for the unknown quantity. Assess the reasonableness of answers using mental computation and estimation strategies including rounding.

4C014240DFE80131F85668A86D17958E.description: Multiply or divide to solve word problems involving multiplicative comparison, e.g., by using drawings and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem, distinguishing multiplicative comparison from additive comparison.

4C00F340DFE80131F85568A86D17958E.description: Interpret a multiplication equation as a comparison, e.g., interpret 35 = 5 × 7 as a statement that 35 is 5 times as many as 7 and 7 times as many as 5. Represent verbal statements of multiplicative comparisons as multiplication equations.

4C00AFF0DFE80131F85468A86D17958E.description: Use the four operations with whole numbers to solve problems.

4C000F30DFE80131F85268A86D17958E.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.
comments: Mathematically proficient students notice if calculations are repeated, and look both for general methods and for shortcuts. Upper elementary students might notice when dividing 25 by 11 that they are repeating the same calculations over and over again, and conclude they have a repeating decimal. By paying attention to the calculation of slope as they repeatedly check whether points are on the line through (1, 2) with slope 3, middle school students might abstract the equation (y – 2)/(x – 1) = 3. Noticing the regularity in the way terms cancel when expanding (x – 1)(x + 1), (x – 1)(x² + x + 1), and (x – 1)(x³ + x² + x + 1) might lead them to the general formula for the sum of a geometric series. As they work to solve a problem, mathematically proficient students maintain oversight of the process, while attending to the details. They continually evaluate the reasonableness of their intermediate results.

4BFFC0F0DFE80131F85168A86D17958E.description: Look for and make use of structure.
comments: Mathematically proficient students look closely to discern a pattern or structure. Young students, for example, might notice that three and seven more is the same amount as seven and three more, or they may sort a collection of shapes according to how many sides the shapes have. Later, students will see 7 × 8 equals the well remembered 7 × 5 + 7 × 3, in preparation for learning about the distributive property. In the expression x² + 9x + 14, older students can see the 14 as 2 × 7 and the 9 as 2 + 7. They recognize the significance of an existing line in a geometric figure and can use the strategy of drawing an auxiliary line for solving problems. They also can step back for an overview and shift perspective. They can see complicated things, such as some algebraic expressions, as single objects or as being composed of several objects. For example, they can see 5 – 3(x – y)² as 5 minus a positive number times a square and use that to realize that its value cannot be more than 5 for any real numbers x and y.

Mathematically proficient students try to communicate precisely to others. They try to use clear definitions in discussion with others and in their own reasoning. They state the meaning of the symbols they choose, including using the equal sign consistently and appropriately. They are careful about specifying units of measure, and labeling axes to clarify the correspondence with quantities in a problem. They calculate accurately and efficiently, express numerical answers with a degree of precision appropriate for the problem context. In the elementary grades, students give carefully formulated explanations to each other. By the time they reach high school they have learned to examine claims and make explicit use of definitions.

Mathematically proficient students consider the available tools when solving a mathematical problem. These tools might include pencil and paper, concrete models, a ruler, a protractor, a calculator, a spreadsheet, a computer algebra system, a statistical package, or dynamic geometry software. Proficient students are sufficiently familiar with tools appropriate for their grade or course to make sound decisions about when each of these tools might be helpful, recognizing both the insight to be gained and their limitations. For example, mathematically proficient high school students analyze graphs of functions and solutions generated using a graphing calculator. They detect possible errors by strategically using estimation and other mathematical knowledge. When making mathematical models, they know that technology can enable them to visualize the results of varying assumptions, explore consequences, and compare predictions with data. Mathematically proficient students at various grade levels are able to identify relevant external mathematical resources, such as digital content located on a website, and use them to pose or solve problems. They are able to use technological tools to explore and deepen their understanding of concepts.

Mathematically proficient students can apply the mathematics they know to solve problems arising in everyday life, society, and the workplace. In early grades, this might be as simple as writing an addition equation to describe a situation. In middle grades, a student might apply proportional reasoning to plan a school event or analyze a problem in the community. By high school, a student might use geometry to solve a design problem or use a function to describe how one quantity of interest depends on another. Mathematically proficient students who can apply what they know are comfortable making assumptions and approximations to simplify a complicated situation, realizing that these may need revision later. They are able to identify important quantities in a practical situation and map their relationships using such tools as diagrams, two-way tables, graphs, flowcharts and formulas. They can analyze those relationships mathematically to draw conclusions. They routinely interpret their mathematical results in the context of the situation and reflect on whether the results make sense, possibly improving the model if it has not served its purpose.

4BFE7BD0DFE80131F84D68A86D17958E.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.
comments: Mathematically proficient students understand and use stated assumptions, definitions, and previously established results in constructing arguments. They make conjectures and build a logical progression of statements to explore the truth of their conjectures. They are able to analyze situations by breaking them into cases, and can recognize and use counterexamples. They justify their conclusions, communicate them to others, and respond to the arguments of others. They reason inductively about data, making plausible arguments that take into account the context from which the data arose. Mathematically proficient students are also able to compare the effectiveness of two plausible arguments, distinguish correct logic or reasoning from that which is flawed, and—if there is a flaw in an argument—explain what it is. Elementary students can construct arguments using concrete referents such as objects, drawings, diagrams, and actions. Such arguments can make sense and be correct, even though they are not generalized or made formal until later grades. Later, students learn to determine domains to which an argument applies. Students at all grades can listen or read the arguments of others, decide whether they make sense, and ask useful questions to clarify or improve the arguments.

Mathematically proficient students make sense of quantities and their relationships in problem situations. They bring two complementary abilities to bear on problems involving quantitative relationships: the ability to decontextualize—to abstract a given situation and represent it symbolically and manipulate the representing symbols as if they have a life of their own, without necessarily attending to their referents—and the ability to contextualize, to pause as needed during the manipulation process in order to probe into the referents for the symbols involved. Quantitative reasoning entails habits of creating a coherent representation of the problem at hand; considering the units involved; attending to the meaning of quantities, not just how to compute them; and knowing and flexibly using different properties of operations and objects.

4BFDDDE0DFE80131F84B68A86D17958E.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.
comments: Mathematically proficient students start by explaining to themselves the meaning of a problem and looking for entry points to its solution. They analyze givens, constraints, relationships, and goals. They make conjectures about the form and meaning of the solution and plan a solution pathway rather than simply jumping into a solution attempt. They consider analogous problems, and try special cases and simpler forms of the original problem in order to gain insight into its solution. They monitor and evaluate their progress and change course if necessary. Older students might, depending on the context of the problem, transform algebraic expressions or change the viewing window on their graphing calculator to get the information they need. Mathematically proficient students can explain correspondences between equations, verbal descriptions, tables, and graphs or draw diagrams of important features and relationships, graph data, and search for regularity or trends. Younger students might rely on using concrete objects or pictures to help conceptualize and solve a problem. Mathematically proficient students check their answers to problems using a different method, and they continually ask themselves, "Does this make sense?" They can understand the approaches of others to solving complex problems and identify correspondences between different approaches.

document.title: Common Core State Standards for English Language Arts

45AF3320DFE80131EE6068A86D17958E.description: Acquire and use accurately grade-appropriate general academic and domain-specific words and phrases, including those that signal contrast, addition, and other logical relationships (e.g., however, although, nevertheless, similarly, moreover, in addition).

45AE1C60DFE80131EE5D68A86D17958E.description: Interpret figurative language, including similes and metaphors, in context.

45ADD640DFE80131EE5C68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

45AD8ED0DFE80131EE5B68A86D17958E.description: Consult reference materials (e.g., dictionaries, glossaries, thesauruses), both print and digital, to find the pronunciation and determine or clarify the precise meaning of key words and phrases.

45ABC6C0DFE80131EE5568A86D17958E.description: Expand, combine, and reduce sentences for meaning, reader/listener interest, and style.

45AB7A60DFE80131EE5468A86D17958E.description: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening.

45AADD70DFE80131EE5268A86D17958E.description: Spell grade-appropriate words correctly, consulting references as needed.

45AA5CA0DFE80131EE5168A86D17958E.description: Use underlining, quotation marks, or italics to indicate titles of works.

45AA0D00DFE80131EE5068A86D17958E.description: Use a comma to set off the words yes and no (e.g., Yes, thank you), to set off a tag question from the rest of the sentence (e.g., It's true, isn't it?), and to indicate direct address (e.g., Is that you, Steve?).

45A83F90DFE80131EE4B68A86D17958E.description: Recognize and correct inappropriate shifts in verb tense.

45A7A390DFE80131EE4968A86D17958E.description: Form and use the perfect (e.g., I had walked; I have walked; I will have walked) verb tenses.

45A75920DFE80131EE4868A86D17958E.description: Explain the function of conjunctions, prepositions, and interjections in general and their function in particular sentences.

45A70B80DFE80131EE4768A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

45A62810DFE80131EE4468A86D17958E.description: Acquire and use accurately a range of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases sufficient for reading, writing, speaking, and listening at the college and career readiness level; demonstrate independence in gathering vocabulary knowledge when encountering an unknown term important to comprehension or expression.

45A5DAC0DFE80131EE4368A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

45A587C0DFE80131EE4268A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases by using context clues, analyzing meaningful word parts, and consulting general and specialized reference materials, as appropriate.

45A4D680DFE80131EE4068A86D17958E.description: Apply knowledge of language to understand how language functions in different contexts, to make effective choices for meaning or style, and to comprehend more fully when reading or listening.

45A44840DFE80131EE3E68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

45A40180DFE80131EE3D68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

45A2E080DFE80131EE3A68A86D17958E.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and tasks, using formal English when appropriate to task and situation.

45909000DFE80131EE0168A86D17958E.description: Conduct short as well as more sustained research projects based on focused questions, demonstrating understanding of the subject under investigation.

document.title: Wisconsin's Model Academic Standards for Nutrition Education

49784980DFE80131F4E168A86D17958E.description: Explain the role of food manufacturing in a global economy, including the negative and positive ramifi cations of food processing and importing/exporting

49780490DFE80131F4E068A86D17958E.description: Describe the relationship between the food guidance system and the Dietary Standards for Americans

4977BAA0DFE80131F4DF68A86D17958E.description: Explain why foods are processed, analyze how foods change during processing (form, texture, additives, nutritional value), and describe how processed foods fit into a food guidance system

497774E0DFE80131F4DE68A86D17958E.description: Identify foods by form, function and source (plant, animal)

497725E0DFE80131F4DD68A86D17958E.description: Students in Wisconsin will be able to appreciate and classify foods. They will also demonstrate an interest and appreciation for a variety of foods.
comments: Foods are classified in many ways. Awareness of the variety and types of foods available may increase willingness to try unfamiliar foods. Identifying and trying new foods is one of the first steps leading to knowledge of foods. Students who understand why foods are processed, and how foods change during processing establish a foundation for understanding how nutritional content can change with changes in form of a food.

49769090DFE80131F4DB68A86D17958E.description: Provide examples of how our health status and belief system may impact our food choices

49764E50DFE80131F4DA68A86D17958E.description: Identify how social and cultural messages about food and eating infl uence nutrition choices

49760E90DFE80131F4D968A86D17958E.description: Evaluate the nutritional and health implications of eating habits of various cultures, economic situations, family traditions and lifestyles

4975BD40DFE80131F4D868A86D17958E.description: Analyze how culture, family traditions and economic situations influence eating and activity behaviors

49757990DFE80131F4D768A86D17958E.description: Examine genetic and cultural connections to weight, size and body shape

497537E0DFE80131F4D668A86D17958E.description: Analyze the availability and variety of affordable and nutritionally adequate foods in the community, including ethnic and other local markets

4974F440DFE80131F4D568A86D17958E.description: Students in Wisconsin will understand that nutritional status and health can be impacted by many factors, and healthy eating must be individualized to meet personal preferences and characteristics.
comments: The Wisconsin population is growing more diverse. Nutritional status is affected by the food choices available and the nutritional adequacy and appropriateness of the food available. In addition, diversity in body size and shape, economic resources and racial and ethnic background may influence and impact food choices.

497470A0DFE80131F4D368A86D17958E.description: Describe how food choices are influenced by availability, individual and family preferences, and the media

document.title: Wisconsin Standards for Health Education

4A1035C0DFE80131F60068A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate conviction in encouraging others to make positive health choices.

4A0FECB0DFE80131F5FF68A86D17958E.description: Implement an advocacy plan for a health issue.

4A0FAAF0DFE80131F5FE68A86D17958E.description: Develop a plan to advocate for a personal, family, or community health issue.

4A0F63D0DFE80131F5FD68A86D17958E.description: Implement an advocacy plan pertaining to a health issue.

4A0F0430DFE80131F5FC68A86D17958E.description: Develop strategies to overcome barriers or resistance to desired health action or behavior.

4A0EA3C0DFE80131F5FB68A86D17958E.description: Apply accurate information to support a health-enhancing message.

4A0E5900DFE80131F5FA68A86D17958E.description: Adapt health-enhancing messages and persuasive communication techniques to a specific target audience.

4A0E0680DFE80131F5F968A86D17958E.description: Apply societal norms to formulate a health-enhancing message.

4A0DC760DFE80131F5F868A86D17958E.description: Develop strategies to advocate for a health issue.

4A0D8830DFE80131F5F768A86D17958E.description: Apply skills to advocate for a health issue.

4A0D46A0DFE80131F5F668A86D17958E.description: Students will demonstrate the ability to advocate for personal, family, and community health.
comments: Advocacy skills help students promote healthy norms and healthy behaviors. This standard helps students develop important skills to target their health- enhancing messages and to encourage others to adopt healthy behaviors

4A0D05F0DFE80131F5F568A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate a variety of behaviors that avoid or reduce health risks to self and others. These include, but are not limited to: various complex safety-related behaviors, appropriately accessing mental and physical health care services, and carefully following medical advice and instructions.

4A0CC0F0DFE80131F5F468A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate a variety of health practices and behaviors that will maintain or improve the health of self and others. These include, but are not limited to: personal behaviors such as regular and health-enhancing physical activity, healthy eating, and accessing appropriate preventive health care services.

4A0C7A50DFE80131F5F368A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate a variety of health-enhancing behaviors.

4A0C3210DFE80131F5F268A86D17958E.description: Analyze the roles of individual responsibility and the health care system in enhancing health.

4A0BEFB0DFE80131F5F168A86D17958E.description: Determine behaviors that will protect and promote health in high risk situations. These may include but are not limited to: refraining from risky sexual behaviors; refraining from alcohol, tobacco, and other drug use; engaging in various forms of physical activity appropriate to current and future life stages; making complex food choices in various food environments to support healthy eating; applying social behaviors to prevent or reduce violence in settings relevant to one's culture; practicing safety-related behaviors in high risk situations; and appropriately accessing health care services for routine preventive care and for illnesses and injuries.

4A0B6AB0DFE80131F5EF68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate age-appropriate, health-enhancing behaviors to reduce health risks.

4A0B2280DFE80131F5EE68A86D17958E.description: Students will demonstrate the ability to use health-enhancing behaviors and avoid or reduce health risks.
comments: Research confirms that the practice of health-enhancing behaviors can contribute to a positive quality of life. In addition, many diseases and injuries can be prevented by reducing harmful and risk-taking behaviors. This standard promotes the acceptance of personal responsibility for health and encourages the practice of health behaviors.

4A0AD020DFE80131F5ED68A86D17958E.description: Implement a plan and monitor progress in achieving a personal health goal.

4A0A7270DFE80131F5EC68A86D17958E.description: Develop a plan to reach a personal health goal that addresses strengths, needs, and risks.

4A0A1950DFE80131F5EB68A86D17958E.description: Formulate an effective long-term personal health goal.

4A09CF90DFE80131F5EA68A86D17958E.description: Apply goal-setting skills to various health-related situations.

4A097CF0DFE80131F5E968A86D17958E.description: Identify strategies that might be utilized to overcome barriers or setbacks.

4A091CB0DFE80131F5E868A86D17958E.description: Evaluate potential barriers or setbacks that may impede one's ability to reach his/her health goal.

4A08CA50DFE80131F5E768A86D17958E.description: Assess personal health practices and their impact on overall health status.

4A088BE0DFE80131F5E668A86D17958E.description: Analyze issues that impact setting a goal.

4A080AB0DFE80131F5E468A86D17958E.description: Students will demonstrate the ability to use goal-setting skills to enhance health.
comments: Goal-setting skills are essential to help students identify, adopt, and maintain health behaviors. This standard includes the critical steps that are needed to achieve both short-term and long-term health goals. These skills make it possible for individuals to have aspirations and plans for the future.

4A07CAC0DFE80131F5E368A86D17958E.description: Evaluate the effectiveness of a health-related decision.

4A078770DFE80131F5E268A86D17958E.description: Defend the healthy choice when making decisions.

4A073E10DFE80131F5E168A86D17958E.description: Predict the potential short-term and long-term impacts of each alternative on self and others.

4A06F330DFE80131F5E068A86D17958E.description: Examine barriers that can hinder healthy decision making.

4A06ADE0DFE80131F5DF68A86D17958E.description: Generate alternatives for health-related issues or problems.

4A0668D0DFE80131F5DE68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate effective decision-making processes related to various complex and relevant health-related situations. These may include but are not limited to: decisions about personal behaviors, decisions related to social behaviors, and use of the health care system.

4A062540DFE80131F5DD68A86D17958E.description: Apply effective decision-making skills to enhance health.

4A05DE10DFE80131F5DC68A86D17958E.description: Justify when individual or collaborative decision making is appropriate.

4A058A80DFE80131F5DB68A86D17958E.description: Identify situations in which using a thoughtful decision-making process would be health-enhancing.

4A052440DFE80131F5DA68A86D17958E.description: Evaluate the impact of a decision-making process on health-related situations.

4A04C810DFE80131F5D968A86D17958E.description: Examine the use of a decision-making process in various health-related situations.

4A048540DFE80131F5D868A86D17958E.description: Students will demonstrate the ability to use decision-making skills to enhance health.
comments: Decision-making skills are needed to identify, implement, and sustain health enhancing behaviors. This standard includes the essential steps that are needed to make healthy decisions. When applied to health issues, the decision-making process enables individuals to collaborate with others to improve their quality of life.

4A044170DFE80131F5D768A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate ways, such as restorative justice practices, to manage or resolve interpersonal conflicts without harming self or others.

4A03F260DFE80131F5D668A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate strategies to prevent interpersonal conflicts.

4A038B50DFE80131F5D568A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate refusal, negotiation, and collaboration skills to enhance health and avoid or reduce health risks.

4A033590DFE80131F5D468A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate communication skills in health-related situations.

4A02F1D0DFE80131F5D368A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate how to ask for and offer assistance to enhance the health of self and others.

4A02AE80DFE80131F5D268A86D17958E.description: Reflect on the impact of communication on enhancing health.

4A025560DFE80131F5D168A86D17958E.description: Analyze communication strategies for effective interaction among family, peers, and others to enhance health.

4A021370DFE80131F5D068A86D17958E.description: Continue to analyze communication skills in various health-related settings.

4A01CCC0DFE80131F5CF68A86D17958E.description: Analyze various communication skills that enhance health and avoid health risks.

4A017D60DFE80131F5CE68A86D17958E.description: Students will demonstrate the ability to use interpersonal communication skills to enhance health and avoid or reduce health risks.
comments: Effective communication enhances personal, family, and community health. This standard focuses on how responsible individuals use verbal and nonverbal skills to develop and maintain healthy personal relationships. The ability to organize and convey information and feelings is the basis for strengthening interpersonal interactions and reducing or avoiding conflict.

4A013360DFE80131F5CD68A86D17958E.description: Evaluate the validity of sources of health information using key criteria.

4A00EE20DFE80131F5CC68A86D17958E.description: Analyze sources of information for validity and reliability.

4A009CF0DFE80131F5CB68A86D17958E.description: Determine when professional health services may be needed and how to access them.

4A004D50DFE80131F5CA68A86D17958E.description: Access health information, products, and services that improve health outcomes.

49FFEF40DFE80131F5C968A86D17958E.description: Determine the availability of information, products, and services that enhance health.

49FFA2C0DFE80131F5C868A86D17958E.description: Continue to apply criteria for choosing accurate sources of information.

49FF5EF0DFE80131F5C768A86D17958E.description: Examine strategies to access valid and reliable sources of health information.

49FF17B0DFE80131F5C668A86D17958E.description: Students will demonstrate the ability to access valid information and products and services to enhance health.
comments: Access to valid health information and health-promoting products and services is critical to prevention, early detection, and treatment of health problems. This standard focuses on how to identify and access valid health information resources and how to reject unproven sources. Application of the skills of analysis, comparison, and evaluation of health resources empowers students to achieve health literacy.

49FED570DFE80131F5C568A86D17958E.description: Predict how various external and internal influences will interact and impact the health behavior of populations.

49FE9050DFE80131F5C468A86D17958E.description: Estimate the impact of internal and external influences on one's own personal health behavior.

49FE4360DFE80131F5C368A86D17958E.description: Examine how social policies can influence health behaviors.

49FDC650DFE80131F5C268A86D17958E.description: Analyze how internal influences, including perception of social norms among peers, can influence individuals' health behaviors and that of certain populations.

49FD7670DFE80131F5C168A86D17958E.description: Analyze how external influences, individually and in combination with others, can influence individuals' health behaviors and that of certain populations.

49FD36C0DFE80131F5C068A86D17958E.description: Analyze the impact of external and internal influences on the health behavior of individuals and populations.

49FCF730DFE80131F5BF68A86D17958E.description: Evaluate how influences impact health behaviors.

49FCB270DFE80131F5BE68A86D17958E.description: Students will analyze the influence of family, peers, culture, media, technology, and other factors on health behaviors.
comments: Health is affected by a variety of positive and negative influences within society. This standard focuses on identifying and understanding the diverse internal and external factors that influence health practices and behaviors among youth, including personal values, beliefs, and perceived norms.

49FC5C20DFE80131F5BD68A86D17958E.description: Examine susceptibility to and severity of injury and illness if engaging in unhealthy behaviors.

49FC1410DFE80131F5BC68A86D17958E.description: Compare the benefits of and barriers to practicing a variety of health behaviors. These may include but are not limited to: refraining from alcohol, tobacco, and other drug use; physical activity; healthy eating; social behaviors to prevent or reduce violence; safety and related behaviors.

49FBCA80DFE80131F5BB68A86D17958E.description: Investigate the relationship between access to health care and health status.

49FB8AA0DFE80131F5BA68A86D17958E.description: Explore factors that impact health status.

49FB4870DFE80131F5B968A86D17958E.description: Analyze how environment and personal health are interrelated.

49FAFD30DFE80131F5B868A86D17958E.description: Predict how personal behaviors and access to appropriate health care can affect health.

49FAAB10DFE80131F5B768A86D17958E.description: Analyze the impact of unhealthy behavior on various dimensions of health (e.g., emotional, mental, physical, social, environmental, and occupational).

49FA5390DFE80131F5B668A86D17958E.description: Examine the interrelationships of various dimensions of health (e.g., emotional, mental, physical, social, environmental, and occupational).

49FA0370DFE80131F5B568A86D17958E.description: Analyze how genetics and family history can affect personal health.

49F9BF40DFE80131F5B468A86D17958E.description: Analyze the impact of determinants of health.

49F97B50DFE80131F5B368A86D17958E.description: Examine and apply health concepts related to health promotion and disease prevention.

49F8E270DFE80131F5B168A86D17958E.description: Students will comprehend concepts related to health promotion and disease prevention to enhance health.
comments: The acquisition of basic health concepts and functional health knowledge provides a foundation for promoting health-enhancing behaviors among youth. This standard includes essential concepts that are based on established health behavior theories and models. Concepts that focus on both health promotion and risk reduction are included in the learning continuum.

document.title: Common Core State Standards for English Language Arts

44205430DFE80131EB3C68A86D17958E.description: Use words and phrases acquired through conversations, reading and being read to, and responding to texts.

44200650DFE80131EB3B68A86D17958E.description: Distinguish shades of meaning among verbs describing the same general action (e.g., walk, march, strut, prance) by acting out the meanings.

441FB170DFE80131EB3A68A86D17958E.description: Identify real-life connections between words and their use (e.g., note places at school that are colorful).

441F5C20DFE80131EB3968A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of frequently occurring verbs and adjectives by relating them to their opposites (antonyms).

441EF2E0DFE80131EB3868A86D17958E.description: Sort common objects into categories (e.g., shapes, foods) to gain a sense of the concepts the categories represent.

441E8AB0DFE80131EB3768A86D17958E.description: With guidance and support from adults, explore word relationships and nuances in word meanings.

441E4380DFE80131EB3668A86D17958E.description: Use the most frequently occurring inflections and affixes (e.g., -ed, -s, re-, un-, pre-, -ful, -less) as a clue to the meaning of an unknown word.

441DFC30DFE80131EB3568A86D17958E.description: Identify new meanings for familiar words and apply them accurately (e.g., knowing duck is a bird and learning the verb to duck).

441DB420DFE80131EB3468A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on kindergarten reading and content.

441C7440DFE80131EB3068A86D17958E.description: Spell simple words phonetically, drawing on knowledge of sound-letter relationships.

441C2150DFE80131EB2F68A86D17958E.description: Write a letter or letters for most consonant and short-vowel sounds (phonemes).

441B86C0DFE80131EB2D68A86D17958E.description: Capitalize the first word in a sentence and the pronoun I.

441B38B0DFE80131EB2C68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

441AE280DFE80131EB2B68A86D17958E.description: Produce and expand complete sentences in shared language activities.

441A9740DFE80131EB2A68A86D17958E.description: Use the most frequently occurring prepositions (e.g., to, from, in, out, on, off, for, of, by, with).

441A4A70DFE80131EB2968A86D17958E.description: Understand and use question words (interrogatives) (e.g., who, what, where, when, why, how).

4419F950DFE80131EB2868A86D17958E.description: Form regular plural nouns orally by adding /s/ or /es/ (e.g., dog, dogs; wish, wishes).

4419A970DFE80131EB2768A86D17958E.description: Use frequently occurring nouns and verbs.

44195740DFE80131EB2668A86D17958E.description: Print many upper- and lowercase letters.

44190370DFE80131EB2568A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

44181900DFE80131EB2268A86D17958E.description: Acquire and use accurately a range of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases sufficient for reading, writing, speaking, and listening at the college and career readiness level; demonstrate independence in gathering vocabulary knowledge when encountering an unknown term important to comprehension or expression.

4417BEE0DFE80131EB2168A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

44175CB0DFE80131EB2068A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases by using context clues, analyzing meaningful word parts, and consulting general and specialized reference materials, as appropriate.

4416A070DFE80131EB1E68A86D17958E.description: Apply knowledge of language to understand how language functions in different contexts, to make effective choices for meaning or style, and to comprehend more fully when reading or listening.

44160220DFE80131EB1C68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

4415AFF0DFE80131EB1B68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

44151E70DFE80131EB1968A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Language

4414D4C0DFE80131EB1868A86D17958E.description: Speak audibly and express thoughts, feelings, and ideas clearly.

441488C0DFE80131EB1768A86D17958E.description: Add drawings or other visual displays to descriptions as desired to provide additional detail.

44143560DFE80131EB1668A86D17958E.description: Describe familiar people, places, things, and events and, with prompting and support, provide additional detail.

441392E0DFE80131EB1468A86D17958E.description: Ask and answer questions in order to seek help, get information, or clarify something that is not understood.

44134990DFE80131EB1368A86D17958E.description: Confirm understanding of a text read aloud or information presented orally or through other media by asking and answering questions about key details and requesting clarification if something is not understood.

44130090DFE80131EB1268A86D17958E.description: Continue a conversation through multiple exchanges.

4412AAE0DFE80131EB1168A86D17958E.description: Follow agreed-upon rules for discussions (e.g., listening to others and taking turns speaking about the topics and texts under discussion).

441254C0DFE80131EB1068A86D17958E.description: Participate in collaborative conversations with diverse partners about kindergarten topics and texts with peers and adults in small and larger groups.

441162A0DFE80131EB0D68A86D17958E.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and communicative tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate.

44110D70DFE80131EB0C68A86D17958E.description: Make strategic use of digital media and visual displays of data to express information and enhance understanding of presentations.

4410AC70DFE80131EB0B68A86D17958E.description: Present information, findings, and supporting evidence such that listeners can follow the line of reasoning and the organization, development, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

44100BF0DFE80131EB0968A86D17958E.description: Evaluate a speaker's point of view, reasoning, and use of evidence and rhetoric.

440FBF50DFE80131EB0868A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.

440F7200DFE80131EB0768A86D17958E.description: Prepare for and participate effectively in a range of conversations and collaborations with diverse partners, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly and persuasively.

440ED050DFE80131EB0568A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Speaking and Listening

440D81A0DFE80131EB0168A86D17958E.description: With guidance and support from adults, recall information from experiences or gather information from provided sources to answer a question.

440D2810DFE80131EB0068A86D17958E.description: Participate in shared research and writing projects (e.g., explore a number of books by a favorite author and express opinions about them).

440CC520DFE80131EAFF68A86D17958E.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

440C6390DFE80131EAFE68A86D17958E.description: With guidance and support from adults, explore a variety of digital tools to produce and publish writing, including in collaboration with peers.

440C16D0DFE80131EAFD68A86D17958E.description: With guidance and support from adults, respond to questions and suggestions from peers and add details to strengthen writing as needed.

440B2A80DFE80131EAFA68A86D17958E.description: Use a combination of drawing, dictating, and writing to narrate a single event or several loosely linked events, tell about the events in the order in which they occurred, and provide a reaction to what happened.

440ADDE0DFE80131EAF968A86D17958E.description: Use a combination of drawing, dictating, and writing to compose informative/explanatory texts in which they name what they are writing about and supply some information about the topic.

440A87A0DFE80131EAF868A86D17958E.description: Use a combination of drawing, dictating, and writing to compose opinion pieces in which they tell a reader the topic or the name of the book they are writing about and state an opinion or preference about the topic or book (e.g., My favorite book is…).

4409A310DFE80131EAF568A86D17958E.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of tasks, purposes, and audiences.

440905B0DFE80131EAF368A86D17958E.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

4408A650DFE80131EAF268A86D17958E.description: Gather relevant information from multiple print and digital sources, assess the credibility and accuracy of each source, and integrate the information while avoiding plagiarism.

44085250DFE80131EAF168A86D17958E.description: Conduct short as well as more sustained research projects based on focused questions, demonstrating understanding of the subject under investigation.

4407F790DFE80131EAF068A86D17958E.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

4407AA10DFE80131EAEF68A86D17958E.description: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce and publish writing and to interact and collaborate with others.

440760B0DFE80131EAEE68A86D17958E.description: Develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach.

44071270DFE80131EAED68A86D17958E.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

44067400DFE80131EAEB68A86D17958E.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, well-chosen details, and well-structured event sequences.

44062510DFE80131EAEA68A86D17958E.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine and convey complex ideas and information clearly and accurately through the effective selection, organization, and analysis of content.

4405D150DFE80131EAE968A86D17958E.description: Write arguments to support claims in an analysis of substantive topics or texts, using valid reasoning and relevant and sufficient evidence.

44052F20DFE80131EAE768A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Writing

4404D080DFE80131EAE668A86D17958E.description: Read emergent-reader texts with purpose and understanding.

44044140DFE80131EAE468A86D17958E.description: Distinguish between similarly spelled words by identifying the sounds of the letters that differ.

4403F970DFE80131EAE368A86D17958E.description: Read common high-frequency words by sight (e.g., the, of, to, you, she, my, is, are, do, does).

4403AE70DFE80131EAE268A86D17958E.description: Associate the long and short sounds with common spellings (graphemes) for the five major vowels.

440354A0DFE80131EAE168A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate basic knowledge of one-to-one letter-sound correspondences by producing the primary or many of the most frequent sound for each consonant.

4402F6D0DFE80131EAE068A86D17958E.description: Know and apply grade-level phonics and word analysis skills in decoding words.

440254F0DFE80131EADE68A86D17958E.description: Add or substitute individual sounds (phonemes) in simple, one-syllable words to make new words.

44020CE0DFE80131EADD68A86D17958E.description: Isolate and pronounce the initial, medial vowel, and final sounds (phonemes) in three-phoneme (consonent-vowel-consonent, or CVC) words. (This does not include CVCs ending with /l/, /r/, or /x/.)

4401C3B0DFE80131EADC68A86D17958E.description: Blend and segment onsets and rimes of single-syllable spoken words.

44017260DFE80131EADB68A86D17958E.description: Count, pronounce, blend, and segment syllables in spoken words.

4400D110DFE80131EAD968A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of spoken words, syllables, and sounds (phonemes).

44001A30DFE80131EAD768A86D17958E.description: Recognize and name all upper- and lowercase letters of the alphabet.

43FFB0E0DFE80131EAD668A86D17958E.description: Understand that words are separated by spaces in print.

43FF5710DFE80131EAD568A86D17958E.description: Recognize that spoken words are represented in written language by specific sequences of letters.

43FF0D70DFE80131EAD468A86D17958E.description: Follow words from left to right, top to bottom, and page by page.

43FEBFA0DFE80131EAD368A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of the organization and basic features of print.

43FDD400DFE80131EAD068A86D17958E.description: Actively engage in group reading activities with purpose and understanding.

43FD6160DFE80131EACF68A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

43FD0920DFE80131EACE68A86D17958E.description: With prompting and support, identify basic similarities in and differences between two texts on the same topic (e.g., in illustrations, descriptions, or procedures).

43FCBCC0DFE80131EACD68A86D17958E.description: With prompting and support, identify the reasons an author gives to support points in a text.

43FC6F00DFE80131EACC68A86D17958E.description: With prompting and support, describe the relationship between illustrations and the text in which they appear (e.g., what person, place, thing, or idea in the text an illustration depicts).

43FBC370DFE80131EACA68A86D17958E.description: Name the author and illustrator of a text and define the role of each in presenting the ideas or information in a text.

43FB71F0DFE80131EAC968A86D17958E.description: Identify the front cover, back cover, and title page of a book.

43FB1960DFE80131EAC868A86D17958E.description: With prompting and support, ask and answer questions about unknown words in a text.

43FA6250DFE80131EAC668A86D17958E.description: With prompting and support, describe the connection between two individuals, events, ideas, or pieces of information in a text.

43FA0780DFE80131EAC568A86D17958E.description: With prompting and support, identify the main topic and retell key details of a text.

43F9C0B0DFE80131EAC468A86D17958E.description: With prompting and support, ask and answer questions about key details in a text.

43F8E9E0DFE80131EAC168A86D17958E.description: Actively engage in group reading activities with purpose and understanding.

43F89960DFE80131EAC068A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

43F845F0DFE80131EABF68A86D17958E.description: With prompting and support, compare and contrast the adventures and experiences of characters in familiar stories.

43F7AF00DFE80131EABD68A86D17958E.description: With prompting and support, describe the relationship between illustrations and the story in which they appear (e.g., what moment in a story an illustration depicts).

43F71040DFE80131EABB68A86D17958E.description: With prompting and support, name the author and illustrator of a story and define the role of each in telling the story.

43F6B2D0DFE80131EABA68A86D17958E.description: Recognize common types of texts (e.g., storybooks, poems).

43F64DA0DFE80131EAB968A86D17958E.description: Ask and answer questions about unknown words in a text.

43F58BB0DFE80131EAB768A86D17958E.description: With prompting and support, identify characters, settings, and major events in a story.

43F539A0DFE80131EAB668A86D17958E.description: With prompting and support, retell familiar stories, including key details.

43F4CD90DFE80131EAB568A86D17958E.description: With prompting and support, ask and answer questions about key details in a text.

43F3DDA0DFE80131EAB268A86D17958E.description: Read and comprehend complex literary and informational texts independently and proficiently.

43F39500DFE80131EAB168A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

43F349C0DFE80131EAB068A86D17958E.description: Analyze how two or more texts address similar themes or topics in order to build knowledge or to compare the approaches the authors take.

43F2F9E0DFE80131EAAF68A86D17958E.description: Delineate and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, including the validity of the reasoning as well as the relevance and sufficiency of the evidence.

43F2A370DFE80131EAAE68A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate content presented in diverse media and formats, including visually and quantitatively, as well as in words.
comments: Please see "Research to Build and Present Knowledge" in Writing and "Comprehension and Collaboration" in Speaking and Listening for additional standards relevant to gathering, assessing, and applying information from print and digital sources.

43F21290DFE80131EAAC68A86D17958E.description: Assess how point of view or purpose shapes the content and style of a text.

43F1C660DFE80131EAAB68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the structure of texts, including how specific sentences, paragraphs, and larger portions of the text (e.g., a section, chapter, scene, or stanza) relate to each other and the whole.

43F170B0DFE80131EAAA68A86D17958E.description: Interpret words and phrases as they are used in a text, including determining technical, connotative, and figurative meanings, and analyze how specific word choices shape meaning or tone.

43F0C000DFE80131EAA868A86D17958E.description: Analyze how and why individuals, events, and ideas develop and interact over the course of a text.

43F07070DFE80131EAA768A86D17958E.description: Determine central ideas or themes of a text and analyze their development; summarize the key supporting details and ideas.

43F01E70DFE80131EAA668A86D17958E.description: Read closely to determine what the text says explicitly and to make logical inferences from it; cite specific textual evidence when writing or speaking to support conclusions drawn from the text.

document.title: Wisconsin's Model Academic Standards for Environmental Education

4DCBCC70DFE80131FBC068A86D17958E.description: Take action in regard to environmental issues in the home, school, or communities

4DCB8270DFE80131FBBF68A86D17958E.description: Write a plan of action based on personal goals of stewardship for an economically and ecologically sustainable environment

4DCB3290DFE80131FBBE68A86D17958E.description: Articulate their personal beliefs regarding their relationship to the environment
comments: (see LA Oral Language)

4DCADED0DFE80131FBBD68A86D17958E.description: Students in Wisconsin will develop an understanding and commitment to environmental stewardship.
