document.title: Wisconsin Standards for Health Education

49E64340DFE80131F5AF68A86D17958E.description: Describe ways to adapt health messages for different audiences.

49E60440DFE80131F5AE68A86D17958E.description: Defend a position relating to a health issue.

49E5C4A0DFE80131F5AD68A86D17958E.description: Apply a plan to advocate for a health issue for people that experience health disparities.

49E58490DFE80131F5AC68A86D17958E.description: Predict how an advocacy plan will influence and support the health status of others.

49E54210DFE80131F5AB68A86D17958E.description: Implement an advocacy plan pertaining to a health issue.

49E4F8D0DFE80131F5AA68A86D17958E.description: Discuss the barriers that could be involved in an advocacy effort.

49E4A3E0DFE80131F5A968A86D17958E.description: Incorporate accurate information as it relates to a health-enhancing position to advocate for self and others.

49E45670DFE80131F5A868A86D17958E.description: Plan ways to advocate for healthy individuals, families, and schools.

49E40060DFE80131F5A768A86D17958E.description: Develop an age-appropriate definition of advocacy.

49E3B120DFE80131F5A668A86D17958E.description: Develop an advocacy plan to promote health.

49E36AB0DFE80131F5A568A86D17958E.description: Develop health-promoting strategies that support family or friends to make positive health choices.

49E322B0DFE80131F5A468A86D17958E.description: Students will demonstrate the ability to advocate for personal, family, and community health.
comments: Advocacy skills help students promote healthy norms and healthy behaviors. This standard helps students develop important skills to target their health- enhancing messages and to encourage others to adopt healthy behaviors

49E2D4B0DFE80131F5A368A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate behaviors that avoid or reduce health risks to self and others.

49E290A0DFE80131F5A268A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate health-enhancing practices and behaviors that help maintain or improve the health of self and others.

49E248F0DFE80131F5A168A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate the role of self-responsibility in enhancing health.

49E1F2D0DFE80131F5A068A86D17958E.description: Evaluate behaviors that maintain or improve the health of self and others. These may include but are not limited to: refraining from risky sexual behaviors; refraining from alcohol, tobacco, and other drug use; engaging in regular and varied physical activity; meal planning that leads to healthy eating; applying social behaviors to prevent or reduce violence; practicing safety-related behaviors in various complex settings; and appropriate use of the health care system.

49E1A480DFE80131F59F68A86D17958E.description: Explain the importance of self-responsibility for personal health behaviors.

49E143D0DFE80131F59E68A86D17958E.description: Apply health-enhancing behaviors that maintain or improve the health of self and others.

49E0E3A0DFE80131F59D68A86D17958E.description: Students will demonstrate the ability to use health-enhancing behaviors and avoid or reduce health risks.
comments: Research confirms that the practice of health-enhancing behaviors can contribute to a positive quality of life. In addition, many diseases and injuries can be prevented by reducing harmful and risk-taking behaviors. This standard promotes the acceptance of personal responsibility for health and encourages the practice of health behaviors.

49E0A3C0DFE80131F59C68A86D17958E.description: Assess the effectiveness of strategies to reach personal health goals.

49E06230DFE80131F59B68A86D17958E.description: Develop goals to maintain or improve personal health status.

49E01FE0DFE80131F59A68A86D17958E.description: Examine how personal health goals can be impacted by various abilities, priorities, and responsibilities that may change throughout the lifespan.

49DFDD60DFE80131F59968A86D17958E.description: Apply goal-setting skills to various health-related situations.

49DF97B0DFE80131F59868A86D17958E.description: Identify strategies that might be utilized to overcome barriers or setbacks.

49DF48D0DFE80131F59768A86D17958E.description: Identify strategies and behaviors needed to maintain or improve health status.

49DEF1F0DFE80131F59668A86D17958E.description: Establish a baseline of personal health behaviors and health status.

49DEA400DFE80131F59568A86D17958E.description: Identify additional steps to setting and achieving realistic health goals.

49DE6420DFE80131F59468A86D17958E.description: Apply goal-setting skills to health situations.

49DE1F20DFE80131F59368A86D17958E.description: Students will demonstrate the ability to use goal-setting skills to enhance health.
comments: Goal-setting skills are essential to help students identify, adopt, and maintain health behaviors. This standard includes the critical steps that are needed to achieve both short-term and long-term health goals. These skills make it possible for individuals to have aspirations and plans for the future.

49DDDBE0DFE80131F59268A86D17958E.description: Analyze the outcome of a health-related decision.

49DD9970DFE80131F59168A86D17958E.description: Predict the impact of each decision on self and others.

49DD5170DFE80131F59068A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate decision making in a health-related situation.

49DD0730DFE80131F58F68A86D17958E.description: Assess the impact of a decision-making process on health-related situations.

49DCC4F0DFE80131F58E68A86D17958E.description: Determine when individual or collaborative decision making is appropriate.

49DC7D10DFE80131F58D68A86D17958E.description: Identify situations where effective decision-making skills are implemented.

49DC17A0DFE80131F58C68A86D17958E.description: Apply a decision-making process in various health-related situations.

49DBAB50DFE80131F58B68A86D17958E.description: Students will demonstrate the ability to use decision-making skills to enhance health.
comments: Decision-making skills are needed to identify, implement, and sustain health enhancing behaviors. This standard includes the essential steps that are needed to make healthy decisions. When applied to health issues, the decision-making process enables individuals to collaborate with others to improve their quality of life.

49DB5FC0DFE80131F58A68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate ways, such as restorative justice practices, to manage or resolve interpersonal conflicts without harming self or others.

49DADA10DFE80131F58868A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate refusal and limit setting skills that avoid health risks.

49DA9AE0DFE80131F58768A86D17958E.description: Apply appropriate communication skills in various health-related settings.

49DA58C0DFE80131F58668A86D17958E.description: Examine the outcomes of using effective and ineffective strategies of communication.

49D9C1E0DFE80131F58468A86D17958E.description: Examine communication strategies in various health-related settings.

49D98240DFE80131F58368A86D17958E.description: Examine and demonstrate communication skills that enhance health and avoid health risks.

49D94010DFE80131F58268A86D17958E.description: Students will demonstrate the ability to use interpersonal communication skills to enhance health and avoid or reduce health risks.
comments: Effective communication enhances personal, family, and community health. This standard focuses on how responsible individuals use verbal and nonverbal skills to develop and maintain healthy personal relationships. The ability to organize and convey information and feelings is the basis for strengthening interpersonal interactions and reducing or avoiding conflict.

49D8FCB0DFE80131F58168A86D17958E.description: Analyze the validity of information about health issues, products, and services.

49D8B880DFE80131F58068A86D17958E.description: Apply models to analyze sources of information for validity and reliability.

49D82A60DFE80131F57E68A86D17958E.description: Locate sources of valid health information from home, school, and community.

49D7E530DFE80131F57D68A86D17958E.description: Describe situations that require accurate health information.

49D79740DFE80131F57C68A86D17958E.description: Identify criteria for choosing accurate sources of information.

49D74780DFE80131F57B68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate and apply strategies to access valid sources of health information.

49D6E160DFE80131F57A68A86D17958E.description: Students will demonstrate the ability to access valid information and products and services to enhance health.
comments: Access to valid health information and health-promoting products and services is critical to prevention, early detection, and treatment of health problems. This standard focuses on how to identify and access valid health information resources and how to reject unproven sources. Application of the skills of analysis, comparison, and evaluation of health resources empowers students to achieve health literacy.

49D689D0DFE80131F57968A86D17958E.description: Examine how one's values and beliefs influence one's own personal health behaviors.

49D63840DFE80131F57868A86D17958E.description: Examine how media and technology influence one's own personal health behaviors.

49D5F720DFE80131F57768A86D17958E.description: Examine how one's family, culture, and peers influence one's own personal health behaviors.

49D5B530DFE80131F57668A86D17958E.description: Provide examples of how factors can interact to influence health behaviors.

49D56EE0DFE80131F57568A86D17958E.description: Examine how external and internal factors can influence health behaviors.

49D4D880DFE80131F57368A86D17958E.description: Examine how internal and external factors influence personal health behaviors.

49D48FD0DFE80131F57268A86D17958E.description: Students will analyze the influence of family, peers, culture, media, technology, and other factors on health behaviors.
comments: Health is affected by a variety of positive and negative influences within society. This standard focuses on identifying and understanding the diverse internal and external factors that influence health practices and behaviors among youth, including personal values, beliefs, and perceived norms.

49D450C0DFE80131F57168A86D17958E.description: Predict the outcomes of a variety of unhealthy behaviors.

49D411A0DFE80131F57068A86D17958E.description: Examine healthy behaviors and consequences related to a health issue.

49D3D2F0DFE80131F56F68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the relationships between healthy behaviors and personal health.

49D39390DFE80131F56E68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the benefits of and barriers to practicing healthy behaviors.

49D35140DFE80131F56D68A86D17958E.description: Describe how physical and social environments can affect personal health.

49D2FFF0DFE80131F56C68A86D17958E.description: Describe how family history can affect personal health.

49D2C000DFE80131F56B68A86D17958E.description: Describe the negative consequences of engaging in unhealthy behaviors.

49D27EF0DFE80131F56A68A86D17958E.description: Describe specific behaviors that can reduce or prevent injuries and communicable or chronic diseases. These may include but are not limited to: refraining from alcohol, tobacco, and other drug use; engaging in physical activity; demonstrating healthy eating; sexual behaviors; applying social behaviors to prevent or reduce violence; safety and related behaviors.

49D23DE0DFE80131F56968A86D17958E.description: Identify the components of health promotion and disease prevention.

49D1FD20DFE80131F56868A86D17958E.description: Comprehend and apply concepts related to health promotion and disease prevention.

49D16880DFE80131F56668A86D17958E.description: Students will comprehend concepts related to health promotion and disease prevention to enhance health.
comments: The acquisition of basic health concepts and functional health knowledge provides a foundation for promoting health-enhancing behaviors among youth. This standard includes essential concepts that are based on established health behavior theories and models. Concepts that focus on both health promotion and risk reduction are included in the learning continuum.

47B21590DFE80131F1C468A86D17958E.description: Analyze seventeenth-, eighteenth-, and nineteenth-century foundational U.S. documents of historical and literary significance (including The Declaration of Independence, the Preamble to the Constitution, the Bill of Rights, and Lincoln's Second Inaugural Address) for their themes, purposes, and rhetorical features.

47B1BFF0DFE80131F1C368A86D17958E.description: Delineate and evaluate the reasoning in seminal U.S. texts, including the application of constitutional principles and use of legal reasoning (e.g., in U.S. Supreme Court majority opinions and dissents) and the premises, purposes, and arguments in works of public advocacy (e.g., The Federalist, presidential addresses).

47B16970DFE80131F1C268A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate multiple sources of information presented in different media or formats (e.g., visually, quantitatively) as well as in words in order to address a question or solve a problem.

47B0B360DFE80131F1C068A86D17958E.description: Determine an author's point of view or purpose in a text in which the rhetoric is particularly effective, analyzing how style and content contribute to the power, persuasiveness, or beauty of the text.

47B056A0DFE80131F1BF68A86D17958E.description: Analyze and evaluate the effectiveness of the structure an author uses in his or her exposition or argument, including whether the structure makes points clear, convincing, and engaging.

47AFF5F0DFE80131F1BE68A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including figurative, connotative, and technical meanings; analyze how an author uses and refines the meaning of a key term or terms over the course of a text (e.g., how Madison defines faction in Federalist No. 10).

47AF3A50DFE80131F1BC68A86D17958E.description: Analyze a complex set of ideas or sequence of events and explain how specific individuals, ideas, or events interact and develop over the course of the text.

47AEE620DFE80131F1BB68A86D17958E.description: Determine two or more central ideas of a text and analyze their development over the course of the text, including how they interact and build on one another to provide a complex analysis; provide an objective summary of the text.

47AE88D0DFE80131F1BA68A86D17958E.description: Cite strong and thorough textual evidence to support analysis of what the text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text, including determining where the text leaves matters uncertain.

47AD5FE0DFE80131F1B768A86D17958E.description:
By the end of grade 11, read and comprehend literature, including stories, dramas, and poems, in the grades 11—CCR text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.
By the end of grade 12, read and comprehend literature, including stories, dramas, and poems, at the high end of the grades 11—CCR text complexity band independently and proficiently.

47AD1300DFE80131F1B668A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

47ACC3D0DFE80131F1B568A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate knowledge of eighteenth-, nineteenth- and early-twentieth-century foundational works of American literature, including how two or more texts from the same period treat similar themes or topics.

47AC7070DFE80131F1B468A86D17958E.description: Analyze multiple interpretations of a story, drama, or poem (e.g., recorded or live production of a play or recorded novel or poetry), evaluating how each version interprets the source text. (Include at least one play by Shakespeare and one play by an American dramatist.)

47AB6650DFE80131F1B168A86D17958E.description: Analyze a case in which grasping point of view requires distinguishing what is directly stated in a text from what is really meant (e.g., satire, sarcasm, irony, or understatement).

47AB0730DFE80131F1B068A86D17958E.description: Analyze how an author's choices concerning how to structure specific parts of a text (e.g., the choice of where to begin or end a story, the choice to provide a comedic or tragic resolution) contribute to its overall structure and meaning as well as its aesthetic impact.

47AAABC0DFE80131F1AF68A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in the text, including figurative and connotative meanings; analyze the impact of specific word choices on meaning and tone, including words with multiple meanings or language that is particularly fresh, engaging, or beautiful. (Include Shakespeare as well as other authors.)

47A9FF70DFE80131F1AD68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the impact of the author's choices regarding how to develop and relate elements of a story or drama (e.g., where a story is set, how the action is ordered, how the characters are introduced and developed).

47A9B060DFE80131F1AC68A86D17958E.description: Determine two or more themes or central ideas of a text and analyze their development over the course of the text, including how they interact and build on one another to produce a complex account; provide an objective summary of the text.

47A96050DFE80131F1AB68A86D17958E.description: Cite strong and thorough textual evidence to support analysis of what the text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text, including determining where the text leaves matters uncertain.

47A861C0DFE80131F1A868A86D17958E.description: Read and comprehend complex literary and informational texts independently and proficiently.

47A81330DFE80131F1A768A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

47A7B280DFE80131F1A668A86D17958E.description: Analyze how two or more texts address similar themes or topics in order to build knowledge or to compare the approaches the authors take.

47A76210DFE80131F1A568A86D17958E.description: Delineate and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, including the validity of the reasoning as well as the relevance and sufficiency of the evidence.

47A703A0DFE80131F1A468A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate content presented in diverse media and formats, including visually and quantitatively, as well as in words.

47A66270DFE80131F1A268A86D17958E.description: Assess how point of view or purpose shapes the content and style of a text.

47A615E0DFE80131F1A168A86D17958E.description: Analyze the structure of texts, including how specific sentences, paragraphs, and larger portions of the text (e.g., a section, chapter, scene, or stanza) relate to each other and the whole.

47A5C760DFE80131F1A068A86D17958E.description: Interpret words and phrases as they are used in a text, including determining technical, connotative, and figurative meanings, and analyze how specific word choices shape meaning or tone.

47A52100DFE80131F19E68A86D17958E.description: Analyze how and why individuals, events, and ideas develop and interact over the course of a text.

47A4D4C0DFE80131F19D68A86D17958E.description: Determine central ideas or themes of a text and analyze their development; summarize the key supporting details and ideas.

47A48550DFE80131F19C68A86D17958E.description: Read closely to determine what the text says explicitly and to make logical inferences from it; cite specific textual evidence when writing or speaking to support conclusions drawn from the text.

document.title: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics

4B9F7840DFE80131F7D568A86D17958E.description: Partition circles and rectangles into two and four equal shares, describe the shares using the words halves, fourths, and quarters, and use the phrases half of, fourth of, and quarter of. Describe the whole as two of, or four of the shares. Understand for these examples that decomposing into more equal shares creates smaller shares.

comments: Students do not need to learn formal names such as "right rectangular prism."
4B9F2D20DFE80131F7D468A86D17958E.description: Compose two-dimensional shapes (rectangles, squares, trapezoids, triangles, half-circles, and quarter-circles) or three-dimensional shapes (cubes, right rectangular prisms, right circular cones, and right circular cylinders) to create a composite shape, and compose new shapes from the composite shape.

4B9EDCC0DFE80131F7D368A86D17958E.description: Distinguish between defining attributes (e.g., triangles are closed and three-sided) versus non-defining attributes (e.g., color, orientation, overall size); build and draw shapes to possess defining attributes.

4B9E9540DFE80131F7D268A86D17958E.description: Reason with shapes and their attributes.

4B9E0A10DFE80131F7D068A86D17958E.description: Organize, represent, and interpret data with up to three categories; ask and answer questions about the total number of data points, how many in each category, and how many more or less are in one category than in another.

4B9D7EF0DFE80131F7CE68A86D17958E.description: Tell and write time in hours and half-hours using analog and digital clocks.

comments: Limit to contexts where the object being measured is spanned by a whole number of length units with no gaps or overlaps.
4B9CFD70DFE80131F7CC68A86D17958E.description: Express the length of an object as a whole number of length units, by laying multiple copies of a shorter object (the length unit) end to end; understand that the length measurement of an object is the number of same-size length units that span it with no gaps or overlaps.

4B9CBD30DFE80131F7CB68A86D17958E.description: Order three objects by length; compare the lengths of two objects indirectly by using a third object.

4B9C7B40DFE80131F7CA68A86D17958E.description: Measure lengths indirectly and by iterating length units.

4B9BE460DFE80131F7C868A86D17958E.description: Subtract multiples of 10 in the range 10-90 from multiples of 10 in the range 10-90 (positive or zero differences), using concrete models or drawings and strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction; relate the strategy to a written method and explain the reasoning used.

4B9B8310DFE80131F7C768A86D17958E.description: Given a two-digit number, mentally find 10 more or 10 less than the number, without having to count; explain the reasoning used.

4B9B3990DFE80131F7C668A86D17958E.description: Add within 100, including adding a two-digit number and a one-digit number, and adding a two-digit number and a multiple of 10, using concrete models or drawings and strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction; relate the strategy to a written method and explain the reasoning used. Understand that in adding two-digit numbers, one adds tens and tens, ones and ones; and sometimes it is necessary to compose a ten.

4B9AE970DFE80131F7C568A86D17958E.description: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to add and subtract.

4B9A9A90DFE80131F7C468A86D17958E.description: Compare two two-digit numbers based on meanings of the tens and ones digits, recording the results of comparisons with the symbols >, =, and <.

4B9A3D00DFE80131F7C368A86D17958E.description: The numbers 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90 refer to one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine tens (and 0 ones).

4B99F5F0DFE80131F7C268A86D17958E.description: The numbers from 11 to 19 are composed of a ten and one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine ones.

4B99B4B0DFE80131F7C168A86D17958E.description: 10 can be thought of as a bundle of ten ones — called a "ten."

4B996F00DFE80131F7C068A86D17958E.description: Understand that the two digits of a two-digit number represent amounts of tens and ones. Understand the following as special cases:

4B98CE00DFE80131F7BE68A86D17958E.description: Count to 120, starting at any number less than 120. In this range, read and write numerals and represent a number of objects with a written numeral.

4B984380DFE80131F7BC68A86D17958E.description: Number and Operations in Base Ten
comments: Grade 4 expectations in this domain are limited to whole numbers less than or equal to 1,000,000.

4B97FD40DFE80131F7BB68A86D17958E.description: Determine the unknown whole number in an addition or subtraction equation relating three whole numbers.
comments: For example, determine the unknown number that makes the equation true in each of the equations 8 + ? = 11, 5 = - 3, 6 + 6 = .

4B97B6E0DFE80131F7BA68A86D17958E.description: Understand the meaning of the equal sign, and determine if equations involving addition and subtraction are true or false.
comments: For example, which of the following equations are true and which are false? 6 = 6, 7 = 8 - 1, 5 + 2 = 2 + 5, 4 + 1 = 5 + 2.

4B9772C0DFE80131F7B968A86D17958E.description: Work with addition and subtraction equations.

4B972900DFE80131F7B868A86D17958E.description: Add and subtract within 20, demonstrating fluency for addition and subtraction within 10. Use strategies such as counting on; making ten (e.g., 8 + 6 = 8 + 2 + 4 = 10 + 4 = 14); decomposing a number leading to a ten (e.g., 13 - 4 = 13 - 3 - 1 = 10 - 1 = 9); using the relationship between addition and subtraction (e.g., knowing that 8 + 4 = 12, one knows 12 - 8 = 4); and creating equivalent but easier or known sums (e.g., adding 6 + 7 by creating the known equivalent 6 + 6 + 1 = 12 + 1 = 13).

4B96D510DFE80131F7B768A86D17958E.description: Relate counting to addition and subtraction (e.g., by counting on 2 to add 2).

4B964CB0DFE80131F7B568A86D17958E.description: Understand subtraction as an unknown-addend problem.
comments: For example, subtract 10 - 8 by finding the number that makes 10 when added to 8.

4B95FA70DFE80131F7B468A86D17958E.description: Apply properties of operations as strategies to add and subtract.
comments: Students need not use formal terms for these properties.
To add 2 + 6 + 4, the second two numbers can be added to make a ten, so 2 + 6 + 4 = 2 + 10 = 12. (Associative property of addition.)
If 8 + 3 = 11 is known, then 3 + 8 = 11 is also known. (Commutative property of addition.)

4B95B0E0DFE80131F7B368A86D17958E.description: Understand and apply properties of operations and the relationship between addition and subtraction.

4B955BC0DFE80131F7B268A86D17958E.description: Solve word problems that call for addition of three whole numbers whose sum is less than or equal to 20, e.g., by using objects, drawings, and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.

4B9507B0DFE80131F7B168A86D17958E.description: Use addition and subtraction within 20 to solve word problems involving situations of adding to, taking from, putting together, taking apart, and comparing, with unknowns in all positions, e.g., by using objects, drawings, and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.

4B94C860DFE80131F7B068A86D17958E.description: Represent and solve problems involving addition and subtraction.

4B943C50DFE80131F7AE68A86D17958E.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.
comments: Mathematically proficient students notice if calculations are repeated, and look both for general methods and for shortcuts. Upper elementary students might notice when dividing 25 by 11 that they are repeating the same calculations over and over again, and conclude they have a repeating decimal. By paying attention to the calculation of slope as they repeatedly check whether points are on the line through (1, 2) with slope 3, middle school students might abstract the equation (y – 2)/(x – 1) = 3. Noticing the regularity in the way terms cancel when expanding (x – 1)(x + 1), (x – 1)(x² + x + 1), and (x – 1)(x³ + x² + x + 1) might lead them to the general formula for the sum of a geometric series. As they work to solve a problem, mathematically proficient students maintain oversight of the process, while attending to the details. They continually evaluate the reasonableness of their intermediate results.

Mathematically proficient students look closely to discern a pattern or structure. Young students, for example, might notice that three and seven more is the same amount as seven and three more, or they may sort a collection of shapes according to how many sides the shapes have. Later, students will see 7 × 8 equals the well remembered 7 × 5 + 7 × 3, in preparation for learning about the distributive property. In the expression x² + 9x + 14, older students can see the 14 as 2 × 7 and the 9 as 2 + 7. They recognize the significance of an existing line in a geometric figure and can use the strategy of drawing an auxiliary line for solving problems. They also can step back for an overview and shift perspective. They can see complicated things, such as some algebraic expressions, as single objects or as being composed of several objects. For example, they can see 5 – 3(x – y)² as 5 minus a positive number times a square and use that to realize that its value cannot be more than 5 for any real numbers x and y.
4B93EB30DFE80131F7AD68A86D17958E.description: Look for and make use of structure.

comments: Mathematically proficient students try to communicate precisely to others. They try to use clear definitions in discussion with others and in their own reasoning. They state the meaning of the symbols they choose, including using the equal sign consistently and appropriately. They are careful about specifying units of measure, and labeling axes to clarify the correspondence with quantities in a problem. They calculate accurately and efficiently, express numerical answers with a degree of precision appropriate for the problem context. In the elementary grades, students give carefully formulated explanations to each other. By the time they reach high school they have learned to examine claims and make explicit use of definitions.

Mathematically proficient students consider the available tools when solving a mathematical problem. These tools might include pencil and paper, concrete models, a ruler, a protractor, a calculator, a spreadsheet, a computer algebra system, a statistical package, or dynamic geometry software. Proficient students are sufficiently familiar with tools appropriate for their grade or course to make sound decisions about when each of these tools might be helpful, recognizing both the insight to be gained and their limitations. For example, mathematically proficient high school students analyze graphs of functions and solutions generated using a graphing calculator. They detect possible errors by strategically using estimation and other mathematical knowledge. When making mathematical models, they know that technology can enable them to visualize the results of varying assumptions, explore consequences, and compare predictions with data. Mathematically proficient students at various grade levels are able to identify relevant external mathematical resources, such as digital content located on a website, and use them to pose or solve problems. They are able to use technological tools to explore and deepen their understanding of concepts.

Mathematically proficient students can apply the mathematics they know to solve problems arising in everyday life, society, and the workplace. In early grades, this might be as simple as writing an addition equation to describe a situation. In middle grades, a student might apply proportional reasoning to plan a school event or analyze a problem in the community. By high school, a student might use geometry to solve a design problem or use a function to describe how one quantity of interest depends on another. Mathematically proficient students who can apply what they know are comfortable making assumptions and approximations to simplify a complicated situation, realizing that these may need revision later. They are able to identify important quantities in a practical situation and map their relationships using such tools as diagrams, two-way tables, graphs, flowcharts and formulas. They can analyze those relationships mathematically to draw conclusions. They routinely interpret their mathematical results in the context of the situation and reflect on whether the results make sense, possibly improving the model if it has not served its purpose.

4B9277B0DFE80131F7A968A86D17958E.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.
comments: Mathematically proficient students understand and use stated assumptions, definitions, and previously established results in constructing arguments. They make conjectures and build a logical progression of statements to explore the truth of their conjectures. They are able to analyze situations by breaking them into cases, and can recognize and use counterexamples. They justify their conclusions, communicate them to others, and respond to the arguments of others. They reason inductively about data, making plausible arguments that take into account the context from which the data arose. Mathematically proficient students are also able to compare the effectiveness of two plausible arguments, distinguish correct logic or reasoning from that which is flawed, and—if there is a flaw in an argument—explain what it is. Elementary students can construct arguments using concrete referents such as objects, drawings, diagrams, and actions. Such arguments can make sense and be correct, even though they are not generalized or made formal until later grades. Later, students learn to determine domains to which an argument applies. Students at all grades can listen or read the arguments of others, decide whether they make sense, and ask useful questions to clarify or improve the arguments.

Mathematically proficient students make sense of quantities and their relationships in problem situations. They bring two complementary abilities to bear on problems involving quantitative relationships: the ability to decontextualize—to abstract a given situation and represent it symbolically and manipulate the representing symbols as if they have a life of their own, without necessarily attending to their referents—and the ability to contextualize, to pause as needed during the manipulation process in order to probe into the referents for the symbols involved. Quantitative reasoning entails habits of creating a coherent representation of the problem at hand; considering the units involved; attending to the meaning of quantities, not just how to compute them; and knowing and flexibly using different properties of operations and objects.

4B91E020DFE80131F7A768A86D17958E.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.
comments: Mathematically proficient students start by explaining to themselves the meaning of a problem and looking for entry points to its solution. They analyze givens, constraints, relationships, and goals. They make conjectures about the form and meaning of the solution and plan a solution pathway rather than simply jumping into a solution attempt. They consider analogous problems, and try special cases and simpler forms of the original problem in order to gain insight into its solution. They monitor and evaluate their progress and change course if necessary. Older students might, depending on the context of the problem, transform algebraic expressions or change the viewing window on their graphing calculator to get the information they need. Mathematically proficient students can explain correspondences between equations, verbal descriptions, tables, and graphs or draw diagrams of important features and relationships, graph data, and search for regularity or trends. Younger students might rely on using concrete objects or pictures to help conceptualize and solve a problem. Mathematically proficient students check their answers to problems using a different method, and they continually ask themselves, "Does this make sense?" They can understand the approaches of others to solving complex problems and identify correspondences between different approaches.

document.title: Wisconsin's Model Academic Standards for Science

4E5D8C50DFE80131FC6068A86D17958E.description: Understand the consequences of decisions affecting personal health and safety

4E5E32A0DFE80131FC6268A86D17958E.description: Present a scientific solution to a problem involving the earth and space, life and environmental, or physical sciences and participate in a consensus-building discussion to arrive at a group decision

4E5DD810DFE80131FC6168A86D17958E.description: Evaluate the scientific evidence used in various media (for example, television, radio, Internet, popular press, and scientific journals) to address a social issue, using criteria of accuracy, logic, bias, relevance of data, and credibility of sources

4E5D3F00DFE80131FC5F68A86D17958E.description: Students in Wisconsin will use scientific information and skills to make decisions about themselves, Wisconsin, and the world in which they live.

4E5CE820DFE80131FC5E68A86D17958E.description: Science in Personal and Social Perspectives

4E224E40DFE80131FC5B68A86D17958E.description: Show evidence of how science and technology are interdependent, using some examples drawn from personally conducted investigations

4E2207E0DFE80131FC5A68A86D17958E.description: Use current texts, encyclopedias, source books, computers, experts, the popular press, or other relevant sources to identify examples of how scientific discoveries have resulted in new technology

4E5C9320DFE80131FC5D68A86D17958E.description: Investigate a specific local problem to which there has been a scientific or technological solution, including proposals for alternative courses of action, the choices that were made, reasons for the choices, any new problems created, and subsequent community satisfaction

4E2175A0DFE80131FC5868A86D17958E.description: Propose a design (or re-design) of an applied science model or a machine that will have an impact in the community or elsewhere in the world and show how the design (or re-design) might work, including potential side-effects

4E21C030DFE80131FC5968A86D17958E.description: Illustrate the impact that science and technology have had, both good and bad, on careers, systems, society, environment, and quality of life

4E212480DFE80131FC5768A86D17958E.description: Explain how current scientific and technological discoveries have an influence on the work people do and how some of these discoveries also lead to new careers

4E5C3960DFE80131FC5C68A86D17958E.description: Identify and investigate the skills people need for a career in science or technology and identify the academic courses that a person pursuing such a career would need

4E20D6C0DFE80131FC5668A86D17958E.description: Students in Wisconsin will demonstrate an understanding of the relationship between science and technology and the ways in which that relationship influences human activities.

4E1E7170DFE80131FC4F68A86D17958E.description: Project how current trends in human resource use and population growth will influence the natural environment, and show how current policies affect those trends

4E1E2860DFE80131FC4E68A86D17958E.description: Explain how some of the changes on the earth are contributing to changes in the balance of life and affecting the survival or population growth of certain species

4E203340DFE80131FC5468A86D17958E.description: Show through investigations how organisms both depend on and contribute to the balance or imbalance of populations and/or ecosystems, which in turn contribute to the total system of life on the planet

4E1BCBA0DFE80131FC4868A86D17958E.description: Understand that an organism's behavior evolves through adaptation to its environment

4E1B7200DFE80131FC4768A86D17958E.description: Understand that an organism is regulated both internally and externally

4E1F7B90DFE80131FC5268A86D17958E.description: Show how different structures both reproduce and pass on characteristics of their group

4E1EFD40DFE80131FC5168A86D17958E.description: Investigate and explain that heredity is comprised of the characteristic traits found in genes within the cell of an organism

4E1D7230DFE80131FC4C68A86D17958E.description: Differentiate between single-celled and multiple-celled organisms (humans) through investigation, comparing the cell functions of specialized cells for each type of organism

4E1CCC10DFE80131FC4A68A86D17958E.description: Show how organisms have adapted structures to match their functions, providing means of encouraging individual and group survival within specific environments

4E1D1990DFE80131FC4B68A86D17958E.description: Understand the structure and function of cells, organs, tissues, organ systems, and whole organisms

4E1C1700DFE80131FC4968A86D17958E.description: Structure and Function in Living Things

4E1AC4F0DFE80131FC4568A86D17958E.description: Students in Wisconsin will demonstrate an understanding of the characteristics and structures of living things, the processes of life, and how living things interact with one another and their environment.

4E1758F0DFE80131FC3A68A86D17958E.description: Using past and current models of the structure of the solar system, explain the daily, monthly, yearly, and long-term cycles of the earth, citing evidence gained from personal observation as well as evidence used by scientists

4E17A570DFE80131FC3B68A86D17958E.description: Describe the general structure of the solar system, galaxies, and the universe, explaining the nature of the evidence used to develop current models of the universe

4E18B900DFE80131FC3E68A86D17958E.description: Describe through investigations the use of the earth's resources by humans in both past and current cultures, particularly how changes in the resources used for the past 100 years are the basis for efforts to conserve and recycle renewable and non-renewable resources

4E185F50DFE80131FC3D68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the geologic and life history of the earth, including change over time, using various forms of scientific evidence

4E194800DFE80131FC4068A86D17958E.description: Using the science themes, analyze the influence living organisms have had on the earth's systems, including their impact on the composition of the atmosphere and the weathering of rocks

4E1A2580DFE80131FC4368A86D17958E.description: Using the science themes during the process of investigation, describe climate, weather, ocean currents, soil movements and changes in the forces acting on the earth

4E198E40DFE80131FC4168A86D17958E.description: Describe underlying structures of the earth that cause changes in the earth's surface

4E19D3B0DFE80131FC4268A86D17958E.description: Using the science themes, explain and predict changes in major features of land, water, and atmospheric systems

4E16C2D0DFE80131FC3868A86D17958E.description: Students in Wisconsin will demonstrate an understanding of the structure and systems of earth and other bodies in the universe and of their interactions.

4E159970DFE80131FC3468A86D17958E.description: Explain how models of the atomic structure of matter have changed over time, including historical models and modern atomic theory

4E162860DFE80131FC3668A86D17958E.description: Explain the behaviors of various forms of energy by using the models of energy transmission, both in the laboratory and in real-life situations in the outside world

4E15E280DFE80131FC3568A86D17958E.description: Describe and investigate the properties of light, heat, gravity, radio waves, magnetic fields, electrical fields, and sound waves as they interact with material objects in common situations

4E12F410DFE80131FC2D68A86D17958E.description: While conducting investigations of common physical and chemical interactions occurring in the laboratory and the outside world, use commonly accepted definitions of energy and the idea of energy conservation

4E124B70DFE80131FC2B68A86D17958E.description: While conducting investigations, explain the motion of objects using concepts of speed, velocity, acceleration, friction, momentum, and changes over time, among others, and apply these concepts and explanations to real-life situations outside the classroom

4E12A6B0DFE80131FC2C68A86D17958E.description: While conducting investigations, explain the motion of objects by describing the forces acting on them

document.title: Wisconsin's Model Academic Standards for Nutrition Education

494139D0DFE80131F48568A86D17958E.description: Identify the basic food groups, and give examples from each group for meals and snacks

4940E110DFE80131F48468A86D17958E.description: Categorize foods by source (plant, animal), including processed foods

4940A550DFE80131F48368A86D17958E.description: Describe different kinds of food (by physical and sensory characteristics — shape, taste, color, texture, etc)

494021F0DFE80131F48168A86D17958E.description: Students in Wisconsin will be able to appreciate and classify foods. They will also demonstrate an interest and appreciation for a variety of foods.
comments: Foods are classified in many ways. Awareness of the variety and types of foods available may increase willingness to try unfamiliar foods. Identifying and trying new foods is one of the first steps leading to knowledge of foods. Students who understand why foods are processed, and how foods change during processing establish a foundation for understanding how nutritional content can change with changes in form of a food.

493FA3B0DFE80131F47F68A86D17958E.description: Describe how food choices are influenced by availability, individual and family preferences, media and background

493F5C90DFE80131F47E68A86D17958E.description: Identify different dietary needs related to food allergies and medical conditions

493F1230DFE80131F47D68A86D17958E.description: Identify examples of cultures and their food customs and habits

493ED6A0DFE80131F47C68A86D17958E.description: Recognize that people come in many shapes and sizes

493E99F0DFE80131F47B68A86D17958E.description: Understand that people eat many different foods as part of a healthy diet

493E58F0DFE80131F47A68A86D17958E.description: Students in Wisconsin will understand that nutritional status and health can be impacted by many factors, and healthy eating must be individualized to meet personal preferences and characteristics.
comments: The Wisconsin population is growing more diverse. Nutritional status is affected by the food choices available and the nutritional adequacy and appropriateness of the food available. In addition, diversity in body size and shape, economic resources and racial and ethnic background may influence and impact food choices.

493DD980DFE80131F47868A86D17958E.description: Recognize the relationship between diet and chronic diseases, such as blood pressure, heart disease and obesity

493D96A0DFE80131F47768A86D17958E.description: Identify sources of fat, sugar, salt, fiber, protein, and calcium in the diet

493D07D0DFE80131F47568A86D17958E.description: Understand the concept of variety, and identify that eating a variety of foods is important to health

493CC030DFE80131F47468A86D17958E.description: Students in Wisconsin will understand concepts related to personal health promotion and disease prevention, and will practice behaviors to promote health, prevent disease, and reduce health risks.
comments: Making nutritious food choices is a cornerstone of healthy behaviors. Knowledge of nutrition concepts will assist students in making informed choices regarding their lifestyles.

493C7BA0DFE80131F47368A86D17958E.description: Nutrition for Health Promotion of Healthy Behaviors

493C1D60DFE80131F47268A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate how to use food labels to select a healthy food or snack

493BC430DFE80131F47168A86D17958E.description: Recognize factors in advertisements to sell foods

493B4C90DFE80131F47068A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast snacks which can contribute to or undermine healthy eating habits and identify why one snack might be a better choice than another snack

493AEA70DFE80131F46F68A86D17958E.description: Graph progress toward achieving a set nutrition goal, using a simple log chart

493A6270DFE80131F46D68A86D17958E.description: Be able to distinguish between food and nonfood items

493A2150DFE80131F46C68A86D17958E.description: Students in Wisconsin will understand and use critical thinking and practical reasoning skills to address food choices, nutrition, and health concerns
comments: Critical thinking and practical reasoning are used in everyday problem solving. Students who develop these skills are more likely to approach everyday problem solving more deliberately, with greater flexibility, and increased open-mindedness.

493989E0DFE80131F46A68A86D17958E.description: Explain the importance of hand-washing during food preparation

49391380DFE80131F46868A86D17958E.description: Trace a food from origin to table

4938D650DFE80131F46768A86D17958E.description: Recognize that eating improperly prepared or spoiled food can make you sick

493896A0DFE80131F46668A86D17958E.description: Identify ways to keep food fresh and safe to eat

49381870DFE80131F46468A86D17958E.description: Students in Wisconsin will understand/know how to keep food safe for consumption and how to prepare food safely.
comments: Food borne illness is a common and serious consequence of poor hygiene, unsafe food handling and improper food preparation.

493767D0DFE80131F46268A86D17958E.description: Match food groups to their primary contribution for a healthy body, realizing that some foods are better fuel than others (nutrient density)

493724B0DFE80131F46168A86D17958E.description: Identify the benefi ts of relationship between physical activity (using energy) and the need for food and water; state that people need to eat food to have energy and grow

4936DD80DFE80131F46068A86D17958E.description: Identify feeling hungry vs. feeling full/satisfied

49369BE0DFE80131F45F68A86D17958E.description: Identify why people need to eat different kinds of foods

493655E0DFE80131F45E68A86D17958E.description: Students in Wisconsin will understand the concepts related to and the connections between food choices, eating habits, activity, and healthy growth.
comments: Nutritional needs vary across the lifecycle. Growth and energy are dependent on healthy eating and nutrition. Students who understand the personal relationship of food choices to energy and growth may be more likely to maintain or improve health.

document.title: Common Core State Standards for English Language Arts

46792060DFE80131EFFD68A86D17958E.description: Acquire and use accurately grade-appropriate general academic and domain-specific words and phrases; gather vocabulary knowledge when considering a word or phrase important to comprehension or expression.

46788AE0DFE80131EFFB68A86D17958E.description: Use the relationship between particular words (e.g., synonym/antonym, analogy) to better understand each of the words.

46783EC0DFE80131EFFA68A86D17958E.description: Interpret figures of speech (e.g., literary, biblical, and mythological allusions) in context.

4677EB10DFE80131EFF968A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

467793C0DFE80131EFF868A86D17958E.description: Verify the preliminary determination of the meaning of a word or phrase (e.g., by checking the inferred meaning in context or in a dictionary).

467741D0DFE80131EFF768A86D17958E.description: Consult general and specialized reference materials (e.g., dictionaries, glossaries, thesauruses), both print and digital, to find the pronunciation of a word or determine or clarify its precise meaning or its part of speech.

4676E080DFE80131EFF668A86D17958E.description: Use common, grade-appropriate Greek or Latin affixes and roots as clues to the meaning of a word (e.g., belligerent, bellicose, rebel).

46768420DFE80131EFF568A86D17958E.description: Use context (e.g., the overall meaning of a sentence or paragraph; a word's position or function in a sentence) as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

467629E0DFE80131EFF468A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grade 7 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.

46758090DFE80131EFF268A86D17958E.description: Choose language that expresses ideas precisely and concisely, recognizing and eliminating wordiness and redundancy.

46753150DFE80131EFF168A86D17958E.description: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening.

46743410DFE80131EFEE68A86D17958E.description: Use a comma to separate coordinate adjectives (e.g., It was a fascinating, enjoyable movie but not He wore an old[,] green shirt).

4673D5A0DFE80131EFED68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

46737760DFE80131EFEC68A86D17958E.description: Place phrases and clauses within a sentence, recognizing and correcting misplaced and dangling modifiers.

46732D70DFE80131EFEB68A86D17958E.description: Choose among simple, compound, complex, and compound-complex sentences to signal differing relationships among ideas.

4672E420DFE80131EFEA68A86D17958E.description: Explain the function of phrases and clauses in general and their function in specific sentences.

46729AB0DFE80131EFE968A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

46715D00DFE80131EFE568A86D17958E.description: Acquire and use accurately a range of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases sufficient for reading, writing, speaking, and listening at the college and career readiness level; demonstrate independence in gathering vocabulary knowledge when considering a word or phrase important to comprehension or expression.

46710E80DFE80131EFE468A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

4670BED0DFE80131EFE368A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases by using context clues, analyzing meaningful word parts, and consulting general and specialized reference materials, as appropriate.

46700DC0DFE80131EFE168A86D17958E.description: Apply knowledge of language to understand how language functions in different contexts, to make effective choices for meaning or style, and to comprehend more fully when reading or listening.

466F6020DFE80131EFDF68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

466F09B0DFE80131EFDE68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

466E4070DFE80131EFDC68A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Language

466DC5D0DFE80131EFDB68A86D17958E.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate.

466D7870DFE80131EFDA68A86D17958E.description: Include multimedia components and visual displays in presentations to clarify claims and findings and emphasize salient points.

466D2C00DFE80131EFD968A86D17958E.description: Present claims and findings, emphasizing salient points in a focused, coherent manner with pertinent descriptions, facts, details, and examples; use appropriate eye contact, adequate volume, and clear pronunciation.

466C7DD0DFE80131EFD768A86D17958E.description: Delineate a speaker's argument and specific claims, evaluating the soundness of the reasoning and the relevance and sufficiency of the evidence.

466C3060DFE80131EFD668A86D17958E.description: Analyze the main ideas and supporting details presented in diverse media and formats (e.g., visually, quantitatively, orally) and explain how the ideas clarify a topic, text, or issue under study.

466BE600DFE80131EFD568A86D17958E.description: Acknowledge new information expressed by others and, when warranted, modify their own views.

466B9A60DFE80131EFD468A86D17958E.description: Pose questions that elicit elaboration and respond to others' questions and comments with relevant observations and ideas that bring the discussion back on topic as needed.

466B4D70DFE80131EFD368A86D17958E.description: Follow rules for collegial discussions, track progress toward specific goals and deadlines, and define individual roles as needed.

466AFA40DFE80131EFD268A86D17958E.description: Come to discussions prepared, having read or researched material under study; explicitly draw on that preparation by referring to evidence on the topic, text, or issue to probe and reflect on ideas under discussion.

466A9ED0DFE80131EFD168A86D17958E.description: Engage effectively in a range of collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in groups, and teacher-led) with diverse partners on grade 7 topics, texts, and issues, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly.

46697820DFE80131EFCE68A86D17958E.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and communicative tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate.

46691090DFE80131EFCD68A86D17958E.description: Make strategic use of digital media and visual displays of data to express information and enhance understanding of presentations.

4668B2E0DFE80131EFCC68A86D17958E.description: Present information, findings, and supporting evidence such that listeners can follow the line of reasoning and the organization, development, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

4667CE30DFE80131EFCA68A86D17958E.description: Evaluate a speaker's point of view, reasoning, and use of evidence and rhetoric.

46677B40DFE80131EFC968A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.

46671ED0DFE80131EFC868A86D17958E.description: Prepare for and participate effectively in a range of conversations and collaborations with diverse partners, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly and persuasively.

46638360DFE80131EFBD68A86D17958E.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

4662D8F0DFE80131EFBB68A86D17958E.description: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the information or explanation presented.

466289A0DFE80131EFBA68A86D17958E.description: Establish and maintain a formal style and objective tone.

46623A00DFE80131EFB968A86D17958E.description: Use precise language and domain-specific vocabulary to inform about or explain the topic.

4661EE20DFE80131EFB868A86D17958E.description: Use appropriate and varied transitions to create cohesion and clarify the relationships among ideas and concepts.

46614E50DFE80131EFB668A86D17958E.description: Introduce a topic clearly, previewing what is to follow; organize ideas, concepts, and information into broader categories as appropriate to achieving purpose; include formatting (e.g., headings), graphics (e.g., charts, tables), and multimedia when useful to aiding comprehension.

4660F310DFE80131EFB568A86D17958E.description: Write informative/explanatory texts, including the narration of historical events, scientific procedures/experiments, or technical processes.

4660A150DFE80131EFB468A86D17958E.description: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from or supports the argument presented.

46605540DFE80131EFB368A86D17958E.description: Establish and maintain a formal style.

465F3E90DFE80131EFB068A86D17958E.description: Introduce claim(s) about a topic or issue, acknowledge and distinguish the claim(s) from alternate or opposing claims, and organize the reasons and evidence logically.

465EF0F0DFE80131EFAF68A86D17958E.description: Write arguments focused on discipline-specific content.
