465E0530DFE80131EFAC68A86D17958E.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of discipline-specific tasks, purposes, and audiences.

465D5770DFE80131EFAA68A86D17958E.description: Apply grade 7 Reading standards to literary nonfiction (e.g. "Trace and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, assessing whether the reasoning is sound and the evidence is relevant and sufficient to support the claims").

465CF7F0DFE80131EFA968A86D17958E.description: Apply grade 7 Reading standards to literature (e.g., "Compare and contrast a fictional portrayal of a time, place, or character and a historical account of the same period as a means of understanding how authors of fiction use or alter history").

465C79F0DFE80131EFA868A86D17958E.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

465C1A00DFE80131EFA768A86D17958E.description: Gather relevant information from multiple print and digital sources, using search terms effectively; assess the credibility and accuracy of each source; and quote or paraphrase the data and conclusions of others while avoiding plagiarism and following a standard format for citation.

465BD110DFE80131EFA668A86D17958E.description: Conduct short research projects to answer a question, drawing on several sources and generating additional related, focused questions for further research and investigation.

465B8950DFE80131EFA568A86D17958E.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

465B3FA0DFE80131EFA468A86D17958E.description: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce and publish writing and link to and cite sources as well as to interact and collaborate with others, including linking to and citing sources.

465AF490DFE80131EFA368A86D17958E.description: With some guidance and support from peers and adults, develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach, focusing on how well purpose and audience have been addressed.

465AA650DFE80131EFA268A86D17958E.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

4659FC80DFE80131EFA068A86D17958E.description: Provide a conclusion that follows from and reflects on the narrated experiences or events.

4659A580DFE80131EF9F68A86D17958E.description: Use precise words and phrases, relevant descriptive details, and sensory language to capture the action and convey experiences and events.

46595430DFE80131EF9E68A86D17958E.description: Use a variety of transition words, phrases, and clauses to convey sequence and signal shifts from one time frame or setting to another.

465901E0DFE80131EF9D68A86D17958E.description: Use narrative techniques, such as dialogue, pacing, and description, to develop experiences, events, and/or characters.

4658AB00DFE80131EF9C68A86D17958E.description: Engage and orient the reader by establishing a context and point of view and introducing a narrator and/or characters; organize an event sequence that unfolds naturally and logically.

46584060DFE80131EF9B68A86D17958E.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, relevant descriptive details, and well-structured event sequences.

4657D530DFE80131EF9A68A86D17958E.description: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the information or explanation presented

46578200DFE80131EF9968A86D17958E.description: Establish and maintain a formal style.

465733A0DFE80131EF9868A86D17958E.description: Use precise language and domain-specific vocabulary to inform about or explain the topic.

4656DC60DFE80131EF9768A86D17958E.description: Use appropriate transitions to create cohesion and clarify the relationships among ideas and concepts.

46567D80DFE80131EF9668A86D17958E.description: Develop the topic with relevant facts, definitions, concrete details, quotations, or other information and examples.

46563370DFE80131EF9568A86D17958E.description: Introduce a topic clearly, previewing what is to follow; organize ideas, concepts, and information, using strategies such as definition, classification, comparison/contrast, and cause/effect; include formatting (e.g., headings), graphics (e.g., charts, tables), and multimedia when useful to aiding comprehension.

4655E8C0DFE80131EF9468A86D17958E.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine a topic and convey ideas, concepts, and information through the selection, organization, and analysis of relevant content

465599B0DFE80131EF9368A86D17958E.description: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the argument presented.

465545C0DFE80131EF9268A86D17958E.description: Establish and maintain a formal style.

4654E4E0DFE80131EF9168A86D17958E.description: Use words, phrases, and clauses to create cohesion and clarify the relationships among claim(s), reasons, and evidence.

46549060DFE80131EF9068A86D17958E.description: Support claim(s) with logical reasoning and relevant evidence, using accurate, credible sources and demonstrating an understanding of the topic or text.

46543F00DFE80131EF8F68A86D17958E.description: Introduce claim(s), acknowledge alternate or opposing claims, and organize the reasons and evidence logically.

4653E010DFE80131EF8E68A86D17958E.description: Write arguments to support claims with clear reasons and relevant evidence.

4652C990DFE80131EF8B68A86D17958E.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of tasks, purposes, and audiences.

46522F50DFE80131EF8968A86D17958E.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

4651E280DFE80131EF8868A86D17958E.description: Gather relevant information from multiple print and digital sources, assess the credibility and accuracy of each source, and integrate the information while avoiding plagiarism.

46518820DFE80131EF8768A86D17958E.description: Conduct short as well as more sustained research projects based on focused questions, demonstrating understanding of the subject under investigation.

46511300DFE80131EF8668A86D17958E.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

4650B670DFE80131EF8568A86D17958E.description: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce and publish writing and to interact and collaborate with others.

46506780DFE80131EF8468A86D17958E.description: Develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach.

46500A90DFE80131EF8368A86D17958E.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

464F6950DFE80131EF8168A86D17958E.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, well-chosen details, and well-structured event sequences.

464F1BE0DFE80131EF8068A86D17958E.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine and convey complex ideas and information clearly and accurately through the effective selection, organization, and analysis of content.

464ECA60DFE80131EF7F68A86D17958E.description: Write arguments to support claims in an analysis of substantive topics or texts, using valid reasoning and relevant and sufficient evidence.

464E20A0DFE80131EF7D68A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Writing

464DA6B0DFE80131EF7C68A86D17958E.description: By the end of grade 8, read and comprehend science/technical texts in the grades 6—8 text complexity band independently and proficiently.

464D5560DFE80131EF7B68A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

464D0BC0DFE80131EF7A68A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast the information gained from experiments, simulations, video, or multimedia sources with that gained from reading a text on the same topic.

464CC120DFE80131EF7968A86D17958E.description: Distinguish among facts, reasoned judgment based on research findings, and speculation in a text.

464C7440DFE80131EF7868A86D17958E.description: Integrate quantitative or technical information expressed in words in a text with a version of that information expressed visually (e.g., in a flowchart, diagram, model, graph, or table).

464BC200DFE80131EF7668A86D17958E.description: Analyze the author's purpose in providing an explanation, describing a procedure, or discussing an experiment in a text.

464B5130DFE80131EF7568A86D17958E.description: Analyze the structure an author uses to organize a text, including how the major sections contribute to the whole and to an understanding of the topic.

464B0200DFE80131EF7468A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of symbols, key terms, and other domain-specific words and phrases as they are used in a specific scientific or technical context relevant to grades 6—8 texts and topics.

464A6340DFE80131EF7268A86D17958E.description: Follow precisely a multistep procedure when carrying out experiments, taking measurements, or performing technical tasks.

464A0980DFE80131EF7168A86D17958E.description: Determine the central ideas or conclusions of a text; provide an accurate summary of the text distinct from prior knowledge or opinions.

4649C2D0DFE80131EF7068A86D17958E.description: Cite specific textual evidence to support analysis of science and technical texts.

46492BD0DFE80131EF6E68A86D17958E.description: Reading Standards for Literacy in Science and Technical Subjects 6—12

4648DCA0DFE80131EF6D68A86D17958E.description: By the end of grade 8, read and comprehend history/social studies texts in the grades 6—8 text complexity band independently and proficiently.

46488450DFE80131EF6C68A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

464827D0DFE80131EF6B68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the relationship between a primary and secondary source on the same topic.

4647DD60DFE80131EF6A68A86D17958E.description: Distinguish among fact, opinion, and reasoned judgment in a text.

46479220DFE80131EF6968A86D17958E.description: Integrate visual information (e.g., in charts, graphs, photographs, videos, or maps) with other information in print and digital texts.

4646F910DFE80131EF6768A86D17958E.description: Identify aspects of a text that reveal an author's point of view or purpose (e.g., loaded language, inclusion or avoidance of particular facts).

46469FD0DFE80131EF6668A86D17958E.description: Describe how a text presents information (e.g., sequentially, comparatively, causally).

464633D0DFE80131EF6568A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including vocabulary specific to domains related to history/social studies.

46455C60DFE80131EF6368A86D17958E.description: Identify key steps in a text's description of a process related to history/social studies (e.g., how a bill becomes law, how interest rates are raised or lowered).

46451290DFE80131EF6268A86D17958E.description: Determine the central ideas or information of a primary or secondary source; provide an accurate summary of the source distinct from prior knowledge or opinions.

4644C6E0DFE80131EF6168A86D17958E.description: Cite specific textual evidence to support analysis of primary and secondary sources.

46441DC0DFE80131EF5F68A86D17958E.description: Reading Standards for Literacy in History/Social Studies 6—12

4643CBB0DFE80131EF5E68A86D17958E.description: By the end of the year, read and comprehend literary nonfiction in the grades 6–8 text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.

46437FA0DFE80131EF5D68A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

464332A0DFE80131EF5C68A86D17958E.description: Analyze how two or more authors writing about the same topic shape their presentations of key information by emphasizing different evidence or advancing different interpretations of facts.

4642E230DFE80131EF5B68A86D17958E.description: Trace and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, assessing whether the reasoning is sound and the evidence is relevant and sufficient to support the claims.

464283E0DFE80131EF5A68A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast a text to an audio, video, or multimedia version of the text, analyzing each medium's portrayal of the subject (e.g., how the delivery of a speech affects the impact of the words).

4641E2D0DFE80131EF5868A86D17958E.description: Determine an author's point of view or purpose in a text and analyze how the author distinguishes his or her position from that of others.

46418470DFE80131EF5768A86D17958E.description: Analyze the structure an author uses to organize a text, including how the major sections contribute to the whole and to the development of the ideas.

46410940DFE80131EF5668A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including figurative, connotative, and technical meanings; analyze the impact of a specific word choice on meaning and tone.

46406340DFE80131EF5468A86D17958E.description: Analyze the interactions between individuals, events, and ideas in a text (e.g., how ideas influence individuals or events, or how individuals influence ideas or events).

46400F90DFE80131EF5368A86D17958E.description: Determine two or more central ideas in a text and analyze their development over the course of the text; provide an objective summary of the text.

463FBC00DFE80131EF5268A86D17958E.description: Cite several pieces of textual evidence to support analysis of what the text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text.

463E9AE0DFE80131EF4F68A86D17958E.description: By the end of the year, read and comprehend literary nonfiction in the grades 6–8 text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.

463E4B20DFE80131EF4E68A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

463DA260DFE80131EF4C68A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast a fictional portrayal of a time, place, or character and a historical account of the same period as a means of understanding how authors of fiction use or alter history.

463D4970DFE80131EF4B68A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast a written story, drama, or poem to its audio, filmed, staged, or multimedia version, analyzing the effects of techniques unique to each medium (e.g., lighting, sound, color, or camera focus and angles in a film).

463CAC40DFE80131EF4968A86D17958E.description: Analyze how an author develops and contrasts the points of view of different characters or narrators in a text.

463C5180DFE80131EF4868A86D17958E.description: Analyze how a drama's or poem's form or structure (e.g., soliloquy, sonnet) contributes to its meaning.

463BF0C0DFE80131EF4768A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including figurative and connotative meanings; analyze the impact of rhymes and other repetitions of sounds (e.g., alliteration) on a specific verse or stanza of a poem or section of a story or drama.

463B3220DFE80131EF4568A86D17958E.description: Analyze how particular elements of a story or drama interact (e.g., how setting shapes the characters or plot).

463ADCA0DFE80131EF4468A86D17958E.description: Determine a theme or central idea of a text and analyze its development over the course of the text; provide an objective summary of the text.

463A85B0DFE80131EF4368A86D17958E.description: Cite several pieces of textual evidence to support analysis of what the text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text.

46395ED0DFE80131EF4068A86D17958E.description: Read and comprehend complex literary and informational texts independently and proficiently.

463913C0DFE80131EF3F68A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

4638C7D0DFE80131EF3E68A86D17958E.description: Analyze how two or more texts address similar themes or topics in order to build knowledge or to compare the approaches the authors take.

46387350DFE80131EF3D68A86D17958E.description: Delineate and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, including the validity of the reasoning as well as the relevance and sufficiency of the evidence.

46382600DFE80131EF3C68A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate content presented in diverse media and formats, including visually and quantitatively, as well as in words.
comments: Please see "Research to Build and Present Knowledge" in Writing and "Comprehension and Collaboration" in Speaking and Listening for additional standards relevant to gathering, assessing, and applying information from print and digital sources.

46378FB0DFE80131EF3A68A86D17958E.description: Assess how point of view or purpose shapes the content and style of a text.

463739E0DFE80131EF3968A86D17958E.description: Analyze the structure of texts, including how specific sentences, paragraphs, and larger portions of the text (e.g., a section, chapter, scene, or stanza) relate to each other and the whole.

4636E7F0DFE80131EF3868A86D17958E.description: Interpret words and phrases as they are used in a text, including determining technical, connotative, and figurative meanings, and analyze how specific word choices shape meaning or tone.

46363D10DFE80131EF3668A86D17958E.description: Analyze how and why individuals, events, and ideas develop and interact over the course of a text.

4635ED00DFE80131EF3568A86D17958E.description: Determine central ideas or themes of a text and analyze their development; summarize the key supporting details and ideas.

46359B50DFE80131EF3468A86D17958E.description: Read closely to determine what the text says explicitly and to make logical inferences from it; cite specific textual evidence when writing or speaking to support conclusions drawn from the text.

4634E8F0DFE80131EF3268A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Reading

document.title: Wisconsin's Model Academic Standards for Theatre

42D49D90DFE80131E93868A86D17958E.description: Rehearse and perform a scene or play for peers or invited guests

42D458F0DFE80131E93768A86D17958E.description: Exhibit understanding of theatre management through direct involvement in a public performance by making posters, selling tickets, and/or ushering

42D41300DFE80131E93668A86D17958E.description: Read a play and describe the potential visual and emotional effect it has on an audience

42D3C030DFE80131E93568A86D17958E.description: Analyze a play and determine appropriate setting, lighting, costume, and makeup requirements

42D379D0DFE80131E93468A86D17958E.description: Develop an understanding of design by creating a floor plan or visual representation of a play or literature selection

42D33270DFE80131E93368A86D17958E.description: Script their scene or play using proper scripting format

42D2EB20DFE80131E93268A86D17958E.description: Improvise a scene or play with a problem or conflict

42D2A4F0DFE80131E93168A86D17958E.description: Students will think and work as playwrights, designers, managers, and/or directors to create and interpret improvised and scripted scenes.

42D22720DFE80131E92F68A86D17958E.description: Identify what they need to do to make their character or scene more believable and/or understandable

42D1E4C0DFE80131E92E68A86D17958E.description: Continue to identify strengths (what worked) and weaknesses (what didn't work) in character work and scenes presented in class

42D19FC0DFE80131E92D68A86D17958E.description: Share their comments constructively and supportively within the group

42D15690DFE80131E92C68A86D17958E.description: Accept and use criticism constructively to revise and refine their own work

42D10C20DFE80131E92B68A86D17958E.description: Students in Wisconsin will work and think as theatre artists and reflect upon and assess the characteristics and merits of their own work and the work of others.

42D07D80DFE80131E92968A86D17958E.description: Continue to find information to help develop characters and the appropriate backgrounds for presentations

42D02F90DFE80131E92868A86D17958E.description: Continue to select stories or topics and plan plays with beginnings, middles, and ends

42CFE690DFE80131E92768A86D17958E.description: Write a review of a play and demonstrate an understanding of how a presentation was the same or different than other media presentations

42CF96C0DFE80131E92668A86D17958E.description: Explain in writing what they liked and didn't like about a dramatic presentation and justify their comments

42CF5790DFE80131E92568A86D17958E.description: Discuss the cultural/historical importance of a play through group discussion or written work

42CF1810DFE80131E92468A86D17958E.description: Read a play and exhibit understanding of the cultural/historical connections through discussions and/or written work

42CED430DFE80131E92368A86D17958E.description: Identify similarities and differences between various artistic mediums such as film, video, or television

42CE8BF0DFE80131E92268A86D17958E.description: Students in Wisconsin will research and analyze methods of presentation and audience response for theatre, the interconnections of theatre, community, other cultures, and historical periods for use as general knowledge.

42CDC750DFE80131E92068A86D17958E.description: Create a character (physically, verbally, and facially) from an original idea

42CD8D20DFE80131E91F68A86D17958E.description: Create a character (physically, verbally, and facially) from a scripted scene

42CD5200DFE80131E91E68A86D17958E.description: Select costume pieces or a hand prop (such as a basket) and create a character based upon that item

42CD1580DFE80131E91D68A86D17958E.description: Create a character that is appropriate to the context of the scene, using facial expressions

42CCD810DFE80131E91C68A86D17958E.description: Create a believable and sustained character within a scripted or improvised context

42CC95D0DFE80131E91B68A86D17958E.description: Create a character verbally, adapting language choices and dialogue to fit requirements of the scene

42CC3DD0DFE80131E91A68A86D17958E.description: Create a character through physical movement, adapting movement and making physical choices to fit the requirements of the scene

42CBED60DFE80131E91968A86D17958E.description: Students in Wisconsin will work and think as actors and develop basic acting skills to portray characters who interact in improvised and scripted scenes.

42CB6F70DFE80131E91768A86D17958E.description:
Read a play and be able to analyze, evaluate, and create personal meaning from the experience through small group discussion
  • say what they liked and didn't like, and why
  • explain what happened in the play and discuss why they think the playwright made particular choices
  • explain the message of the play

42CB2D70DFE80131E91668A86D17958E.description:
Attend a live theatrical performance and be able to analyze, evaluate, and create personal meaning from the experience through small group discussion
  • say what they liked and didn't like, and why
  • explain what happened in the play and discuss why they think the playwright made particular choices
  • explain how the technical aspects of the play helped to present the message of the play
  • explain the message of the play

42CAEA40DFE80131E91568A86D17958E.description: Students in Wisconsin will attend live theatre and read plays, be able to analyze and evaluate the play, and articulate (create meaning from) the play's message for individuals and society.

document.title: Wisconsin's Model Academic Standards for Science

4E8E7C00DFE80131FCBB68A86D17958E.description: Evaluate data and sources of information when using scientific information to make decisions

4E8F6F70DFE80131FCBE68A86D17958E.description: Investigate how current plans or proposals concerning resource management, scientific knowledge, or technological development will have an impact on the environment, ecology, and quality of life in a community or region

4E8DA1C0DFE80131FCB868A86D17958E.description: Advocate a solution or combination of solutions to a problem in science or technology

4E8DF000DFE80131FCB968A86D17958E.description: Show how policy decisions in science depend on social values, ethics, beliefs, and time-frames as well as considerations of science and technology

4E8E3720DFE80131FCBA68A86D17958E.description: Evaluate proposed policy recommendations (local, state, and/or national) in science and technology for validity, evidence, reasoning, and implications, both short and long-term

4E8F1D20DFE80131FCBD68A86D17958E.description: Using the science themes and knowledge of the earth and space, life and environmental, and physical sciences, analyze the costs, risks, benefits, and consequences of a proposal concerning resource management in the community and determine the potential impact of the proposal on life in the community and the region

4E8EC000DFE80131FCBC68A86D17958E.description: When making decisions, construct a plan that includes the use of current scientific knowledge and scientific reasoning

4E8D5E40DFE80131FCB768A86D17958E.description: Students in Wisconsin will use scientific information and skills to make decisions about themselves, Wisconsin, and the world in which they live.

4E8D1910DFE80131FCB668A86D17958E.description: Science in Personal and Social Perspectives

4E8C3E70DFE80131FCB368A86D17958E.description: Choose a specific problem in our society, identify alternative scientific or technological solutions to that problem and argue its merits

4E8BE4B0DFE80131FCB268A86D17958E.description: Show how a major scientific or technological change has had an impact on work, leisure, or the home

4E8B9210DFE80131FCB168A86D17958E.description: Analyze the costs, benefits, or problems resulting from a scientific or technological innovation, including implications for the individual and the community

4E8CD310DFE80131FCB568A86D17958E.description: Design, build, evaluate, and revise models and explanations related to the earth and space, life and environmental, and physical sciences

4E8C8B70DFE80131FCB468A86D17958E.description: Identify personal interests in science and technology, implications that these interests might have for future education, and decisions to be considered

4E8B3FE0DFE80131FCB068A86D17958E.description: Students in Wisconsin will demonstrate an understanding of the relationship between science and technology and the ways in which that relationship influences human activities.

4E85B760DFE80131FC9E68A86D17958E.description: Trace how the sensory and nervous systems of various organisms react to the internal and external environment and transmit survival or learning stimuli to cause changes in behavior or responses

4E88CE70DFE80131FCA868A86D17958E.description: Investigate how the complexity and organization of organisms accommodates the need for obtaining, transforming, transporting, releasing, and eliminating the matter and energy used to sustain an organism

4E882D00DFE80131FCA668A86D17958E.description: Understand the impact of energy on organisms in living systems

4E887C10DFE80131FCA768A86D17958E.description: Using the science themes, investigate energy systems (related to food chains) to show how energy is stored in food (plants and animals) and how energy is released by digestion and metabolism

4E87E4F0DFE80131FCA568A86D17958E.description: Matter, Energy and Organization in Living Systems

4E879A10DFE80131FCA468A86D17958E.description: Using the science themes, infer changes in ecosystems prompted by the introduction of new species, environmental conditions, chemicals, and air, water, or earth pollution

4E8751A0DFE80131FCA368A86D17958E.description: Investigate how organisms both cooperate and compete in ecosystems

4E89B820DFE80131FCAB68A86D17958E.description: Using concepts of evolution and heredity, account for changes in species and the diversity of species, include the influence of these changes on science, e.g. breeding of plants or animals

4E896760DFE80131FCAA68A86D17958E.description: Understand the theory of evolution, natural selection, and biological classification

4E865FE0DFE80131FCA068A86D17958E.description: State the relationships between functions of the cell and functions of the organism as related to genetics and heredity

4E86BFA0DFE80131FCA168A86D17958E.description: Explain current scientific ideas and information about the molecular and genetic basis of heredity

4E8AA100DFE80131FCAE68A86D17958E.description: Understand how cells differentiate and how cells are regulated

4E8A5A70DFE80131FCAD68A86D17958E.description: Evaluate the normal structures and the general and special functions of cells in single-celled and multiple-celled organisms

4E8520E0DFE80131FC9C68A86D17958E.description: Students in Wisconsin will demonstrate an understanding of the characteristics and structures of living things, the processes of life, and how living things interact with one another and their environment.

4E83DB60DFE80131FC9868A86D17958E.description: Using the science themes, understand that the origin of the universe is not completely understood, but that there are current ideas in science that attempt to explain its origin

4E836600DFE80131FC9768A86D17958E.description: The Origin and Evolution of the Universe

4E827980DFE80131FC9468A86D17958E.description: Analyze the benefits, costs, and limitations of past, present, and projected use of resources and technology and explain the consequences to the environment

4E822770DFE80131FC9368A86D17958E.description: Using the science themes, describe theories of the origins and evolution of the universe and solar system, including the earth system as a part of the solar system, and relate these theories and their implications to geologic time on earth

4E81D750DFE80131FC9268A86D17958E.description: The Origin and Evolution of the Earth System

4E848210DFE80131FC9A68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the geochemical and physical cycles of the earth and use them to describe movements of matter

4E8313C0DFE80131FC9668A86D17958E.description: Using the science themes, distinguish between internal energies (decay of radioactive isotopes, gravity) and external energies (sun) in the earth's systems and show how these sources of energy have an impact on those systems

4E818C30DFE80131FC9168A86D17958E.description: Students in Wisconsin will demonstrate an understanding of the structure and systems of earth and other bodies in the universe and of their interactions.

4E7D7F70DFE80131FC8468A86D17958E.description: Using the science themes, illustrate the law of conservation of energy during chemical and nuclear reactions

4E7D3C40DFE80131FC8368A86D17958E.description: Conservation of Energy and the Increase in Disorder

4E7E1240DFE80131FC8668A86D17958E.description: Through investigations, identify the types of chemical interactions, including endothermic, exothermic, oxidation, photosynthesis, and acid/base reactions

4E7EC220DFE80131FC8868A86D17958E.description: Identify patterns in chemical and physical properties and use them to predict likely chemical and physical changes and interactions

4E7E71D0DFE80131FC8768A86D17958E.description: Explain how substances, both simple and complex, interact with one another to produce new substances

4E808220DFE80131FC8E68A86D17958E.description: Explain exchanges of energy in chemical interactions and exchange of mass and energy in atomic/nuclear reactions

4E80D850DFE80131FC8F68A86D17958E.description: Explain the forces that hold the atom together and illustrate how nuclear interactions change the atom

4E803520DFE80131FC8D68A86D17958E.description: Describe atomic structure and the properties of atoms, molecules, and matter during physical and chemical interactions

4E7CF7B0DFE80131FC8268A86D17958E.description: Describe models of light, heat, and sound and through investigations describe similarities and differences in the way these energy forms behave

4E7CB130DFE80131FC8168A86D17958E.description: Understand the forces of gravitation, the electromagnetic force, intermolecular force, and explain their impact in the universal system

4E7C5E60DFE80131FC8068A86D17958E.description: Qualitatively and quantitatively analyze changes in the motion of objects and the forces that act on them and represent analytical data both algebraically and graphically

4E7BCC40DFE80131FC7E68A86D17958E.description: Students in Wisconsin will demonstrate an understanding of the physical and chemical properties of matter, the forms and properties of energy, and the ways in which matter and energy interact.

4E7B3170DFE80131FC7C68A86D17958E.description: Evaluate articles and reports in the popular press, in scientific journals, on television, and on the Internet, using criteria related to accuracy, degree of error, sampling, treatment of data, and other standards of experimental design

4E7994A0DFE80131FC7768A86D17958E.description: Present the results of investigations to groups concerned with the issues, explaining the meaning and implications of the results, and answering questions in terms the audience can understand

4E7A7D00DFE80131FC7A68A86D17958E.description: Use the explanations and models found in the earth and space, life and environmental, and physical sciences to develop likely explanations for the results of their investigations

4E79EA70DFE80131FC7868A86D17958E.description: During investigations, choose the best data-collection procedures and materials available, use them competently, and calculate the degree of precision of the resulting data

4E7AD800DFE80131FC7B68A86D17958E.description: Evaluate the data collected during an investigation, critique the data-collection procedures and results, and suggest ways to make any needed improvements

4E7A3580DFE80131FC7968A86D17958E.description: Identify issues from an area of science study, write questions that could be investigated, review previous research on these questions, and design and conduct responsible and safe investigations to help answer the questions

4E793990DFE80131FC7668A86D17958E.description: When studying science content, ask questions suggested by current social issues, scientific literature, and observations of phenomena, build hypotheses that might answer some of these questions, design possible investigations, and describe results that might emerge from such investigations

4E78DE10DFE80131FC7568A86D17958E.description: Students in Wisconsin will investigate questions using scientific methods and tools, revise their personal understanding to accommodate knowledge, and communicate these understandings to others.

4E776150DFE80131FC7068A86D17958E.description: Explain how science is based on assumptions about the natural world and themes that describe the natural world

4E782FA0DFE80131FC7368A86D17958E.description: Show how basic research and applied research contribute to new discoveries, inventions, and applications

4E77A5F0DFE80131FC7168A86D17958E.description: Relate the major themes of science to human progress in understanding science and the world

4E77EA50DFE80131FC7268A86D17958E.description: Identify the cultural conditions that are usually present during great periods of discovery, scientific development, and invention

4E771710DFE80131FC6F68A86D17958E.description: Show how cultures and individuals have contributed to the development of major ideas in the earth and space, life and environmental, and physical sciences

4E74FCF0DFE80131FC6868A86D17958E.description: Identify and, using evidence learned or discovered, replace inaccurate personal models and explanations of science-related events

document.title: Wisconsin's Model Academic Standards for Technology Education

4A3EAC40DFE80131F64768A86D17958E.description: Explain that people can control the technologies they develop and use and that people are responsible for the effects their technology has on society and the environment

4A3E63E0DFE80131F64668A86D17958E.description: Explain why people must think about how a new technology might affect other people, societies, and the ecosystem in which we live

4A3E1640DFE80131F64568A86D17958E.description: Contrast the advantages and disadvantages of given technology and make adjustments or develop new technologies if disadvantages outweigh the advantages

4A3DC110DFE80131F64468A86D17958E.description: Explain the importance of making projections, studying scenarios, and making thoughtful decisions because of the direct and indirect effects technology will have on the future

4A3D7990DFE80131F64368A86D17958E.description: Explain the difficulty in predicting the effects a new technology will have on society and the environment due to a lack of experience with the technology

4A3D2180DFE80131F64268A86D17958E.description: Students in Wisconsin will understand that technology affects society and the environment in ways that are both planned and unplanned and desirable and undesirable.
comments: People develop and use technology to enhance their quality of life. Technologies like the automobile, nuclear power, genetic engineering, and factory automation have enhanced our mobility, enabled us to harness new energy resources, increased food production, reduced disease, and freed people from tedious or dangerous tasks. While each of these technologies has very distinct advantages, they also have clear disadvantages that need to be weighed carefully by those who live in a technological society. Given the rapid growth in technological capability, it is important that every citizen take an active role in promoting the common good by making informed decisions about risks and benefits of technology. To be active citizens, students need to understand the positive and negative impacts of technology on society and the environment. They need to weigh carefully the benefits and risks of technologies, and make informed decisions about technological issues.

4A3C91E0DFE80131F64068A86D17958E.description: Explain how changing the physical characteristics of material or the format of information can increase its usefulness

4A3C4810DFE80131F63F68A86D17958E.description: Explain the value of technical knowledge and teamwork in the development of a device or process

4A3C0A50DFE80131F63E68A86D17958E.description: Predict possible outcomes of a newly designed technological system

4A3BCDB0DFE80131F63D68A86D17958E.description: Brainstorm and illustrate ways to integrate efficiency into design through the reuse of materials, resources, and waste in technological systems

4A3B8F90DFE80131F63C68A86D17958E.description: Explain and demonstrate several solutions to a problem or opportunity using technological design, tools, careful planning, experimentation, and testing

4A3B4DE0DFE80131F63B68A86D17958E.description: Research and develop a set of solutions to solve a problem not knowing all constraints

4A3AED80DFE80131F63A68A86D17958E.description: Students in Wisconsin will be able to define problems, gather information, explore options, devise a solution, evaluate the outcome, and communicate the results.
comments: Humans have historically been involved in technological activity. We use our knowledge, physical ability, and technology to solve problems and seize opportunity. The design, development, and use of technological items is a direct result of human resourcefulness. When a new technology is introduced and opportunities are acted upon, the technology begins to evolve bringing more opportunity and still more problems to solve.

4A3A5850DFE80131F63868A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast the use of tools, processes, and materials in diverse applications; such as, auto production, health care, food processing , laboratory research, and space exploration

4A3A1C10DFE80131F63768A86D17958E.description: Identify all the resources necessary for a given system; analyze how the use of the resources will be affected by consideration for cost, availability, appropriate application, and regard for the environment

4A39E080DFE80131F63668A86D17958E.description: Evaluate large and complex systems to determine the ways in which they are creations of human ingenuity

4A39A250DFE80131F63568A86D17958E.description: Discover that resources are essential; they must be used effectively to produce a desired outcome, and outputs from one system may be inputs to another system

4A395E40DFE80131F63468A86D17958E.description: Identify potential sources of failure in a system; such as, defective parts, maintenance needs, a large number of complex components, or use in applications beyond its original purpose

4A3914F0DFE80131F63368A86D17958E.description: Analyze various systems and identify the ways in which they are controlled to produce a desired outcome

4A38D910DFE80131F63268A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast the function of each of the following common elements of technological systems: inputs, processes, outputs, and feedback

comments: Technological systems have always been a part of daily life. Recently, they have become more apparent because of their sophistication and influence. By coordinating and processing resources, these systems help to provide products and services such as food, clothing, shelter, entertainment, health care, security, and other necessities and comforts of life. Though often subtle, these systems are everywhere in our world and, without exception, they impact all of us.
4A3899C0DFE80131F63168A86D17958E.description: Students in Wisconsin will recognize that systems are made up of individual components and that each component affects the operation of the system and its relationship to other systems.

4A3821F0DFE80131F62F68A86D17958E.description: Discover that human will or desire can lead to the design of new technology in order to seize an opportunity or solve a problem

4A37E0A0DFE80131F62E68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the distribution and access of various technologies and explain how inequities occur because of social and political systems

4A377E30DFE80131F62D68A86D17958E.description: Analyze how cultures and groups value technology differently and how these values influence the development and acceptance of technology

4A372DF0DFE80131F62C68A86D17958E.description: Determine that technological knowledge is valuable but not always available to everyone on an equal basis

4A36EC00DFE80131F62B68A86D17958E.description: Identify and contrast the connections and differences between technology and other disciplines

4A36A3D0DFE80131F62A68A86D17958E.description: Explain the need for and application of knowledge and skills from other disciplines when engaging in technological activities

4A365B80DFE80131F62968A86D17958E.description: Show that technology has allowed us to further the efforts of science and, in turn, science has enabled us to develop better technology

4A360E50DFE80131F62868A86D17958E.description: Students in Wisconsin will understand that technology is an extension of human capability.
comments: As long as there have been people, there has been technology. Indeed, the techniques of shaping tools are taken as the chief evidence of the beginning of human culture. On the whole, technology has been a powerful force in the development of civilization, all the more so as its link with science has been forged. Technology-like language, ritual, values, commerce, and the arts-is an intrinsic part of a cultural system and it both shapes and reflects the system's values. In today's world, technology is a complex social enterprise that includes not only research, design, and crafts but also finance, manufacturing, management, labor, marketing, and maintenance.

document.title: Common Core State Standards for English Language Arts

44621E40DFE80131EBB868A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

document.title: Wisconsin's Model Academic Standards for Technology Education

4A2758D0DFE80131F62568A86D17958E.description: Identify the advantages, disadvantages, risks, and benefits of given technologies

4A271C50DFE80131F62468A86D17958E.description: Evaluate and explain the impact people have had on the earth, including plant and animal life, through the development and introduction of technologies

4A26DEF0DFE80131F62368A86D17958E.description: Identify instances where technologies have had benefits and applications that no one predicted when they were first invented

4A269DA0DFE80131F62268A86D17958E.description: Explain how given technologies make life and work easier, but also how they may make them more complicated

4A265020DFE80131F62168A86D17958E.description: Identify new problems which result from using tools, materials, and processes to solve existing problems

comments: People develop and use technology to enhance their quality of life. Technologies like the automobile, nuclear power, genetic engineering, and factory automation have enhanced our mobility, enabled us to harness new energy resources, increased food production, reduced disease, and freed people from tedious or dangerous tasks. While each of these technologies has very distinct advantages, they also have clear disadvantages that need to be weighed carefully by those who live in a technological society. Given the rapid growth in technological capability, it is important that every citizen take an active role in promoting the common good by making informed decisions about risks and benefits of technology. To be active citizens, students need to understand the positive and negative impacts of technology on society and the environment. They need to weigh carefully the benefits and risks of technologies, and make informed decisions about technological issues.
4A2608C0DFE80131F62068A86D17958E.description: Students in Wisconsin will understand that technology affects society and the environment in ways that are both planned and unplanned and desirable and undesirable.

4A258B40DFE80131F61E68A86D17958E.description: Develop abilities in technological design and engineering around simple constraints

4A250950DFE80131F61C68A86D17958E.description: Approach problem and opportunity situations given a set of constraints and illustrate possible solutions using basic design principles

4A24C320DFE80131F61B68A86D17958E.description: Explain why people work collaboratively to design and produce products

4A246C10DFE80131F61A68A86D17958E.description: Use tools and materials to design, develop, or improve products that satisfy human wants and needs

4A241E20DFE80131F61968A86D17958E.description: Show how modern inventions and innovations have evolved as a result of new knowledge and technology

4A23D620DFE80131F61868A86D17958E.description: Examine products and processes and communicate how that product or process solved a human need or want

4A238610DFE80131F61768A86D17958E.description: Students in Wisconsin will be able to define problems, gather information, explore options, devise a solution, evaluate the outcome, and communicate the results.
comments: Humans have historically been involved in technological activity. We use our knowledge, physical ability, and technology to solve problems and seize opportunity. The design, development, and use of technological items is a direct result of human resourcefulness. When a new technology is introduced and opportunities are acted upon, the technology begins to evolve bringing more opportunity and still more problems to solve.

4A22E200DFE80131F61568A86D17958E.description: Explain how tools and materials are used to provide services and create products

4A227BA0DFE80131F61468A86D17958E.description: Follow a set of instructions to produce a product using appropriate tools and materials

4A224030DFE80131F61368A86D17958E.description: Identify and compare enterprises as technological systems

4A2203F0DFE80131F61268A86D17958E.description: Explain how systems depend on a variety of resources to produce a desirable outcome

4A21C4E0DFE80131F61168A86D17958E.description: Describe various reasons systems may fail; such as, overuse, lack of proper maintenance or management, improper design, or other natural or unnatural factors that may occur

4A218410DFE80131F61068A86D17958E.description: Identify the parts of a system and explain how the parts working together allow the system to do things the individual parts are unable to do alone

4A2143D0DFE80131F60F68A86D17958E.description: Identify and categorize systems that provide food, clothing, shelter, entertainment, health care, security, and other necessities and comforts of life

4A20F580DFE80131F60E68A86D17958E.description: Students in Wisconsin will recognize that systems are made up of individual components and that each component affects the operation of the system and its relationship to other systems.
comments: Technological systems have always been a part of daily life. Recently, they have become more apparent because of their sophistication and influence. By coordinating and processing resources, these systems help to provide products and services such as food, clothing, shelter, entertainment, health care, security, and other necessities and comforts of life. Though often subtle, these systems are everywhere in our world and, without exception, they impact all of us.

4A206E90DFE80131F60C68A86D17958E.description: Predict possible evolution scenarios for a modern piece of technology

4A203080DFE80131F60B68A86D17958E.description: Use tools to observe, measure, make things, and transfer information

4A1FF480DFE80131F60A68A86D17958E.description: Research how different groups in the world use technology

4A1FB3F0DFE80131F60968A86D17958E.description: Illustrate how technology has evolved throughout human history

4A1F4DD0DFE80131F60868A86D17958E.description: Determine that humans have always developed tools to communicate, build, move things, and reshape their environment to meet their wants and needs

4A1EF930DFE80131F60768A86D17958E.description: Explain that the purpose of a designed object is to solve a problem or enhance the quality of life

4A1EB520DFE80131F60668A86D17958E.description: Conclude that technology cannot always satisfy every human want and need

4A1E7090DFE80131F60568A86D17958E.description: Realize that all humans engage in technological activities; therefore, everyone is a technologist

4A1E2BF0DFE80131F60468A86D17958E.description: Discover that technology is know-how that extends human capabilities to solve problems or enhances the quality of life while science helps us to discover what is natural

4A1DE130DFE80131F60368A86D17958E.description: Students in Wisconsin will understand that technology is an extension of human capability.
comments: As long as there have been people, there has been technology. Indeed, the techniques of shaping tools are taken as the chief evidence of the beginning of human culture. On the whole, technology has been a powerful force in the development of civilization, all the more so as its link with science has been forged. Technology-like language, ritual, values, commerce, and the arts-is an intrinsic part of a cultural system and it both shapes and reflects the system's values. In today's world, technology is a complex social enterprise that includes not only research, design, and crafts but also finance, manufacturing, management, labor, marketing, and maintenance.

4BC318A0DFE80131F80968A86D17958E.description: Partition circles and rectangles into two, three, or four equal shares, describe the shares using the words halves, thirds, half of, a third of, etc., and describe the whole as two halves, three thirds, four fourths. 4BC0AA20DFE80131F80168A86D17958E.description: Represent whole numbers as lengths from 0 on a number line diagram with equally spaced points corresponding to the numbers 0, 1, 2, …, and represent whole-number sums and differences within 100 on a number line diagram.

4BBFA690DFE80131F7FD68A86D17958E.description: Estimate lengths using units of inches, feet, centimeters, and meters.
