50FE88FDB8EA4F41A4D3D1CEF6A1F28D.description:
The ocean exerts a major influence on weather and climate by absorbing energy from the sun, releasing it over time, and globally
redistributing it through ocean currents. (MS-ESS2-6)

B80A48F580C34C4996ACA4D0FD5278DB.description:
Weather and climate are influenced by interactions involving sunlight,
the ocean, the atmosphere, ice, landforms, and living things. These
interactions vary with latitude, altitude, and local and regional
geography, all of which can affect oceanic and atmospheric flow
patterns. (MS-ESS2-6)

E903598D958D44929854BD4C2D66BEAC.description:
Variations in density due to variations in temperature and salinity drive
a global pattern of interconnected ocean currents. (MS-ESS2-6)

D13F0CFF7A664ADAA9257D92DC33A791.description:
Develop and use a model to describe how unequal heating and rotation of the Earth cause patterns of
atmospheric and oceanic circulation that determine regional climates.

C701B2AFBE6543DFB25B4212FEA181BA.description:
Because these patterns are so complex, weather can only be predicted
probabilistically. (MS-ESS2-5)

932A9AE663EA4632B59CF39C5B87838C.description:
The complex patterns of the changes and the movement of water in the
atmosphere, determined by winds, landforms, and ocean temperatures
and currents, are major determinants of local weather patterns. (MSESS2-5)

3436B05AE41D49ADB62FDB87116392DB.description:
Collect data to provide evidence for how the motions and complex interactions of air masses results in changes
in weather conditions.

01457D22257F46DF83C40B36D4714E5D.description:
Global movements of water and its changes in form are propelled by
sunlight and gravity. (MS-ESS2-4)

42B5768FEAF847C59B5C92E59EA5391B.description:
Water continually cycles among land, ocean, and atmosphere via
transpiration, evaporation, condensation and crystallization, and
precipitation, as well as downhill flows on land. (MS-ESS2-4)

82BF4F7C7FB74F71BF3D3A9A86820FBD.description:
Develop a model to describe the cycling of water through Earth’s systems driven by energy from the sun and the
force of gravity.

B2AA561CE1024D5CA53BD184ABF611AB.description:
Maps of ancient land and water patterns, based on investigations of
rocks and fossils, make clear how Earth’s plates have moved great
distances, collided, and spread apart. (MS-ESS2-3)

D204DB4B209242B7BB2CD3769A105930.description:
Tectonic processes continually generate new ocean sea floor at ridges
and destroy old sea floor at trenches. (HS.ESS1.C GBE) (secondary to
MS-ESS2-3)

28BD0B3E03424BB79D65E2B55DAC9F24.description:
Analyze and interpret data on the distribution of fossils and rocks, continental shapes, and seafloor structures to
provide evidence of the past plate motions.

8750195A440A42C19D97F7C6050D4AFB.description:
Water’s movements—both on the land and underground—cause
weathering and erosion, which change the land’s surface features and
create underground formations. (MS-ESS2-2)

DB31927818904224A337B9B2CE555454.description:
The planet’s systems interact over scales that range from microscopic to
global in size, and they operate over fractions of a second to billions of
years. These interactions have shaped Earth’s history and will determine
its future. (MS-ESS2-2)

B939426430FD45B1BDE1676259B1194D.description:
Construct an explanation based on evidence for how geoscience processes have changed Earth’s surface at
varying time and spatial scales.

E9144225E9334535A87C033EE123B9BB.description:
All Earth processes are the result of energy flowing and matter cycling
within and among the planet’s systems. This energy is derived from the
sun and Earth’s hot interior. The energy that flows and matter that
cycles produce chemical and physical changes in Earth’s materials and
living organisms. (MS-ESS2-1)

9F7198AF46BA4B78B6AED62F334BBB13.description: Develop a model to describe the cycling of Earth’s materials and the flow of energy that drives this process.

document.title: Wisconsin Standards for English Language Arts

3C8B0CDEA47146F4915345B4FA3F1031.description: Demonstrate contextually appropriate use of the conventions of standardized English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing. Discern when and where it is appropriate to use standardized English. Appropriately use and explain the intended purpose in conventions with:

D026990E2DC84127980FD9973659C2B4.description: Simple, compound, and complex sentences signaling differing relationships among ideas.

19D73C67E5C945FBAA79D4A1AAD454B0.description: Demonstrate contextually appropriate use of the conventions of standardized English grammar and usage when writing or speaking. Discern when and where it is appropriate to use standardized English. Appropriately use and explain the intended purpose of language choice with:

3AF4BC6D367C41DEB5E0C41A2B5B4A1A.description: Demonstrate an ability to collaboratively and independently build vocabulary knowledge when encountering unknown words including cultural, general academic, and discipline-specific terms and phrases; make intentional vocabulary choices appropriate to the context and situation.

781CFEC3B2A844A69141EC985E38FEA6.description: Analyze the impact of rhyme and other repetitions of sound (e.g., alliteration; assonance) in varied texts (e.g., poetry; drama; section of a story).

CCD0D2BD89274F1F977F06AAE23E8AB0.description: Determine the denotative, connotative, and figurative meanings of words and phrases used in texts; when words have similar denotations, be able to describe differences in connotation and their impact on meaning and tone.

67326FF831D443AC8DBE6E364D00D5A8.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

FED4095BCD64428E8CDF8A03DB3677A3.description: Use grade-appropriate Greek or Latin affixes and roots as clues to the meaning of a word.

9A2063F4A89546F19456AE6CDBFD41F4.description: Verify the preliminary determination of the meaning of a word or phrase (e.g., by checking the inferred meaning in context or in a dictionary).

55972DDFBDF14A8085D502D8CA153AF0.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases in grade-level reading and content; use context clues, analyze meaningful word parts, consult general and specialized reference materials, and apply word solving strategies (for meaning) as appropriate

EC1066ED14FC4B9AAEB466C748A23C2E.description: When appropriate, eliminate wordiness and redundancy.

E062940AA633419D938BE70A629E47AE.description: Maintain consistency in style and tone.

5694066310EB4E4F8B0C611D66F95E89.description: Determine the language demands of a writing/speaking situation; respond in appropriate ways (e.g., precise and concise language; extended and descriptive language; incorporation of code-meshing, etc.).

0EE8634B83864EBCAA2F2F25AD0194A0.description: Recognize that standardized English is only one dialect of many and has a specific history that is implicated in power relationships.

3B05204A152B454DB5A1BBC52D96B43E.description: Demonstrate an understanding of how language functions in different cultures, contexts, and disciplines; apply this knowledge to comprehend more fully when reading and listening, and make effective choices when composing, creating, and speaking.

DFA4C3B24A2C40939F498559FA137CD0.description: Include multimedia components and visual displays in presentations to clarify claims and findings and emphasize significant points.

FB0690961F674F5CBADE1F5EA578AC58.description: Present claims and findings, emphasizing significant points in a focused, coherent manner using relevant evidence. Communicate clearly and in an engaging manner, considering the audience, purpose, and situation. Explain purpose of language choices.

3F3E1B0896E64E7EA1841769326F608A.description: Understand and evaluate a speaker's argument and specific claims, evaluating the soundness of the reasoning and the relevance and sufficiency of the evidence.

0521195728294180AE165850A164FCB3.description: Analyze the main ideas and supporting details presented in diverse media and formats and explain how the ideas clarify a topic, text, or issue under study.

DFFB49C319D9480EAF954DF2F3CB56CC.description: Review the key ideas expressed and demonstrate an understanding of multiple perspectives through analysis, including reflection, clarification, and paraphrasing.

DC1E7248D4884F64ADD58C1E86A46C62.description: Pose questions that invite elaboration and respond to others' questions and comments with relevant observations and ideas that bring the discussion back on topic as needed. Promote multiple perspectives.

000271A183BF4AF9881B8E4E9F330B0D.description: With guidance and support, set and track specific norms and goals for collegial discussions (e.g., gaining attention in respectful ways, actively listening, speaking one at a time about the topics and texts under discussion).

F4D0B0DADDFB45F288605F3B99A4234C.description: Come to discussions prepared and explicitly draw on that preparation by referring to evidence on the topic, text, or issue. Support analysis by making connections, paraphrasing, clarifying, or explaining the evidence.

2E42AD10BCB64348B7970918CA3F1A95.description: Engage effectively in a range of collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in groups, and teacher led) with diverse partners on topics, texts, and issues, building on others' ideas and expressing one's thinking clearly.

287DB35782C44B35B7BD21D0A8252BD6.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and inquiry.

1AE93BB7BC724DC898F72CDA17C8A638.description: Gather relevant information from multiple print and digital sources, using search terms effectively; assess the credibility and accuracy of each source; quote or paraphrase the data and conclusions of others while avoiding plagiarism and following a standard format for citation.

B139CFEC47B643148CA7AFB3DC8D4975.description: Conduct short inquiry projects to answer a question, drawing on several sources and generating additional related, focused questions for further research and investigation.

0A4A686092E049578BA67EEE3321AEF4.description: Inquiry to Build and Present Knowledge

CE81408DF189439BB5431F05F125C1A0.description: Use technology, (including paper and pencil, internet, audio, visual, multilingual, multimodal, mobile, and/or other interactive formats), to produce and publish writing and present the relationships between information and ideas efficiently, as well as to interact and collaborate with others, including linking to and citing sources.

7801D246DF554689B94F2776EA7AD848.description: With some guidance and support from peers and adults, develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach, focusing on how well purpose and audience have been addressed.

AC52E3592C7E4046BEB9360C38434BBE.description: Independently and collaboratively produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are culturally-sustaining and rhetorically authentic to task, purpose, and audience.

DD44B6FB94F84316A4231B034BBEDDD1.description: Word Choice (including domain specific): use words, phrases, and clauses to create cohesion and clarify the relationships. Use sensory language to describe experiences and events.

23BD309814924C45AAF43619CC440A26.description: Transitions: use a variety of appropriate transitions that connect and develop ideas.

DDB8CAF871994120B7D1455C4F4BA2C5.description: Organization: provide an introduction that creates suspense and anticipation for the reader. Structure of the text supports and clarifies the purpose and topic. Provide a concluding statement appropriate to the mode of writing.

F5E1741E0E5A435E862641C14EC18FAA.description: Write narratives that develop real or imagined experiences or events using relevant descriptive details and well-structured event sequences that organize an event sequence logically. Engage and orient the reader by establishing a context and point of view and introduces a narrator or characters; using techniques, such as dialogue, pacing, description, and reflection, to develop experiences, events, and characters.

6B8F06395DBD4674A344E5487E607BF1.description: Write informative text that examines a topic and conveys ideas, concepts, and information through the selection and organization of relevant content by introducing and developing a topic with relevant, well-chosen facts, definitions, concrete details, quotations, or other information and examples, organizing ideas, concepts, and information into broader categories; include formatting (e.g., headings), graphics (e.g., charts, tables), and multimedia when useful to aiding comprehension.

59FC55C2D05B458DA08394AB625C931F.description: Write arguments to support claims with clear reasons, relevant evidence and literary theory. Introduce claim(s), acknowledge alternate or opposing claims, and organize the reasons and evidence logically. Use accurate, credible sources.

47AB84C94CCE4E3CA391E90EB86AAC3E.description: Write text in a variety of modes:

1F1725D56645450D8B3BE8CE1B157AEF.description: Compose reflective, formal, and creative writing, which may happen simultaneously or independently, for a variety of high-stakes and low-stakes purposes.

9BB4C752BE104798B170E189CFD13145.description: Evaluate the quality of texts. Make connections to other texts, ideas, cultural perspectives, identities, eras, and personal experiences.

28F0CD33676A474EB202C6F3317912FF.description: Trace and evaluate the development of an argument and specific claims in a text. Assess whether the reasoning is valid and the evidence is relevant and sufficient. Recognize when irrelevant evidence is introduced.

F088F70702EA497BBD81D1F8E9D41478.description: Compare and contrast a written text with audio, filmed, staged, or digital versions in order to analyze the effects of techniques unique to each media and each format's portrayal of a subject.

14739902389A4CA4AA67B4E08654F8BB.description:
In literary texts, analyze how an author develops and contrasts the point of view, possible biases, and the perspectives of different characters or narrators.
  • In informational texts, explain how an author's geographic location, identity, and/or culture affect perspective. Analyze how the author distinguishes his or her position from that of others.

2D4A6DB037634A80BF919FB401BB569D.description:
In literary texts, analyze how structure, including genre-specific features, contributes to the development of themes or central ideas.
  • In informational texts, analyze the structure an author uses to organize a text, including how the sections contribute to the whole and to the development of themes or central ideas.

7355EEABC04B4F539CA08ADF586D03FA.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases, including figurative and connotative meanings. Analyze the impact of specific word choices on meaning, tone, and mood, including words with multiple meanings within a text.

0679EC32C4204F79A54E6A236D78A60F.description:
In literary texts, analyze how elements of plot are related, affect one another, and contribute to meaning.
  • In informational texts, analyze how individuals, events, and ideas are introduced, related to each other, and developed.

A3222CA89F6C430792F96A876C989755.description: Summarize texts, from a variety of genres, to determine a theme or central idea and analyze its development over the course of the text.

FA78034678974B0D9D8A8E0182A2E383.description: Cite textual evidence to support an analysis of what the text says explicitly/implicitly and make logical inferences.

document.title: Wisconsin Standards for Mathematics

2307231DD55141D59E818B869197E34B.description: Partition circles and rectangles into two, three, or four equal shares, describe and count the shares using the words halves, thirds, and fourths, and use phrases half of, a third of, and a fourth of the whole. Describe the whole as composed of two halves, three thirds, and four fourths. Recognize that equal shares of identical wholes need not have the same shape.

643ED3AA69DE4852BC3BA0E7B6497FCF.description: Partition a rectangle into rows and columns of same-size squares and count to find the total number of them.

F8C0E31241514514B140B3C6EF8AAFCD.description: Recognize and draw shapes having specified attributes, such as a given number of angles or a given number of equal faces. Identify triangles, quadrilaterals, pentagons, hexagons, and cubes. Sizes are compared directly or visually, not compared by measuring.

DBFA990747744F449F6F79C6914203A4.description: Reason with shapes and their attributes.

33DE584F2D074EDB8A0B8AA41CEAFB6F.description: Draw a picture graph and a bar graph (with single-unit scale) to represent a data set with up to four categories. Solve simple put together, take-apart, and compare problems using information presented in a bar graph.

01B7254ECCC8488CA250320AD1B491B3.description: Generate measurement data by measuring lengths of several objects to the nearest whole unit, or by making repeated measurements of the same object. Show the measurements by making a line plot, where the horizontal scale is marked off in whole-number units.

966090126B8B4B81AF412B46F34EC0F7.description: Solve word problems involving dollar bills, quarters, dimes, nickels, and pennies, using $ and ¢ symbols appropriately.

CB2C54F46DFC4BB7939C3773B99111FE.description: Tell and write time from analog and digital clocks to the nearest five minutes, using a.m. and p.m.

B944E7F9F7F64C4E9D6F1B64692FC2B3.description: Represent whole numbers as lengths from 0 on a number line with equally spaced points corresponding to the numbers 0, 1, 2 ... and represent whole-number sums and differences within 100 on a number line.

035557B757A34500B9BE7244FA159AD3.description: Use addition and subtraction within 100 to solve word problems involving lengths that are given in the same units, e.g., by using drawings (such as number lines) and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.

020174FEF49A495893ACD68A847136CD.description: Relate addition and subtraction to length.

D51C82CF1702458F8D9B59AA553459EF.description: Measure to determine how much longer one object is than another, expressing the length difference in terms of a standard length unit.

A59FEB88DD7140BDA158572C9717CD8F.description: Estimate lengths using units of inches, feet, centimeters, and meters.

4D4B3FBA4AFE4AD9B72F41C1B509ED11.description: Measure the length of an object twice, using length units of different lengths for the two measurements; describe how the two measurements relate to the size of the unit chosen.

F388DECE67604CF69285C27A39C944CF.description: Measure the length of an object by selecting and using appropriate tools such as rulers, yardsticks, meter sticks, and measuring tapes.

FACF7383E1A64571BC67BEC850640256.description: Measure and estimate lengths in standard units.

A92E4A9C2295436B806FDC6FCA08E87B.description: Explain why addition and subtraction strategies work, using place value and the properties of operations. These explanations may be supported by drawings or objects.

66784C7B55EF46F79FD9A9FB2869B3B9.description: Mentally add 10 or 100 to a given number 100 - 900, and mentally subtract 10 or 100 from a given number 100 - 900.

CCF4FB9751AC4E0ABE1B4F681F2A111A.description: Add and subtract within 1000, using concrete models or drawings and strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction; relate the strategy to a written method. Understand that in adding or subtracting three digit numbers, one adds or subtracts hundreds and hundreds, tens and tens, ones and ones; and sometimes it is necessary to compose or decompose tens or hundreds.

3C31B9D6E1414499AB9012ACC6711E1B.description: Add up to four two-digit numbers using strategies based on place value and properties of operations.

187F72C475CB48AB9498DEEDC658CADE.description: Flexibly and efficiently add and subtract within 100 using strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction. In Grade 2, subtraction with decomposition is an exception and may include drawings/representations.

A1CAE7FD9AB8497B97CC95A55FC2B5FA.description: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to add and subtract.

3F8A88428C844C219A651D4D2A7000A9.description: Compare two three-digit numbers based on meanings of the hundreds, tens, and ones digits, and describe the result of the comparison using words and symbols ( >, =, and < ).

83A3BF95F79948908C316F823056706E.description: Read and write numbers to 1000 using base-ten numerals, number names, and expanded form.

01B3B003E9C34FADAA1E8136420D814D.description: The numbers 100,200,300,400,500,600,700,800, 900 refer to one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine hundreds (and 0 tens and 0 ones).

B245D707B53D4A85902512DDAEA5438D.description: 100 can be thought of as a bundle of ten tens -- called a "hundred".

D295A2229F9642899CF329D3557F3A22.description: Understand that the three digits of a three-digit number represent amounts of hundreds, tens, and ones; e.g., 706 equals 7 hundreds, 0 tens, and 6 ones. Understand the following as special cases:

FBE4E2CF983D4367999DC2020C0069DA.description: Number and Operations in Base Ten

7C046506F61740CBA1A4ED3C052490CA.description: Use addition to find the total number of objects arranged in rectangular arrays with up to 5 rows and up to 5 columns; write an equation to express the total as a sum of equal addends.

B5B84213188146BA8F0C916454936321.description: Determine whether a group of objects (up to 20) has an odd or even number of members, e.g., by pairing objects or counting them by 2s; write an equation to express an even number as a sum of two equal addends.

76234862B0364B11A27F4E5F1B4DEE8D.description: Work with equal groups of objects to gain foundations for multiplication.

9BE6A49F618B4734A804F682F9BED747.description: Flexibly and efficiently add and subtract within 20 using multiple mental strategies which may include counting on; making ten; decomposing a number leading to a ten; using the relationship between addition and subtraction (e.g., knowing that 8 + 4 = 12, one knows 12 - 8 = 4); and creating equivalent but easier or known sums (e.g., adding 6 + 7 by creating the known equivalent 6 + 6 + 1 = 12 + 1 = 13).

DA666C42DD3D444092F79D9709BAB97C.description: Use addition and subtraction within 100 to solve one- and two-step word problems involving situations of adding to, taking from, putting together, taking apart, and comparing, with unknowns in all positions, e.g., by using drawings and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.

14C33D83627744FF87CF13A8BD473B96.description: Represent and solve problems involving addition and subtraction.

EBA5D4B6D1C04FE9A597B58A7B6FD9DC.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

5309B75737E24AECA424CC0E49BB7BCD.description: Look for and make use of structure.

5B34CCFD1FEE4E2D9F9BC2418A9C9ABB.description: Construct viable arguments, and appreciate and critique the reasoning of others.

9D174E6E6E8448289FABB47EF90B246A.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

document.title: Wisconsin Standards for Personal Financial Literacy

36602897A0B14AB78AE3E8AB3D1F3AE2.description: Determine the best type(s) of protection for given scenarios regarding risk (e.g., wearing a coat in the cold or wearing a bike helmet).

F69EA7F069B649A2825088A359413963.description: Illustrate what both people have to do when they enter an agreement.

0293993CFFD44A25930369634E31043B.description: Predict consequences of not having protection for various scenarios.

280785E761874C00893B709B16B411B5.description: Identify why someone would get insurance on valuable items (e.g., cell phone or game console).

950BC513E3CA4CD3BE2105E9C09C0186.description: Students will assess possible choices to protect themselves from financial risk.

C12A3B0C824A491594D8080543C6F068.description: Predict some risks in everyday situations (e.g., playing on the playground, staying up too late, or riding a bike) and explain ways to limit these risks.

2EBBF88984B844B088A24B5E1135053B.description: Describe the feeling of losing an object (e.g., losing money, losing a favorite toy, or losing homework assignments).

B3F40FCD949F4BFE8CF6A77D43B83B2E.description: Students will contrast different types of risk and how it could affect their financial decisions.

EE87745B6DA548CCB362C8986DAAE00E.description: Identify different forms of payment methods (e.g., online, cash, debit card, credit card, or loan).

1B5C1670E15B4A7DAE6018DF423675B8.description: Students will interpret lending options, consumer rights, and responsibilities.

B42B96CB5CDA42BF87EB5495C710EAFC.description: Explain who can assist in solving problems (e.g., parents, teachers, or counselors).

CEBA0EAD9BBD4233A0BC55C40C93E371.description: Identify actions a borrower can take to satisfy a lender when a borrowed item cannot be repaid, is lost, or damaged.

C0F2EF0C1F34469A915A63A7E3123DF3.description: Explain how people can borrow money or an item if they promise to return it.

2C22DA1EB90842E28C81DA4C92087425.description: Explain the difference between buying and borrowing.

226FA2C493484786B22CCC6B752E0CD5.description: Explain why something borrowed must be returned.

4A91F250EBC14993A769E37D6BB5C674.description: Students will examine the benefits and costs of using credit.

619430C41D5542DD8F7807ED7009A315.description: Identify how items of value may fluctuate over time.

5C5D3818B48542E484F74307ECB1D508.description: Identify the difference between short-term and long-term (e.g., today versus Saturday versus the future or elementary versus middle school versus high school).

1BD57EBBD4D641FCAF92C2540779A21E.description: Differentiate between owning something of value, keeping money in a financial institution, or giving money to someone else in return for future value.

01A41809695D40DD99837644CCFD3D1E.description: Explain how gathering items of value may build net worth.

C832CD29B7984E7180FB8E4096DA5096.description: Students will explore investing concepts and apply this knowledge to attain financial security.

D0C9B1C0E81A4A8F8869842CE90EB5AC.description: Explain how financial institutions help people make choices about how to save money.

10A2A45A6F8B413B96AB7BC5AC32D926.description: Explain how choices we make now affect what we get in the future.

593762380AA049CF86C7C94FA34280BD.description: Identify places where something valuable would be secure.

53578D9DB762478BB420DF4B8CEE328A.description: Identify an experience of waiting to have enough money to buy something.

669DFFE5BBE7459CA64771477F9A60CB.description: Students will explore savings concepts and apply this knowledge to attain financial security.

C7E3F13CC2D24721B3B26B0C4368479F.description: Describe how paying for goods and services online is still using real money.

DF3A6A4790694F3582C71E122C83B599.description: Recognize that items of value, including money, can be earned and exchanged for goods and services.

8D73D52284B1442D80E5C38FF2258250.description: Identify financial institutions within the community.

DF871EAA1BCA4110AED0BE8676768D5C.description: Students will utilize financial institutions and service providers to support money management

216CDDC5B37E484AB5952D700C7E5E61.description: Identify that there are three ways you can use money - save, spend, and give.

E785627089894BCA93498DCD10C42504.description: Explain the importance of a budget.

41687BC3EA194F1D9E453F3804080DEC.description: Students will demonstrate their ability to use money management skills and strategies.

15402C1FF356412B8B77FC2E611D9C84.description: Describe how specific jobs or career fields have changed over time.

1081A8D984CE47C28A4BB38316B372ED.description: Categorize jobs as high demand or low demand.

5AF3A1686176425B86AD3AD0FDD22CA5.description: Discover the different skills associated with various job or career fields (e.g., what skills are needed to be a plumber, teacher, dentist, firefighter or store manager).

9B5884C0F9CA4B049325A2ADCCB030DC.description: Identify skills needed for different types of jobs.

9D1EB4F16B0B4C0EA467CCA803AA0635.description: Students will evaluate the impact of lifelong learning on one’s ability to function effectively in a diverse and changing economy.

57B32F2E023B42FF804E7BE53093E319.description:
Summarize goods and Explain behaviors and
services that the government decisions that reflect
provides (e.g., roads, schools, interests, likes, and dislikes.
or police).

33B1DE04C11A442590A3DDED6EAFA9D2.description: Students will compare the effect of personal income on their goals.

E4F42A95AC644ACFBA121B090F1851DB.description: List websites or mobile apps and identify what types of information people access online.

9CD8AE799E144C88845D7B9A615992D9.description: Define sources of digital information and storage (e.g., Internet, World Wide Web, and personal devices).

E16D463D4A564AA989A2CA5692CE3B32.description: Explain the importance of an online password, and identify reasons to use a password.

16D30D3E11F94BFEBF8FB99D6C9F5082.description: Students will establish digital awareness to enhance their financial mindset.

9ED2FCC4A2F248F392AA6AE1540DB53E.description: Recognize ways to give back (e.g., donating to a charity or volunteering) in our classroom, school, community, state, tribal nation, country, and in the world.

459FB07C2E0145F4B04C26A8628CB1D1.description: Civic Engagement and Philanthropy (e.g., giving back, volunteering, donation, or charity)

6258A9483313409EB07512FA8A989149.description: Identify the importance of a financial goal (e.g., purchasing a bicycle or toy).

B058AC60DA4E4B50A555808E1C15FBE0.description: Identify external influences (e.g., peers, family, or community) that may affect what someone wants.

C3742F95A08F4A418FC14AC07AF10001.description: Identify how emotions may be the same or different from other people.

C3500A43EC8245AAA3EF5AE8EC2CD1C0.description: Identify why people decide to earn, save, spend, or give money.

5C241E5DE89B41F1BB948C81137868BD.description: Students will analyze how aspects of financial psychology impact financial well-being.

F74188B253084D0781B5F7FFCB81DD8D.description: Differentiate between a want and a need.

023565ADC61041749AA1D4A489B468C3.description: Identify and analyze leverage points and cause and effect relationships within a system.

8FDAFBA4606B417CB1D7B24EBF9F2641.description: Analyze the role of feedback loops in reinforcing the interconnectedness of parts within a system and the consequences of actions by each of those parts on the whole.

C37AB63077C14EA9ABBB6535BD1460E8.description: Students analyze the dynamic balance between natural and cultural systems.

2E7C09F07556483AA9FF830CA932B56B.description: Evaluate how natural resource use, practices, and technological advances impact natural and cultural systems.

DE9847B86F724DB0B055DBCE5885661C.description: Analyze historical and contemporary strategies to solving sustainability issues to develop alternative approaches for addressing parallel issues in the future.

5C7AE0F29C464E05A49708B82BCB91B4.description: Create and interpret models to describe how change in the flow of energy into and out of Earth's systems by human and nonhuman causes impacts natural and cultural systems, such as climate.

6609C4C1259F43A19D4AAECD94FEA7F3.description: Examine historic and projected climate patterns to evaluate potential impacts on the stability of natural and cultural systems and identify strategies for adaptation and mitigation.

10C1112C2E8A4C91BC43BD6D14108F06.description: Create a model that demonstrates how to restore or increase the stability of a system in response to change.

6276B64F64C74519B754DB2519284ED9.description: Evaluate how feedback loops impact natural systems over time and predict adaptive strategies.

B07FAF43AF5941A8818A91056CA40357.description: Argue a perspective regarding a sustainability issue by examining individual and group actions, critiquing the decision-making processes, describing shared and conflicting values and principles, and assessing the impact on natural and cultural systems.

1DB52FD5A5BE49AD9F592B14F625EC4D.description: Investigate and analyze how change and adaptation impact natural and cultural systems.

386E513879F94C8995C5A02B2880D347.description: Analyze how the movement of natural resources through acquisition, production, consumption, and disposal impact sustainability of local, regional, and global systems.

4D516252856C4AA1B25CC0D696622B7F.description: Examine the role of renewable and nonrenewable resources in creating sustainable economies.

6D908304776846F6837E70D81D821069.description: Apply the laws of conservation of mass and energy to analyze cycles and flows of Earth's systems, including: the cycling of matter and flow of energy among the biotic and abiotic components in the biosphere, atmosphere, geosphere, and hydrosphere; the transfer and loss of energy and mass at each link in an ecosystem ; and the roles of photosynthesis, cellular respiration, and carbon sequestration in the global carbon cycle.

7241A5CBC96D4EB3B591DE0CEF9D0B8A.description: Analyze the interactions and outcomes of cycles and flows in natural and cultural systems.

2D3E6564DFED44BF9BC8FE723B4B4B5B.description: Analyze, compare, and critique the ethics of societal actions and impacts of ethnocentrism.

BE2BDC49128049028833774144048ECA.description: Analyze the use and distribution of resources worldwide and the impact on populations, including historically marginalized populations.

62F3E1835013457E87FEB4A40C4813D6.description: Evaluate how groups have addressed issues of equity in environmental health and sustainability.

24913032D0824CC1B9F1CBAAF2424DBA.description: Evaluate, from a variety of cultural perspectives, the concept of shared natural resources and what is needed to maintain its health and accessibility for all.

DD38517EE75545378ED05E057E3AEBFF.description: Design and evaluate solutions that improve environmental quality or implement sustainable practices, including but not limited to areas lacking desired resources.

6B6F69F263804F66A38FA5AF0ED6EAB4.description: Evaluate and compare the characteristics of two communities and analyze how the diversity, health, and resilience of natural systems impact the quality and health of cultural systems.

61A9EABF802441AE87953118211D7B68.description: Evaluate the impacts on health and quality of natural systems resulting from resource use at the global level and propose solutions to increase system resiliency.

3AC181F5C8BA4B5C9B4C813F5B5A12D4.description: Analyze and weigh relevance of sources through a disciplinary lens to determine how the author, context, audience, and purpose affect the reliability, limitations, and usefulness of a source.

F5B5E910E2034EF4ADC635AE0F746C9F.description: Compare parallel historical and contemporary sustainability issues and articulate the perspectives, including unstated, absent, under-represented groups and future generations, critique the balance of stakeholder interests in the outcome, and propose alternative solutions.

3D37001F9DC245C4A190FBEB8AD96426.description: Students assess how diversity influences health and resilience of natural and cultural systems.

FC8A7BE13A614156AEBAF32935DD4BEB.description: Design a solution for a natural resource scarcity issue using available resources in a different way or developing a new resource, and analyze intended and unintended consequences on sustainability in natural and cultural systems

666DF4050D24428FA290F4A0C01B4529.description: Assess the roles of individuals, government, and special interest groups in setting policies at the local, state, tribal, national, and international level; analyze the cultural and environmental dimensions of the policy; and propose a strategy to address concerns related to the policy.

E8B02C196090466F8713B20B8FDB7055.description: Compare and contrast the competitive, predatory, and mutually beneficial interactions between different species and ecosystems and evaluate the impacts of each on the system.

DE36D5F6D39343278E5868027174A852.description: Identify and analyze limitations in our understanding of systems and the outcomes.

AC19870407E54F9C8F48E876A9F5CF38.description: Examine nested systems within identified relationships and sub-perspectives of individual and group perspectives.

63EAC3DE432E492387EEE0B77A0BAD45.description: Recommend alternative models of systems to address different perspectives, define new boundaries, and achieve new outcomes.

67D121F6C9414D4EBEC2E50E82104780.description: Students evaluate relationships and structures of natural and cultural systems and analyze their interdependence.

7DCA00A27B4B45F084D29B72C205E017.description: Design and implement a home, school, or community wellness improvement plan that integrates the outdoors to develop mindfulness, confidence, and self-regulation; evaluate the outcomes, and communicate the results.

18F5FE890C0745188C0BD113E3A6B4BE.description: Analyze the effects of environment and time outdoors on mental, socio-emotional, and physical health.

69DB3F3D4D5946B99C3BF88F5504620F.description: Reflect and share how one's perspectives influence personal curiosity, the pursuit of knowledge, and respect for others and the environment.

0FFD9719CCB84F6F95D782FC5B64EE1B.description: Investigate and analyze one's own curiosities about patterns that emerge from outdoor exploration to develop new questions, draw conclusions, or formulate new ideas or solutions.

00AE93B67B1E4AE69E39E09446602FD9.description: Analyze relationships between parts of local and global natural and cultural systems. Compare and contrast historical and current resource use, and analyze the effects on local, regional, and global natural and cultural systems.

39006927623B48A88EC0042385ADE5C0.description: Evaluate personal mental models of well-being, equity, social and environmental welfare, economic health, and concern for living beings.

BA6CDA8107464BEDBC3FDA945DE096DF.description: Students develop and connect with their sense of place and well-being through observation, exploration, and questioning .

document.title: Wisconsin Standards for Mathematics

3DD4F7B4CA1148EB95057BDE48A301B7.description: Compose simple shapes to form larger shapes.

19DB02D380AF4E859F8F1047BEE3262E.description: Model shapes in the world by building shapes from components (e.g., sticks and clay balls) and drawing shapes.

CC63C9B870524993B10DBFA39ABEF2F9.description: Analyze and compare two- and three-dimensional shapes, in different sizes and orientations, using informal language to describe their similarities, differences, parts (e.g., number of sides and vertices/"corners") and other attributes (e.g., having sides of equal length).

3248CA10DB6B4ADEAC3AE3000ED8173C.description: Analyze, compare, create, and compose shapes.

8628940620E4486DBD9A26A9E17BD0A3.description: Identify shapes as two-dimensional (lying in a plane, "flat") or three-dimensional ("solid").

54A03A528FE6400B8DF9EC2F843034F1.description: Correctly name shapes regardless of their orientations or overall size.

DC3E84118143461B9898DF1B66B537FD.description: Describe objects in the environment using names of shapes, and describe the relative positions of these objects using terms such as above, below, beside, in front of, behind, and next to.

87BB424A5E3B46D5BA6A8545A957C3B8.description: Identify and describe shapes (squares, circles, triangles, rectangles, hexagons, cubes, cones, cylinders, and spheres).

69D7D4C78E3848C7BAB297B8C959743E.description: Classify objects into given categories; count the numbers of objects in each category and sort the categories by count. Limit category counts to be less than or equal to 10.

E019CD5EE8524400933E7190427B484E.description: Classify objects and count the number of objects in each category.

EF4E9B8E5B79462C980D1261EDB2D255.description: Directly compare two objects with a measurable attribute in common, to see which object has "more of"/"less of" the attribute, and describe the difference.

287F4A440D814527AE713BC70E0C94AD.description: Describe measurable attributes of objects, such as length or weight. Describe several measurable attributes of a single object.

E91C80DE951340A590DCDB0263F6FC7E.description: Compose and decompose numbers from 11 to 19 into ten ones and some further ones, e.g., by using objects or drawings, and record each composition or decomposition by a drawing or numbers; understand that these numbers are composed of ten ones and one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine ones.

E61AC1A604E54544BF86F8FCC886D2EF.description: Work with numbers 11-19 to gain foundations for place value.

A04A1A8C7D3D432AB13AA5C85858F47F.description: Number and Operations in Base Ten

20257879421F45CB92F6B2A9C9CE7CF0.description: Flexibly and efficiently add and subtract within 5 using mental images and composing/decomposing numbers up to 5.

298DDE3E17CB4FBFA2E3C0C70FDC76EC.description: For any number from 1 to 9, find the number that makes 10 when added to the given number, e.g., by using objects or drawings, and record the answer with a drawing or numbers.

62C76BFB40A44DFFBA96F9120C5651EE.description: Quickly name the quantity of objects briefly shown in structured arrangements anchored to 5 (e.g., fingers, ten frames, math rack/rekenrek) with totals up to 10 without counting by recognizing the arrangement or seeing the quantity in subgroups that are combined (conceptual subitizing).

729E324E20084FFC90DE9FEB376DE73C.description: Decompose numbers less than or equal to 10 into pairs in more than one way, e.g., by using objects or drawings, and record each decomposition with drawings or numbers.

03ED1E972A2F487C8B66EDE1C7A442AC.description: Solve addition and subtraction word problems, and add and subtract within 10, e.g., by using objects or drawings to represent the problem.

397A54E6CD79443B94F92738866305D5.description: Represent addition and subtraction with objects, fingers, mental images, drawings, sounds (e.g., claps), acting out situations, verbal explanations, or numbers. Drawings need not show details, but should show the mathematics in the problem.

13205ACCED01450FBE48EB81AF8C8FE7.description: Understand addition as putting together and adding to, and understand subtraction as taking apart and taking from.

4A130CE620F54EBC9875B568B84638C2.description: Compare two numbers between 1 and 10 presented as written numerals using student generated ways to record the comparison.

49A526ED9D4D4BFE96CEA3AF82F4DAB8.description: Identify whether the number of objects (up to 10) in one group is greater than, less than, or equal to the number of objects in another group, e.g., by using matching and counting strategies.

18A4A133A1974E37802C62F8E777DFFA.description: Count to answer "how many?" questions about as many as 20 things arranged in a line, a rectangular array, or a circle, or as many as 10 things in a scattered configuration; given a number from 1-20, count out that many objects.

05B5BEC7A3AF401DA0555EF6D2E3FB43.description: Quickly recognize and name the quantity of up to 5 objects briefly shown in structured or unstructured arrangements without counting (perceptual subitizing).

F4C9DD7573884B4795F73BF43DC1E15D.description: Understand that each successive number name refers to a quantity that is one larger and the previous number is one smaller (hierarchical inclusion).

8AB675595022470B940D4711B13E412A.description: Understand that the last number name said tells the number of objects counted (cardinality). The number of objects is the same regardless of their arrangement or the order in which they were counted (number conservation).

CD89A8E0931641B5A9DD30A8B681D8C3.description: When counting objects, say the number names in the standard order, pairing each object with one and only one number name and each number name with one and only one object (one to one correspondence).

A20CD0B0F29B40F7BE563FBBFB4E43E6.description: Understand the relationship between numbers and quantities; connect counting to cardinality.

61B85F875F8A436282940392077BABC1.description: Write numbers from 0 to 20. Represent a number of objects with a written numeral 0-20 (with 0 representing a count of no objects).

82987FD52F4B483E92F86BFF32331747.description: Count forward beginning from a given number within the known sequence (instead of having to begin at 1).

F0C4212645EF444D98A67E87147328ED.description: Count to 100 by ones and by tens.

02850EFE70EF42C7A6B6B8E9EF69E708.description: Know number names and the count sequence.

CC6CD9BB9BA04AE780AD89CF936ED255.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

5303571C0CFB490DB2590F1407B4C864.description: Look for and make use of structure.

7A85A0C710224989AED1E870A1CE90DE.description: Construct viable arguments, and appreciate and critique the reasoning of others.

DA03A22FABA540139B887995332C800D.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

document.title: Wisconsin Standards for Mathematics

09851E3E49EB473F8D54953C53A5ADA2.description: Partition circles and rectangles into two and four equal shares, describe and count the shares using the words halves and fourths, and use the phrases half of and fourth of the whole. Describe the whole as being two of the shares, or four of the shares. Understand for these examples that decomposing into more equal shares creates smaller shares.

C3DABB6BCE384504A3F371AE1D539FE9.description: Compose two-dimensional shapes (rectangles, squares, trapezoids, triangles, half-circles, and quarter-circles) or three-dimensional shapes (cubes, right rectangular prisms, right circular cones, and right circular cylinders) to create a composite shape, and compose new shapes from the composite shape. Student use of formal names such as "right rectangular prism" is not expected.

3E55EFA4ECA14468A72D14E5CF614E51.description: Distinguish between defining attributes (e.g., triangles are closed and three-sided) versus non-defining attributes (e.g., color, orientation, overall size); build and draw shapes to possess defining attributes.

BD544DE95A0048129D7E5E9B076141E3.description: Reason with shapes and their attributes.

75BF597F93034003902E0406D3A72A72.description: Organize, represent, and interpret data with up to three categories; ask and answer questions about the total number of data points, how many in each category, and how many more or less are in one category than in another.

21F3FDCFD0AB46CA98A551371708A22D.description: Tell and write time in hours and half-hours using analog and digital clocks.

611894A01200456EAA0E9A85F0E76B29.description: Express the length of an object as a whole number of length units, by laying multiple copies of a shorter object (the length unit) end to end; understand that the length measurement of an object is the number of same-size length units that span it with no gaps or overlaps.

BC87073B7BAE4DD28B7C83AB572C6FE8.description: Order three objects by length; compare the lengths of two objects indirectly by using a third object.

645DB14623394692BA4418806A562686.description: Measure lengths indirectly and by iterating length units.

E7CF2D21D5E644279C98E616092E327B.description: Subtract multiples of 10 in the range 10-90 from multiples of 10 in the range 10-90 (positive or zero differences), using concrete models or drawings and strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction; relate the strategy to a written method and explain the reasoning used.

D0374A72617647E3BAC11831DEEBB760.description: Given a two-digit number, mentally find 10 more or 10 less than the number, without having to count; explain the reasoning used.

40F70E2107574B19A13998DF69ECDE8A.description: Add within 100, including adding a two-digit number and a one-digit number, and adding a two-digit number and a multiple of 10, using concrete models or drawings and strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction; relate the strategy to a written method and explain the reasoning used. Understand that in adding two-digit numbers, one adds tens and tens, ones and ones; and sometimes it is necessary to compose a ten.

5D4CBB68CA6B41AF8AC23A8D375CBC57.description: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to add and subtract.

A673995EF6384885836D128F1425F3D9.description: Compare two two-digit numbers based on meanings of the tens and ones digits and describe the result of the comparison using words and symbols ( >, =, and < ).

A174F2A5343E4470B9ACD8A1FB7F11AB.description: The numbers 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90 refer to one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine tens (and 0 ones).

2166B4D3CA704B1EB0006C4DEAD7925A.description: The numbers from 11 to 19 are composed of a ten and one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine ones.

F352040BE8824CA18BBB72F8648803E7.description: 10 can be thought of as a bundle of ten ones -- called a "ten".

7A5BE26A2A8241E8B42CA7D0C55BEA05.description: Understand that the two digits of a two-digit number represent amounts of tens and ones. Understand the following as special cases:

2BFAED518C004EAAB868EA435C405C34.description: Count to 120, starting at any number less than 120. In this range, read and write numerals and represent a number of objects with a written numeral.

2168F656CD194355B9407CBA43742802.description: Number and Operations in Base Ten

82A184B04A654B908092C80E0C8CF49C.description: Understand the meaning of the equal sign as "has the same value/amount as" and determine if equations involving addition and subtraction are true or false.

5467B4A5AAA148E7BD3CEE4660AD02A9.description: Work with addition and subtraction equations.

C01A9FB89656453A9619A77E97A5FA68.description: Add and subtract within 20 using objects, drawings or equations. Use multiple strategies that may include counting on; making a ten (e.g., 8 + 6 = 8 + 2 + 4 = 10 + 4 = 14) ; decomposing a number leading to a ten (e.g., 13 - 4 = 13 - 3 - 1 = 10 - 1 = 9); using the relationship between addition and subtraction (e.g., knowing that 8 + 4 = 12, one knows 12 - 8 = 4); and creating equivalent but easier or known sums (e.g., adding 6 + 7 by creating the known equivalent 6 + 6 + 1 = 12 + 1 = 13).

BFAB6B5FDECD4569A3802D051C031AB8.description: Flexibly and efficiently add and subtract within 10 using strategies that may include mental images and composing/decomposing up to 10.

F5EA1BD283A34149984FB34CD2026C12.description: Use multiple strategies to add and subtract within 20.

4DD91C87F42A43BA946121E7725A4648.description: Use conceptual subitizing in unstructured arrangements with totals up to 10 and structured arrangements anchored to 5 or 10 (e.g., 10 frames, double ten frames, math rack/rekenrek) with totals up to 20 to relate the compositions and decompositions to addition and subtraction.

37B0E1B007594828805E00486F7C0DE0.description: Relate counting to addition and subtraction (e.g., by counting on 2 to add 2).

957EA751996145A0923EAF8962C290BA.description: Use counting and subitizing strategies to explain addition and subtraction.

B1FD7A97E0154071B5FDCF82DA6169DF.description: Understand subtraction as an unknown-addend problem.

97A3F27AA02B4D41827F7D00F83E7572.description: Apply properties of operations as strategies to add and subtract.

ABA939DF546E48F3A0824DE8575EB187.description: Understand and apply properties of operations and the relationship between addition and subtraction.

9CDB939FBDCB4261B88F940D76EFC2DC.description: Solve word problems that call for addition of three whole numbers whose sum is less than or equal to 20, e.g., by using objects, drawings, and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.

06E3BCBAD1F74977991AD644EAC66E4D.description: Use addition and subtraction within 20 to solve word problems involving situations of adding to, taking from, putting together, taking apart, and comparing, with unknowns in all positions, e.g., by using objects, drawings, and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.

E7C6CA99ACD34DF3ABED79914365C7BB.description: Represent and solve problems involving addition and subtraction.

7956CB226BC84E34978DC042A98E3808.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

A60BC8A4D53A4942B82432F47CE39471.description: Look for and make use of structure.

48E977D704794BB79061D1FE6A7C4A22.description: Construct viable arguments, and appreciate and critique the reasoning of others.

0890DD3C6E3643538A149FFE43B7171F.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

document.title: Wisconsin Standards for Mathematics

8431260419E9449491ED60FE287D969E.description: Compare two fractions with the same numerator or the same denominator by reasoning about their size. Recognize that comparisons are valid only when the two fractions refer to the same whole. Justify the conclusions by using a visual fraction model (e.g., tape diagram or number line) and describe the result of the comparison using words and symbols ( >, =, and < ).

82C70D022FBA42449A327D13353245D3.description: Express whole numbers as fractions (3 = 3/1), and recognize fractions that are equivalent to whole numbers (4/4 = 1).

BB666E874AD54719B02F3D5EA09BBD32.description: Recognize and generate simple equivalent fractions, e.g., ½ = 2/4, 4/6 = 2/3) and explain why the fractions are equivalent by using a visual fraction model (e.g., tape diagram or number line).

999A1E2FF53C46E39F7F2B2EEA135E39.description: Understand two fractions as equivalent (equal) if they are the same size or name the same point on a number line.

4C369865B1534EAEB0CE5C5682A1F981.description: Explain equivalence of fractions and compare fractions by reasoning about their size.

A8F535A132434B6A8957E9EF5925A6D5.description: Represent fractions on a number line by iterating lengths of the unit fraction from 0. Recognize that the resulting interval represents the size of the fraction and that its endpoint locates the fraction as a number on the number line.

C7DD0938DEFA4E7C9E3632D5FCBA4BF4.description: Understand the whole on a number line is defined as the interval from 0 to 1 and the unit fraction is defined by partitioning the interval into equal parts (i.e., equal-sized lengths).

359F3077022F4D90AF804285C4B76E01.description: Understand and represent a fraction as a number on the number line.

CB617F0DA4654612814B1766DA54E5C7.description: Understand a unit fraction as the quantity formed when a whole is partitioned into equal parts and explain that a unit fraction is one of those parts (e.g., ¼). Understand fractions are composed of unit fractions, for example, 7/4 is the quantity formed by 7 parts of the size ¼.

567BBD837690446BA108A0FB3FCEB994.description: Develop understanding of fractions as numbers.

2EFE68F9C05A45BBA20A65CD0F310750.description: Partition shapes into parts with equal areas. Express the area of each part as a unit fraction of the whole.

397A11336A7343BCA8DAA29EFE721FDA.description: Understand that shapes in different categories (e.g., rhombuses, rectangles, and others) may share attributes (e.g., having four sides), and that the shared attributes can define a larger category (e.g., quadrilaterals). Recognize rhombuses, rectangles, and squares as examples of quadrilaterals, and draw examples of quadrilaterals that do not belong to any of these subcategories.

C173A8CEE19C4EA9A7481875F96251D0.description: Reason with shapes and their attributes.

9A492C838F9248269DC71DB003C3240A.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving perimeters of polygons, including finding the perimeter given the side lengths, finding an unknown side length, and exhibiting rectangles with the same perimeter and different areas or with the same area and different perimeters.

A0C53E6B2DD9465CACB16A98003AC575.description: Geometric measurement: recognize perimeter as an attribute of plane figures and distinguish between linear and area measures.

EDA9A40F88B34EA18C64EE3548B12401.description: Recognize area as additive. Find areas of rectilinear figures by decomposing them into non-overlapping rectangles and adding the areas of the non-overlapping parts, applying this technique to solve real-world problems.

9E1CE5C35E134B5FA77EB38AE7A7CD05.description: Use tiling to show in a concrete case that the area of a rectangle with whole-number side lengths a and b + c is the sum of a x b and a x c. Use area models to represent the distributive property in mathematical reasoning.

34BB9C9062414F73BC91B05523A7F0DA.description: Multiply side lengths to find areas of rectangles with whole number side lengths in the context of solving real-world and mathematical problems, and represent whole-number products as rectangular areas in mathematical reasoning.

20FA21C1D2CA4B1F86354DFD9E46A672.description: Find the area of a rectangle with whole-number side lengths by tiling it, and show that the area is the same as would be found by multiplying the side lengths.

E8AA569D85234554B319D4C864069389.description: Relate area to the operations of multiplication and addition.

345B567315BF4C70BD7B396254049D52.description: Measure areas by counting unit squares (square cm, square m, square in, square ft., and improvised units).

400C305564534CCFAB2195ADC1B95C75.description: A plane figure which can be covered without gaps or overlaps by n unit squares is said to have an area of n square units.

BF1F75FB55344E3DB7DC6466FDA8AD27.description: A square with side length 1 unit, called "a unit square" is said to have "one square unit" of area, and can be used to measure area.

7A1A89D1DB4D4C08897AC0B841DE7D67.description: Recognize area as an attribute of plane figures and understand concepts of area measurement.

993BC495A193406296EA0F643AED43C2.description: Geometric measurement: understand concepts of area and relate area to multiplication and to addition.

EFF76432AA3044709156079C09D0369B.description: Generate measurement data by measuring lengths using rulers marked with halves and fourths of an inch. Show the data by making a line plot, where the horizontal scale is marked off in appropriate units -- whole numbers, halves, fourths.

416E173AF8C14621B3C130F74E7D2E08.description: Draw a scaled picture graph and a scaled bar graph to represent a data set with several categories. Solve one- and two-step "how many more" and "how many less" problems using information presented in scaled bar graphs.

C7D4A468E1C6455684AFD28310599360.description: Measure and estimate liquid volumes and masses of objects using standard units of grams (g), kilograms (kg), and liters (l), excluding compound units such as cm3 and finding the geometric volume of a container. Add, subtract, multiply, or divide to solve one-step word problems involving masses or volumes that are given in the same units, e.g., by using drawings (such as a beaker with a measurement scale) to represent the problem.

6D351DEB55E54F2EB8635E852E1A5A09.description: Tell and write time to the nearest minute and measure time intervals in minutes. Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of time intervals in minutes, e.g., by representing the problem on a number line.

BD953F1850E94723BB4AE3CA5FAAAACD.description: Solve problems involving measurement and estimation of intervals of time, liquid volumes, and masses of objects.

C2EF6A8AC0024D3EA90C060C432BD3E1.description: Multiply one-digit whole numbers by multiples of 10 in the range 10-90 (e.g., 9 x 80, 5 x 60) using strategies based on place value and properties of operations.

54774A06033A441BA1AD36A4A7ECD40E.description: Flexibly and efficiently add and subtract within 1,000 using strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction.

077F95AE3DAF4C4CBDA4129E85F74228.description: Use place value understanding to generate estimates for problems in real-world situations, with whole numbers within 1,000, using strategies such as mental math, benchmark numbers, compatible numbers, and rounding. Assess the reasonableness of their estimates (e.g., Is my estimate too low or too high? What degree of precision do I need for this situation?).

CE19CDB0BE6045D188067AA7ACC877D1.description: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to perform multi-digit arithmetic, using a variety of strategies.

0E6B3AB7950F4BC6941E3BD11B60A979.description: Number and Operations in Base Ten

B359F12389F74185BAE2B220A88F82CF.description: Identify arithmetic patterns (including patterns in the addition table or multiplication table), and explain them using properties of operations.

9C31EEAA9A9440D9AB2ACCC69870ADFB.description: Solve two-step word problems, posed with whole numbers and having whole number answers, using the four operations. Represent these problems using one or two equations with a letter standing for the unknown quantity. If one equation is used, grouping symbols (i.e. parentheses) may be needed. Assess the reasonableness of answers using mental computation and estimation strategies.

7293D5470E6E4F4B99B566FA06800533.description: Solve problems involving the four operations, and identify and explain patterns in arithmetic.

47177CC6971D4E1897F88C7E235F40B3.description: Flexibly and efficiently use strategies, the relationship between the operations, and properties of operations to find products and quotients with multiples of 0, 1, 2, 5, & 10 within 100.

14E2C3C9AF2D483EA34B80548A5DDC7B.description: Use the meanings of multiplication and division, the relationship between the operations (e.g., knowing that 8 x 5 = 40, one could reason that 40 ÷ 5 = 8), and properties of operations (e.g., the distributive property) to develop and understand strategies to multiply and divide within 100.

770998DB56C64209B1B0F081808065D9.description: Use multiplicative thinking to multiply and divide within 100.

29EE022521DB4E3CB81FDE48329D8C21.description: Understand division as an unknown-factor problem.

756B2F25D097431EAE1DED10EDF9088B.description: Apply properties of operations as strategies to multiply and divide. Student use of the formal terms for these properties is not necessary.

A99B0F8432C14C6491F3210A567681FB.description: Understand properties of multiplication and the relationship between multiplication and division.

10E18E893F044876853BB49270CA6575.description: Use multiplication and division within 100 to solve word problems in situations involving equal groups, arrays, and measurement quantities, e.g., by using drawings and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.

2801A3E13535482897EF6552F86C106A.description: Interpret whole-number quotients of whole numbers, e.g., interpret 56 ÷ 8 as the number of objects in each share when 56 objects are partitioned equally into 8 shares, or as a number of shares when 56 objects are partitioned into equal shares of 8 objects each.

B32F2DF4306540A790D3315D52477770.description: Interpret products of whole numbers, e.g., interpret 5 x 7 as the total number of objects in 5 groups of 7 objects each.

15C360DA73DE41D98B29F0100B0B1F80.description: Represent and solve problems involving multiplication and division.

D2B74FD9DB0F4245960B4DDF2B07D70C.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

A99032082FC14FC3A2CF72800F440CF0.description: Look for and make use of structure.

80C6C8EC265949E6A2AFB5489B1988EF.description: Construct viable arguments, and appreciate and critique the reasoning of others.

1E2157815E8647D3B39021187EE6B308.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

document.title: Wisconsin Standards for Mathematics

DB3F0F1943534B6CB85614A3AB791248.description: Compare decimals to hundredths by reasoning about their size and using benchmarks. Recognize that comparisons are valid only when the decimals refer to the same whole. Justify the conclusions, by using explanations or visual models (e.g., number line or area model) and describe the result of the comparison using words and symbols ( >, =, and < ).

E9D7B5ADA5B34C5ABF7B09C23A251F4D.description: Use decimal notation for fractions with denominators 10 or 100, connect decimals to real-world contexts, and represent with visual models (e.g., number line or area model).

714FC366B8C847E5A2F06A8D45281810.description: Express a fraction with denominator 10 as an equivalent fraction with denominator 100, and use this technique to add two fractions with respective denominators 10 and 100.

EF2B1F9DA6C64B0386E09C7D4E50F857.description: Understand decimal notation for fractions, and compare decimal fractions.

1DFA3C24F882496BAEA9C7F42C1A3127.description: Solve word problems involving multiplication of a whole number times a fraction by using visual fraction models and equations to represent the problem. Understand a reasonable answer range when multiplying with fractions.

4E644BB6934548F988AC7F4BDE050E45.description: Represent a whole number times a non-unit fraction (e.g., 3 x 2/5) using visual fraction models and understand this as combining equal groups of the non-unit fraction (3 groups of 2/5) and as a collection of unit fractions (6 groups of 1/5), recognizing this product as 6/5.

762196469EAD4C1B80FE6023E6782CC8.description: Understand a fraction as a group of unit fractions or as a multiple of a unit fraction.

F04CD03150C34A77868AF27A366AEF4F.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication to multiply a whole number times a fraction.

678C7783791842E78A51C0FEC47A129F.description: Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions with like and related denominators, including mixed numbers, by using visual fraction models and equations to represent the problem.

A5EAFA723C1A4D02982FD80B300C4D83.description: Add and subtract fractions, including mixed numbers, with like denominators (e.g., 3/8 + 2/8) and related denominators (e.g., ½ + ¼, 1/3 + 1/6) by using visual fraction models (e.g., tape diagrams and number lines), properties of operations, and the relationship between addition and subtraction.

55EE9FD684EC4CFBBF989544125D4DAC.description: Decompose a fraction into a sum of unit fractions and/or multiples of that unit fraction in more than one way, recording each decomposition by an equation. Justify decompositions with explanations, visual fraction models, or equations.

7A9B6C26456A47E482259381F43C145A.description: Understand addition and subtraction of fractions as joining and separating parts referring to the same whole.

3F7D40AADEC644FC8BCB17D587D0249C.description: Build fractions from unit fractions by applying and extending previous understandings of operations on whole numbers.

6655AC09B582411FA79B70DD5225FF6E.description: Compare fractions with different numerators and different denominators while recognizing that comparisons are valid only when the fractions refer to the same whole. Justify the conclusions by using visual fraction models (e.g., tape diagrams and number lines) and by reasoning about the size of the fractions, using benchmark fractions (including whole numbers), or creating common denominators or numerators. Describe the result of the comparison using words and symbols ( >, =, and < ).

434BF78134CD45B2AE389B4A30F552CC.description: Understand and use a general principle to recognize and generate equivalent fractions that name the same amount.

51183DDAC8A648E89B1C311F97527AE8.description: Explain why a fraction is equivalent to another fraction by using visual fraction models (e.g., tape diagrams and number lines), with attention to how the number and the size of the parts differ even though the two fractions themselves are the same size.

BD8701B2D1704FD78628DFED176C5E41.description: Recognize a line of symmetry for a two-dimensional figure as a line across the figure such that the figure can be folded along the line into matching parts. Identify line-symmetric figures and draw lines of symmetry.

FA82D6993A66459481F5479AF7AA9F13.description: Classify two-dimensional figures based on the presence or absence of parallel or perpendicular lines, or the presence or absence of angles of a specified size. Recognize right triangles as a category, and identify right triangles.

0A792A49A05D45F6B9D50F0F78BE02B7.description: Draw points, lines, line segments, rays, angles (right, acute, obtuse), and perpendicular and parallel lines. Identify these in two-dimensional figures.

5B6B53C8B4014C9980BB0659F93B97FD.description: Draw and identify lines and angles, and classify shapes by properties of their lines and angles.

93C4C61D8C6E4E62932D25BAB9310DD7.description: Recognize angle measure as additive. When an angle is decomposed into non-overlapping parts, the angle measure of the whole is the sum of the angle measures of the parts. Solve addition and subtraction problems to find unknown angles on a diagram in real-world and mathematical problems, e.g., by using an equation with a symbol for the unknown angle measure.

8BCF6051327E45C79D50E125A5AA609C.description: Measure angles in whole-number degrees using a protractor. Sketch angles of specified measure.

208C24A916EE41009B761AC63A43AE2B.description: An angle that turns through n one-degree angles is said to have an angle measure of n degrees.

25E975DBCEC54499AC97DBDA6E76D585.description: An angle is measured with reference to a circle with its center at the common endpoint of the rays, by considering the fraction of the circular arc between the points where the two rays intersect the circle. An angle that turns through 1/360 of a circle is called a "one-degree angle" and can be used to measure angles.

A09355F7DD4D4FB196C578AE3293B741.description: Recognize angles as geometric shapes that are formed wherever two rays share a common endpoint, and understand concepts of angle measurement:

7CDA48A0B8D84007B0F9C04D2A2F0EDC.description: Geometric measurement: understand concepts of angle and measure angles.

BF4AD320AC5E4CCBB28629EC6E5885E9.description: Make a line plot to display a data set of measurements in fractions of a unit (½, ¼, 1/8). Solve problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions by using information presented in line plots.

145D3B052AB44196A082EF65FDABF25B.description: Apply the area and perimeter formulas for rectangles in real-world and mathematical problems.

2A6BDA6DD3EB4671A98537B07627A0A3.description: Use the four operations to solve word problems involving distances, intervals of time, liquid volumes, masses of objects, and money, including problems involving simple fractions or decimals, and problems that require expressing measurements given in a larger unit in terms of a smaller unit. Represent measurement quantities using diagrams such as a number line that feature a measurement scale.

53FDFE0F230F4E919F62CBFC47457F3F.description: Know relative sizes of measurement units within one system of units including km, m, cm; kg, g; lb., oz.; l, ml; hr., min., sec. Within a single system of measurement, express measurements in a larger unit in terms of a smaller unit. Record measurement equivalents in a two-column table.

E7481E40A4C04F3091AA741748BA6ACF.description: Solve problems involving measurement and conversion of measurements from a larger unit to a smaller unit.

91268FF9CB25400F9CFA893ADBA36E7D.description: Find whole-number quotients and remainders with up to four-digit dividends and one-digit divisors, using strategies based on place value, the properties of operations, and/or the relationship between multiplication and division. Illustrate and explain the calculation by using equations, rectangular arrays, and/or area models.

A18DC2BB1DB44331ABCEE36FEA879AC8.description: Multiply a whole number of up to four digits by a one-digit whole number, and multiply two two-digit numbers, using strategies based on place value and the properties of operations. Illustrate and explain the calculation by using equations, rectangular arrays, and/or area models.

11F5AF4FE8A34049A37CB4AA9398CA31.description: Flexibly and efficiently add and subtract multi-digit whole numbers using strategies or algorithms based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction.

9941986FEDB54556960223B5DD3982BA.description: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to perform multi-digit arithmetic.

DBC45EE0061941F5AE1D70B569707527.description: Use place value understanding to generate estimates for real-world problem situations, with multi-digit whole numbers, using strategies such as mental math, benchmark numbers, compatible numbers, and rounding. Assess the reasonableness of their estimates. (e.g., Is my estimate too low or too high? What degree of precision do I need for this situation?)

8FC4305697194C1F8FAEE3CBF437D9C6.description: Read and write multi-digit whole numbers using base-ten numerals, number names, and expanded form. Compare two multi-digit numbers based on meanings of the digits in each place and describe the result of the comparison using words and symbols ( >, =, and < ).

732015E0E3084749BCC4839CFEE60ED0.description: Recognize that in a multi-digit whole number, a digit in one place represents ten times what it represents in the place to its right.

235C3F016E88400799BC3D848A43155E.description: Generalize place value understanding for multi-digit whole numbers.

433916E8EA43437A82E6CBE41A70DC6C.description: Number and Operations in Base Ten

42C1278E29004BC192E387C0436235C2.description: Flexibly and efficiently multiply and divide within 100, using strategies such as the relationship between multiplication and division (e.g., knowing that 8 x 5 = 40, one knows 40 ÷ 5 = 8) or properties of operations [e.g., knowing that 7 x 6 can be thought of as 7 groups of 6 so one could think 5 groups of 6 is 30 and 2 more groups of 6 is 12 and 30 + 12 = 42 (informal use of the distributive property)].

BDC167EB8A354E8A8FD0E4FA7BB756BC.description: Generate a number or shape pattern that follows a given rule. Identify apparent features of the pattern that were not explicit in the rule itself.

30322BA0428646B98F0E8DB2398F75FD.description: Find all factor pairs for a whole number in the range 1-100. Recognize that a whole number is a multiple of each of its factors. Determine whether a given whole number in the range 1-100 is a multiple of a given one-digit number. Determine whether a given whole number in the range 1-100 is prime or composite.

6AFACAECBDD6412C94025A62847878B6.description: Gain familiarity with factors and multiples.

6989A5DF957F4CBBA9B2E3B47410F62B.description: Solve multi-step word problems posed with whole numbers and having whole-number answers using the four operations, including problems in which remainders must be interpreted. Represent these problems using equations with a letter standing for the unknown quantity. Assess the reasonableness of answers using mental computation and estimation strategies.

55067028805643E28489589A92AA87E0.description: Multiply or divide to solve word problems involving multiplicative comparison, e.g., by using drawings and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem, distinguishing multiplicative comparison from additive comparison.

67FAEE0D73114BF09FCCB97A6B57DDFE.description: Interpret a multiplication equation as a multiplicative comparison, e.g., interpret 35 = 5 x 7 as a statement that 35 is 5 times as many as 7 and 7 times as many as 5. Represent verbal statements of multiplicative comparisons as multiplication equations.

F5CFF79D5D2749FAA4B46572A1775971.description: Use the four operations with whole numbers to solve problems.

E7520060F41F4CE9A642335C99C9D3FE.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

B20FE8DFAD4A430A9FA118A404A52C9D.description: Look for and make use of structure.

0BB5D619AD92429AAD00B1957D29FE5F.description: Construct viable arguments, and appreciate and critique the reasoning of others.

CCA46CD9F50440A0AA1F3B8855B597D8.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

document.title: Wisconsin Standards for Mathematics

5B8605ACBBA9499295A0B457A8DC9F43.description: Solve real-world problems involving division of unit fractions by non-zero whole numbers and division of whole numbers by unit fractions by using visual fraction models and equations to represent the problem.

41A050BBA2BB42BF909D3995EAEB9209.description: Interpret and represent division of a whole number by a unit fraction as a measurement division situation.

5E64FFDC05504CFAAD9F520DABFE04BF.description: Interpret and represent division of a unit fraction by a non-zero whole number as an equal sharing division situation.

F02513A35A7A4D439BC85A835FEA1954.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of division to divide unit fractions by whole numbers (e.g., 1/3 ÷ 4) and whole numbers by unit fractions (e.g., 4 ÷ 1/5). Students able to multiply fractions can develop strategies to divide fractions by reasoning about the relationship between multiplication and division. But division of a fraction by a fraction is not a requirement at this grade.

8B9B56551BEC4465816EABD22524D141.description: Solve real-world problems involving multiplication of fractions and mixed numbers by using visual fraction models (e.g., tape diagrams, area models, or number lines) and equations to represent the problem. Use benchmark fractions and number sense of fractions to estimate mentally and assess the reasonableness of answers.

47B5EA251C0643A5AFE086683F6DBF1C.description: Relate the principle of fraction equivalence to the effect of multiplying or dividing a fraction by 1 or an equivalent form of 1 (e.g., 3/3, 5/5).

958030C1F04B4B82A5D0FD2C692513E2.description: Explain why multiplying a given number by a fraction greater than 1 results in a product greater than the given number and explain why multiplying a given number by a fraction less than 1 results in a product smaller than the given number.

CA03D3256BE64BF19BFFC81ABE8C6FDC.description: Interpret multiplication as scaling (resizing) by estimating whether a product will be larger or smaller than a given factor on the basis of the size of the other factor, without performing the indicated multiplication.

FC8654AF39FB4A368EFEABB02A612E0F.description: Find the area of a rectangle with fractional side lengths by tiling it with unit squares of the appropriate unit fraction side lengths, and show that the area is the same as would be found by multiplying the side lengths. Multiply fractional side lengths to find areas of rectangles, and represent fraction products as rectangular areas.

765D7E5188E14E829C70B7821BCD2D78.description: Represent word problems involving multiplication of fractions using visual models to develop flexible and efficient strategies.

30F9943ACD144FBB807FD97BD015684B.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication to multiply a fraction times a whole number (e.g., 2/3 x 4) or a fraction times a fraction (e.g., 2/3 x 4/5), including mixed numbers.

CF9D5CFE790748ECA68545B19E792A33.description: Interpret a fraction as an equal sharing division situation, where a quantity (the numerator) is divided into equal parts (the denominator). Solve word problems involving division of whole numbers leading to answers in the form of fractions or mixed numbers, by using visual fraction models (e.g., tape diagrams or area models) or equations to represent the problem.
