D68D0010D90A43C7AB5DEAAACB76204F.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication and division to multiply and divide fractions.

C77F37D696724F1A9E564FBB5FE7A4CC.description: Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions referring to the same whole using visual fraction models or equations to represent the problem. Use benchmark fractions and number sense of fractions to estimate mentally and assess the reasonableness of answers.

CBBA36DFC5774437AEDBE2AFB7DA5AA0.description: Add and subtract fractions and mixed numbers using flexible and efficient strategies, including renaming fractions with equivalent fractions. Justify using visual models (e.g., tape diagrams or number lines) and equations.

D1FCF36668CE48248C72225CD8F5F7E2.description: Use equivalent fractions as a strategy to add and subtract fractions.

3CA1B6C78109485292138F318D131270.description: Classify two-dimensional figures in a hierarchy based on properties.

9B5111F184AD4434A2CC5FE191F78540.description: Understand that attributes belonging to a category of two-dimensional figures also belong to all subcategories of that category.

55EADB4203F6413881E002A26EE47875.description: Classify two-dimensional figures into categories based on their properties.

F51BDE3A7371481B95A17094628BF406.description: Represent real-world and mathematical problems by graphing points in the first quadrant of the coordinate plane, and interpret coordinate values of points in the context of the situation.

C7D055E3EBAE419588159EF4B4A209D9.description: Use a pair of perpendicular number lines, called axes, to define a coordinate system, with the intersection of the lines (the origin) arranged to coincide with the 0 on each line and a given point in the plane located by using an ordered pair of numbers, called its coordinates. Understand that the first number indicates how far to travel from the origin in the direction of one axis, and the second number indicates how far to travel in the direction of the second axis, with the convention that the names of the two axes and the coordinates correspond (e.g., x-axis and x-coordinate, y-axis and y-coordinate).

352405CDF2424F2E927973AF8D5924B8.description: Graph points on the coordinate plane to solve real-world and mathematical problems.

502C681F143F4121B14D3673AA9D9F72.description: Recognize volume as additive. Find volumes of solid figures composed of two non-overlapping right rectangular prisms by adding the volumes of the non-overlapping parts, applying this technique to solve real-world problems.

3361E17410CF42AB87A604E03A70FAC1.description: Apply the formulas V = l x w x h and V = B x h for rectangular prisms to find volumes of right rectangular prisms with whole number edge lengths in the context of solving real-world and mathematical problems.

0152B60877EA4E0D98CD8CB6C7535A03.description: Find the volume of a right rectangular prism with whole-number side lengths by packing it with unit cubes, and show that the volume is the same as would be found by multiplying the edge lengths, equivalently by multiplying the height by the area of the base. Represent threefold whole-number products as volumes, e.g., to represent the associative property of multiplication.

EB4EF92FA5E1452C95A2EE1956C55E6B.description: Relate volume to the operations of multiplication and addition and solve real-world and mathematical problems involving volume.

4D4A28C5F1074E51B91FF93A182720A1.description: Measure volumes by counting unit cubes, using cubic cm, cubic in., cubic ft., and improvised units.

26AB7D118CB94A12B9D228995143EB3A.description: A solid figure which can be packed without gaps or overlaps using n unit cubes is said to have a volume of n cubic units.

CD8D56F9E8EC479D95C62114BE00ACD4.description: A cube with side length 1 unit, called a "unit cube", is said to have "one cubic unit" of volume, and can be used to measure volume.

890D2F53403C40D0A02AC76C0DA1F094.description: Recognize volume as an attribute of solid figures and understand concepts of volume measurement.

0419409C83684BEF9A04ECDB39FA8DB0.description: Geometric measurement: understand concepts of volume and relate volume to multiplication and to addition.

0F56CE2D912E40138ADFA8C0B49F7089.description: Make a line plot to display a data set of measurements in fractions of a unit (1/2, 1/4, 1/8). Use operations on fractions for this grade to solve problems involving information presented in line plots.

54AE38790E394DC3A7732A51BC1E76E0.description: Convert among different-sized standard measurement units within a given measurement system (e.g., convert 5 cm to 0.05 m), and use these conversions in solving multi-step, real-world problems.

6C90E263F8D04607A891F2A29CCA00AA.description: Convert like measurement units within a given measurement system.

3383A422C91A403E910C3AEF71F4B352.description: Add, subtract, multiply, and divide decimals to hundredths, using concrete models or drawings and strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction; relate the strategy to a written method and explain the reasoning used.

1B94B5428A314AFBA64DC461922B8EB4.description: Find whole-number quotients of whole numbers with up to four-digit dividends and two-digit divisors, using strategies based on place value, the properties of operations, and/or the relationship between multiplication and division. Illustrate and explain the calculation by using equations, rectangular arrays, and/or area models.

5E30C4D011364AFA81B731D8E31FE8CA.description: Flexibly and efficiently multiply multi-digit whole numbers using strategies or algorithms based on place value, area models, and the properties of operations.

4CC88991ACD64A05A65EFD67D87F79E0.description: Perform operations with multi-digit whole numbers and with decimals to hundredths.

A79A51449EAF4A329C9279DD460CE8C5.description: Use place value understanding to generate estimates for problems in real-world situations, with decimals, using strategies such as mental math, benchmark numbers, compatible numbers, and rounding. Assess the reasonableness of their estimates (e.g. Is my estimate too low or too high? What degree of precision do I need for this situation?

7377D783EC5F42D49CACC1DE7F9F5912.description: Compare decimals to thousandths based on meanings of the digits in each place and describe the result of the comparison using words and symbols ( >, =, and < ).

B6228DDDD27F4941B01C1A4183D6D6C1.description: Read and write decimals to thousandths using base-ten numerals, number names, and expanded form, e.g., 347.392 = 3 x 100 + 4 x 10 + 7 x 1 + 3 x (1/10) + 9 x (1/100) + 2 x (1/1000).

70E7CA1A5C4A428E9CEBF2C0FC675D96.description: Read, write, and compare decimals to thousandths.

D85E4F6F4A5247A2938E3E1702F9CA90.description: Explain patterns in the number of zeros of the product when multiplying a number by powers of 10, and explain patterns in the placement of the decimal point when a decimal is multiplied or divided by a power of 10. Use whole-number exponents to denote powers of 10.

DBE89289312D4FBABEC590F96C777D19.description: Recognize that in a multi-digit number, a digit in one place represents 10 times as much as it represents in the place to its right and 1/10 of what it represents in the place to its left.

D851A52E14764F41B2243C08C3888FCF.description: Number and Operations in Base Ten

0DFB3135539C4F5D9547FE4A6DB41E2B.description: Generate two numerical patterns using two given rules. Identify apparent relationships between corresponding terms. Form ordered pairs consisting of corresponding terms from the two patterns, and graph the ordered pairs on a coordinate plane.

DA62D8BCBA0B403EB9CB13BF6B1D4372.description: Write simple expressions that record calculations with numbers, and interpret numerical expressions without evaluating them.

AD0A7838A5E5476A9073487F235A3B90.description: Use parentheses, brackets, or braces in numerical expressions, and evaluate expressions with these symbols.

9A105BFA72CB4C3BAC0377D69AAAD124.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

666A284771084077ACCC13E09B5875FB.description: Look for and make use of structure.

8B940EB8C2474E5A9CA41D8EA41DD170.description: Construct viable arguments, and appreciate and critique the reasoning of others.

D0553F421BBC479BA71B8A6FAFE7804E.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

document.title: Wisconsin Standards for Mathematics

1F465429E9074644BBB2AC8E819B9196.description: Relating the choice of measures of center and variability to the shape of the data distribution and the context in which the data were gathered.

DFD9B51EE8C04837B05CC8DDA05521D2.description: Describing any overall pattern and any striking deviations from the overall pattern with reference to the context in which the data were gathered and the quantitative measures of center (median and/or mean) and variability (interquartile range and/or mean absolute deviation) were given.

FC6B3CB264B2448EAB4D92378CE1946E.description: Describing the nature of the attribute under investigation, including how it was measured and its units of measurement.

87E4EFD5A88647A8BBD34590ADA154EC.description: Summarize numerical data sets in relation to their context, such as by:

1AF31716C7E54D3484F6A98AA967F7EB.description: Display numerical data in plots on a number line, including dot plots, histograms, and box plots.

12C3C16C3505458ABC9A314AA5EC7DA7.description: Recognize that a measure of center for a numerical data set summarizes all of its values with a single number, while a measure of variation describes how its values vary with a single number.

C662D49565414359A779610594BB3820.description: Understand that a set of data collected to answer a statistical question has a distribution which can be described by its center, spread, and overall shape.

23026123BFD84DE1A66B80046012FF87.description: Recognize a statistical question as one that anticipates variability in the data related to the question and accounts for it in the answers.

26C81D9AFC2248149A306B5AE20029AA.description: Use variables to represent two quantities in a real-world problem that change in relationship to one another; write an equation to express one quantity, thought of as the dependent variable, in terms of the other quantity, thought of as the independent variable. Analyze the relationship between the dependent and independent variables using graphs and tables, and relate these to the equation.

30BF7BA0FE184C08A83654F8B9307416.description: Represent and analyze quantitative relationships between dependent and independent variables.

4EEEE94D78C84323BF9A5CEDDBC15C00.description: Write an inequality of the form x > c or x < c to represent a constraint or condition in a real-world or mathematical problem. Recognize that inequalities of the form x > c or x < c have infinitely many solutions; represent solutions of such inequalities on number line diagrams.

3AB488A725EC4B98BBF989DAF4B04440.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems by writing and solving equations of the form x + p = q and px = q for cases in which p, q and x are all nonnegative rational numbers.

4B33767E54064444A40AB2E2480D4B77.description: Use variables to represent numbers and write expressions when solving a real-world or mathematical problem; understand that a variable can represent an unknown number, or, depending on the purpose at hand, any number in a specified set.

6DBE838222A446B18DF01C626F0212C8.description: Understand solving an equation or inequality as a process of answering a question: which values from a specified set, if any, make the equation or inequality true? Use substitution to determine whether a given number in a specified set makes an equation or inequality true.

7FE001BB683448D88785E2F63062EE79.description: Reason about and solve one-variable equations and inequalities.

1DF3B509DC6B4F6EBE34D83CDA4A6C6E.description: Identify when two expressions are equivalent (e.g., when the two expressions name the same number regardless of which value is substituted into them).

13F17694C1574093946E3A31EEB0DCC3.description: Apply the properties of operations to generate equivalent expressions.

A8A184BE9B634C1896B9E8CBC86B6209.description: Evaluate expressions at specific values of their variables. Include expressions that arise from formulas used in real-world problems. Perform arithmetic operations, including those involving whole number exponents, in the conventional order when there are no parentheses to specify a particular order (Order of Operations).

2E45B70CE96443368A67AEC3C5490D48.description: Identify parts of an expression using mathematical terms (sum, term, product, factor, quotient, coefficient); view one or more parts of an expression as a single entity.

491563E51E3A434EA3B5542653770F89.description: Write expressions that record operations with numbers and with letters standing for numbers.

9033FAAEC27D4C478F9789BBECBF765F.description: Write, read, and evaluate expressions in which letters stand for numbers.

E3251E43F45B49BE8EE992952DAD73CC.description: Write and evaluate numerical expressions involving whole-number exponents.

EF0DA4A111524139A752B051DF4A8A55.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of arithmetic to algebraic expressions.

5B9F94B3255D423A839B9F0C58CC2BAE.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems by graphing points in all four quadrants of the coordinate plane. Include use of coordinates and absolute value to find distances between points with the same first coordinate or the same second coordinate.

2E2D6AE4EFD64FEC8EB2D07295AE9BAE.description: Distinguish comparisons of absolute value from statements about order.

E4189E5C537E4DCA9869E42F8C0BB0D6.description: Understand the absolute value of a rational number as its distance from 0 on the number line; interpret absolute value as magnitude for a positive or negative quantity in a real-world situation.

13A6AE4DD4C64FA1A40FD1D86EDB589C.description: Write, interpret, and explain statements of order for rational numbers in real-world contexts.

3A2E7E06C1CC48EEB13119AF7F64F80C.description: Interpret statements of inequality as statements about the relative position of two numbers on a number line.

2F67362297FF471C9B77B86BF9C42161.description: Understand ordering and absolute value of rational numbers.

27495A66B34D4D8B81598BFAA017DC95.description: Find and position integers and other rational numbers on a horizontal or vertical number line; find and position pairs of integers and other rational numbers on a coordinate plane.

DEB04C03D8854D268A0FD55C67A97F33.description: Understand signs of numbers in ordered pairs as indicating locations in quadrants of the coordinate plane; recognize that when two ordered pairs differ only by signs, the locations of the points are related by reflections across one or both axes.

F85297410FA649128064C3C2A98BAA6D.description: Recognize opposite signs of numbers as indicating locations on opposite sides of 0 on the number line; recognize that the opposite of the opposite of a number is the number itself, e.g., -(-3) = 3, and that 0 is its own opposite.

6853F582D60A462C8B8D4C6123688E81.description: Understand a rational number as a point on the number line. Extend number lines and coordinate axes familiar from previous grades to represent points on the line and in the plane with negative number coordinates.

DD9C46712BC545948C4FE7099BFA64E8.description: Understand that positive and negative numbers are used together to describe quantities having opposite directions or values (e.g., temperature above/below zero, elevation above/below sea level, credits/debits, positive/negative electric charge); use positive and negative numbers to represent quantities in real-world contexts, explaining the meaning of 0 in each situation.

DF47998137B04160A5183DCA7AEB6DE4.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of numbers to the system of rational numbers.

98A59CC490BE44BBA92B536F55C52309.description: Find the greatest common factor of two whole numbers less than or equal to 100 and the least common multiple of two whole numbers less than or equal to 12. Use the distributive property to express a sum of two whole numbers 1-100 with a common factor as a multiple of a sum of two whole numbers with no common factor.

34FAEAF4CB4A4E0B8A836CDFD4603A49.description: Flexibly and efficiently add, subtract, multiply, and divide multi-digit decimals using strategies or algorithms based on place value, visual models, the relationship between operations and the properties of operations.

CC7AF4D977D4471889CA4684CC5C246E.description: Flexibly and efficiently compute with multi-digit numbers and find common factors and multiples.

AEEB5987FCA84F258A81010B33DBC539.description: Flexibly and efficiently divide multi-digit whole numbers using strategies or algorithms based on place value, area models, and the properties of operations.

5149A6A79579437C97BE52478F6F3B46.description: Interpret, represent and compute division of fractions by fractions; and solve word problems by using visual fraction models (e.g., tape diagrams, area models, or number lines), equations, and the relationship between multiplication and division.

D235A429F11A4FBBBB0C1242E4C24E8A.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication and division to divide fractions by fractions.

78EBF1B9FBC4434CA32B490DBD52CB9F.description: Use ratio reasoning to convert measurement units; manipulate and transform units appropriately when multiplying or dividing quantities.

1895C60738344E0F86F29DD31E25F8C7.description: Find a percent of a quantity as a rate per 100 (e.g., 30% of a quantity means 30/100 times the quantity); solve problems involving finding the whole, given a part and the percent.

7DFE4D71F1BA477496D27C8B758DBEDC.description: Solve unit rate problems including those involving unit pricing and constant speed.

24F1E8B0707844B0A681899F5EC8BB8E.description: Make tables of equivalent ratios relating quantities with whole number measurements, find missing values in the tables, and plot the pairs of values on the coordinate plane. Use tables to compare ratios.

B27B9170744143BB8F0FB6F8587B5AFA.description: Use ratio and rate reasoning to solve real-world and mathematical problems, e.g., by reasoning about tables of equivalent ratios, tape diagrams, double number lines, or equations.

01D04868F7E6426EA033CCCAC3B25ECA.description: Understand the concept of a unit rate a/b associated with a ratio a:b with b ≠ 0, and use rate language in the context of a ratio relationship.

E89FA45C47E04BC7BDC866977D5E5C1E.description: Understand the concept of a ratio and use ratio language to describe a ratio relationship between two quantities.

697C4A335ADA4141A86E45C9E971D8CB.description: Understand ratio concepts and use ratio reasoning to solve problems.

FAEAB70FA9634AE3A2CC9664589D5E1A.description: Represent three-dimensional figures using nets made up of rectangles and triangles, and use the nets to find the surface area of these figures. Apply these techniques in the context of solving real-world and mathematical problems.

ED45F488F5D7419D99BDAF063D51BFC1.description: Draw polygons in the coordinate plane given coordinates for the vertices; use coordinates to find the length of a side joining points with the same first coordinate or the same second coordinate. Apply these techniques in the context of solving real-world and mathematical problems.

7E5C00B7740D402B9BD0415618AC53E3.description: Find volumes of right rectangular prisms with fractional edge lengths by using physical or virtual unit cubes. Develop (construct) and apply the formulas V = l w h and V = B h to find volumes of right rectangular prisms in the context of solving real-world and mathematical problems.

222188C0CAB0430599B1BAD69FD915DC.description: Find the area of right triangles, other triangles, special quadrilaterals, and polygons by composing into rectangles or decomposing into triangles and other shapes; apply these techniques in the context of solving real-world and mathematical problems.

A60E796633024206A661FF5FF2179955.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving area, surface area, and volume.

6DCDEE82C569435DACB8AA95D499713D.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

939359FB86A14262A63D0825323ED1E6.description: Look for and make use of structure.

B59EE44CF84748ACB05C6CFB04CC7067.description: Construct viable arguments, and appreciate and critique the reasoning of others.

FEDCAF0D3F6F49B4B8D1A586232EC9D1.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

document.title: Wisconsin Standards for Mathematics

2255D210A1504C10AFC03226CE81668D.description: Design and use a simulation to generate frequencies for compound events.

3AC73E4EBD2349E3B5E1C871AC60B51A.description: Represent sample spaces for compound events using methods such as organized lists, tables and tree diagrams. For an event described in everyday language (e.g., "rolling double sixes"), identify the outcomes in the sample space which compose the event.

AF4CA248649940F8BB6BA1D4A187930B.description: Understand that, just as with simple events, the probability of a compound event is the fraction of outcomes in the sample space for which the compound event occurs.

9E17D11B100C49AF8748CF61D231AC68.description: Find probabilities of compound events using organized lists, tables, tree diagrams, and simulation.

51606F69A1C249FCAB6BDB7F0B32F062.description: Develop a probability model (which may not be uniform) by observing frequencies in data generated from a chance process.

6D55B1E95F7F46C88697D2A4FEDFA472.description: Develop a uniform probability model by assigning equal probability to all outcomes, and use the model to determine probabilities of events.

3DF02B8EC3954B358909D43781C8E76E.description: Develop a probability model and use it to find probabilities of events. Compare probabilities from a model to observed frequencies; if the agreement is not good, explain possible sources of the discrepancy.

ED0E075672AB4D38A6580B35B982C9AF.description: Approximate the probability of a chance event by collecting data on the chance process that produces it and observing its long-run relative frequency, and predict the approximate relative frequency given the probability.

28899562FCE5433AB2D9D67E47CD37DD.description: Understand that the probability of a chance event is a number between 0 and 1 that expresses the likelihood of the event occurring. Larger numbers indicate greater likelihood. A probability near 0 indicates an unlikely event, a probability around ½ indicates an event that is neither unlikely nor likely, and a probability near 1 indicates a likely event.

F5367753912842F9BD41B7E0CBA51C2F.description: Investigate chance processes and develop, use, and evaluate probability models.

5CFA509982E64CCAB658BAC62D1570C6.description: Use measures of center and measures of variability for numerical data from random samples to draw informal comparative inferences about two populations.

DB48BF351CA64CC19C86F9903A50EE14.description: Informally assess the degree of visual overlap of two numerical data distributions with similar variabilities, measuring the difference between the centers by expressing it as a multiple of a measure of variability.

5C66FCD24ECE4067A2A1B285A0F82F64.description: Draw informal comparative inferences about two populations.

DCDF76CBDFA74AC1909CFA52BAF3885A.description: Use data from a random sample to draw inferences about a population with an unknown characteristic of interest. Generate multiple samples (or simulated samples) of the same size to gauge the variation in estimates or predictions.

CE36A02292C94310878DBDFF2C1D538D.description: Understand that statistics can be used to gain information about a population by examining a sample of the population; generalizations about a population from a sample are valid only if the sample is representative of that population. Understand that random sampling tends to produce representative samples and support valid inferences.

9D42B19DDD2C4C25A5FB884C74B52089.description: Use random sampling to draw inferences about a population.

186BA4CB6B9B42B2B18F75F0AC9AE79F.description: Solve word problems leading to inequalities of the form px + q > r or px + q < r, where p, q, and r are specific rational numbers. Graph the solution set of the inequality and interpret it in the context of the problem.

4B1BFF021972411AB1635DA8169513D7.description: Solve word problems leading to equations of the form px + q = r and p(x + q) = r, where p, q, and r are specific rational numbers. Flexibly and efficiently apply the properties of operations and equality to solve equations of these forms. Compare an algebraic solution to an arithmetic solution, identifying the sequence of the operations used in each approach.

58F95FBEA4A34AD1ABF901C67B526627.description: Use variables to represent quantities in a real-world or mathematical problem, and construct simple equations and inequalities to solve problems by reasoning about the quantities.

1B2CA06BF3994699B763A1BC93599053.description: Solve multi-step real-life and mathematical problems posed with positive and negative rational numbers in any form (whole numbers, fractions, and decimals), using tools strategically. Apply properties of operations to calculate with numbers in any form; convert between forms as appropriate; and assess the reasonableness of answers using mental computation and estimation strategies.

9035F3D6678743B1BC9FD3A1C9A6B842.description: Solve real-life and mathematical problems using numerical and algebraic expressions and equations.

990ECEEAABF6403F8EE87689FE9A85D9.description: Understand that rewriting an expression in different forms in a problem context can shed light on the problem and how the quantities in it are related.

E57708010D6E47029FCCA2EAD7F4D1E0.description: Apply properties of operations as strategies to add, subtract, factor, and expand linear expressions with rational coefficients.

464D14E102694DC5A972D464557CFA39.description: Use properties of operations to generate equivalent expressions.

223FD85B07D34C7EAFA83FFE751A998F.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving the four operations with rational numbers.

99C3808D868A4227B7A9984FB214FB3F.description: Convert a rational number to a decimal using long division; know that the decimal form of a rational number terminates in 0s or eventually repeats.

59F9CB492D604447A1489D16D07C0532.description: Apply properties of operations as strategies to multiply and divide rational numbers.

17DDF12C729643DB8858B19985EFBB3B.description: Understand that integers can be divided, provided that the divisor is not zero, and every quotient of integers (with non-zero divisor) is a rational number. If p and q are integers, then -(p/q) = (-p)/q = p/(-q). Interpret quotients of rational numbers by describing real-world contexts.

4C97398A29204DA1AFFECFDBBBBAB1F0.description: Understand that multiplication is extended from fractions to rational numbers by requiring that operations continue to satisfy the properties of operations, particularly the distributive property, leading to products such as (-1)(-1) = 1 and the rules for multiplying signed numbers. Interpret products of rational numbers by describing real-world contexts.

7287385285EA4AF7AEF376E00A77F34A.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication and division and of fractions to multiply and divide rational numbers.

3C74CB38E5124239AC54B387D4FDD6A8.description: Apply properties of operations as strategies to add and subtract rational numbers.

B3EF640F6DFE45ECA2C3DDA9B0103FC3.description: Understand subtraction of rational numbers as adding the additive inverse, p - q = p + (-q). Show that the distance between two rational numbers on the number line is the absolute value of their difference, and apply this principle in real-world contexts.

ED97A7C8785D40FF9256038B8591810B.description: Understand p + q as the number located a distance |q| from p, in the positive or negative direction depending on whether q is positive or negative. Show that a number and its opposite have a sum of 0 (are additive inverses). Interpret sums of rational numbers by describing real-world contexts.

0BB2E41C5E6F48C0B0622F807B76A36C.description: Describe situations in which opposite quantities combine to make 0.

5D843BD6567F4131BF522606160E098A.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of addition and subtraction to add and subtract rational numbers; represent addition and subtraction on a horizontal or vertical number line.

8E541F5992D846A1823BE485A0F23399.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of operations with fractions to add, subtract, multiply, and divide rational numbers.

36C1E265FB454DDEA609A102C665DBB6.description: Use proportional relationships to solve multi-step ratio and percent problems.

ECCC47BA97B44201BCD2758C0C425952.description: Explain what a point (x, y) on the graph of a proportional relationship means in terms of the situation, with special attention to the points (0, 0) and (1, r) where r is the unit rate.

54100C74D6454A22A504AB40B7C7FCAE.description: Identify the constant of proportionality (unit rate) in tables, graphs, equations, diagrams, and verbal descriptions of proportional relationships.

3DB798F6524D49E6A1A0242C525EC009.description: Decide whether two quantities are in a proportional relationship, e.g., by testing for equivalent ratios in a table or graphing on a coordinate plane and observing whether the graph is a straight line through the origin.

32E9E41FDBF54B65882BEB01FF12D2FA.description: Recognize and represent proportional relationships between quantities.

6ACA3E1FFD284117925C0A4DD6CAB78D.description: Compute unit rates associated with ratios of fractions, including ratios of lengths, areas and other quantities measured in like or different units.

FBFDCB9C1388465C89F058BFB4E6BA06.description: Analyze proportional relationships and use them to solve real-world and mathematical problems.

6D88AC5F4FEE4F20ACE87454FFE12F77.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving area, volume and surface area of two- and three-dimensional objects composed of triangles, quadrilaterals, polygons, cubes, and right prisms.

0335BBBA65EE494E9E860095318DA8AF.description: Use facts about supplementary, complementary, vertical, and adjacent angles in a multi-step problem to write and solve simple equations for an unknown angle in a figure.

07710E5DC5AF410194FEFCDABC69FEA4.description: Know the formulas for the area and circumference of a circle and use them to solve problems; give an informal derivation of the relationship between the circumference and area of a circle.

C548FDFB815044EFA8500A3D1CD8F282.description: Solve real-life and mathematical problems involving angle measure, area, surface area, and volume.

27356942951D4D4EBAAA5EDED809004F.description: Describe the two-dimensional figures that result from slicing three dimensional figures parallel to the base, as in plane sections of right rectangular prisms and right rectangular pyramids.

4C924F1AE9604CA28B3DB3D43864C648.description: Draw (freehand, with ruler and protractor, and with technology) geometric shapes with given conditions. Focus on constructing triangles from three measures of angles or sides, noticing when the conditions determine a unique triangle, more than one triangle, or no triangle.

C5F96347DBDD46E08D6B0CF1832FB6A8.description: Solve problems involving scale drawings of geometric figures, including computing actual lengths and areas from a scale drawing and reproducing a scale drawing at a different scale.

5A24E59BF04C4C1986A9C2734619DFD1.description: Draw, construct, and describe geometrical figures and describe the relationships between them.

D0D6A69C0B4C46E8B3219F5FD137794C.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

AB4F94B1DF52453F9844AF750956EFD2.description: Look for and make use of structure.

D0532B9A04AB4BF584B556C71DC4D363.description: Construct viable arguments, and appreciate and critique the reasoning of others.

2DB8505FDCC647BF92655D25F4DF1D82.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

document.title: Wisconsin Standards for Mathematics

15481A93629A4E7BA43B7A1823F8AA52.description: Describe qualitatively the functional relationship between two quantities by analyzing a graph (e.g., where the function is increasing or decreasing, linear or nonlinear, continuous or discrete). Sketch a graph that exhibits the qualitative features of a function that has been described verbally.

91E608F4F8BF4C908226500540D0F94F.description: Construct a function to model a linear relationship between two quantities. Determine the rate of change and initial value of the function from a description of a relationship or from two (x, y) values, including reading these from a table or from a graph. Interpret the rate of change and initial value of a linear function in terms of the situation it models, and in terms of its graph or a table of values.

5BC149A01F36485082685EED7EEAA353.description: Use functions to model relationships between quantities.

6E86400449AC47C78DB667190866F7FC.description: Interpret the equation y = mx + b as defining a linear function, whose graph is a straight line; give examples of functions that are not linear.

476268A0CA6046D587CD36500595D5E0.description: Compare properties of two functions each represented in a different way (algebraically, graphically, numerically in tables, or by verbal descriptions).

F08A4458A53A436881121B80DCA6B057.description: Understand that a function is a rule that assigns to each input exactly one output. The graph of a numerically valued function is the set of ordered pairs consisting of an input and the corresponding output. Function notation is not required in Grade 8.

6B48B8947BA34F608221FB03C81DC6E6.description: Understand that patterns of association can also be seen in bivariate categorical data by displaying frequencies and relative frequencies in a two-way table. Construct and interpret a two-way table summarizing data on two categorical variables collected from the same subjects. Use relative frequencies calculated for rows or columns to describe possible association between the two variables.

9A19FB4DA83D405DB4408D49F8C62212.description: Use the equation of a linear model to solve problems in the context of bivariate measurement data, interpreting the slope and intercept.

ABF93FB0EB1B451CA1E2B2D4441E0C56.description: Know that straight lines are widely used to model relationships between two quantitative variables. For scatter plots that suggest a linear association, informally fit a straight line, and informally assess the model fit by judging the closeness of the data points to the line.

2FC1B068DC904522B1B61E78325B67E9.description: Construct and interpret scatter plots for bivariate measurement data to investigate patterns of association between two quantities. Describe patterns such as clustering, outliers, positive or negative association, linear association, and nonlinear association.

C3C3530BCB6B452397430C97C932B3A5.description: Investigate patterns of association in bivariate data.

23E2862901404A779E24AAA743AD4500.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems leading to two linear equations in two variables.

91B16E4D72AB47D7B0AE3DDE097CAA66.description: Solve systems of two linear equations in two variables by graphing and analyzing tables. Solve simple cases represented in algebraic symbols by inspection.

89FFBE37F15B49368B34B8548D7AFA8C.description: Understand that solutions to a system of two linear equations in two variables correspond to points of intersection of their graphs, because points of intersection satisfy both equations simultaneously.

D13C1F7D9B3D4F63BCFAC143B8134D00.description: Analyze and solve pairs of simultaneous linear equations.

DCE578348E39465987088EF50EA8F168.description: Solve linear equations with rational number coefficients, including equations whose solutions require expanding expressions using the distributive property and collecting like terms.

35987ADCADF24FB6B15F1D8A1051E286.description: Give examples of linear equations in one variable with one solution, infinitely many solutions, or no solutions. Show which of these possibilities is the case by successively transforming the given equation into equivalent forms.

77EE6764BC8B474896B23880F461BFE3.description: Solve linear equations in one variable.

9F46B72145CA4910B91ACD59E3C7192E.description: Analyze and solve linear equations and pairs of simultaneous linear equations.

D9F23B9DC740407CB16865A9D359C45C.description: Use similar triangles to explain why the slope m is the same between any two distinct points on a non-vertical line in the coordinate plane; derive the equation y = mx for a line through the origin and the equation y = mx + b for a line intercepting the vertical axis at b.

6D6DA3B8E65E4207BA1C15A2BDF6ED93.description: Graph proportional relationships, interpreting the unit rate as the slope of the graph. Compare two different proportional relationships represented in different ways.

6F9D0AAEF88C493692A40406152E5BC7.description: Understand the connections between proportional relationships, lines, and linear equations.

84B79D5A162343FCB4D80F30EA5666C4.description: Use technology to interpret and perform operations with numbers expressed in scientific notation. Choose units of appropriate size for measurements of very large or very small quantities (e.g., use millimeters per year for seafloor spreading).

178BE3DFC5A7432E8DBF63558A9DD9E6.description: Use numbers expressed in the form of a single digit times an integer power of 10 to estimate very large or very small quantities, and to express how many times as much one is than the other.

38EBB01D30254E0ABC7686583F042FBE.description: Use square root and cube root symbols to represent solutions to equations of the form x² = p and x³ = p, where p is a positive rational number. Evaluate square roots of small perfect squares and cube roots of small perfect cubes. Know that √2 is irrational.

BEFDDBB19DDA43FBA8665FF874D86E6B.description: Know and apply the properties of integer exponents to generate equivalent numerical expressions.

C4C63E063F0F415D8A6B88AB967ABAF2.description: Work with radicals and integer exponents.

1CCDF5B318F34DC8B398D0E8B93CA891.description: Use rational approximations of irrational numbers to compare the size of irrational numbers, locate them approximately on a number line, and estimate the value of expressions (e.g., π²).

0A6553DE9E384BDDA2FAFDDDA198F765.description: Know that numbers that are not rational are called irrational. Understand informally that every number has a decimal expansion; for rational numbers show that the decimal expansion repeats eventually, and use patterns to rewrite a decimal expansion that repeats into a rational number.

C42A7278B05243A69AC99C08C7FA6BB5.description: Know that there are numbers that are not rational, and approximate them by rational numbers.

91DFF1EA807645BDA181B68EB4ED4BD3.description: Know the relationship among the formulas for the volumes of cones, cylinders, and spheres (given the same height and diameter) and use them to solve real-world and mathematical problems.

54A812DCE1194120B03E3078FE1C202A.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving volume of cylinders, cones, and spheres.

85DCD6E6FA544C778B2E999F5013EC22.description: Apply the Pythagorean Theorem to find the distance between two points in a coordinate system.

D14B16ACBFC741B0AEB4AF3B63339F44.description: Apply the Pythagorean Theorem to determine unknown side lengths in right triangles in real-world and mathematical problems in two and three dimensions.

F12B40A2854D49869479AED927DBB034.description: Justify the relationship between the lengths of the legs and the length of the hypotenuse of a right triangle, and the converse of the Pythagorean theorem.

C8EFE74708F046B9A270FB57805993D3.description: Understand and apply the Pythagorean Theorem.

958B426ACD1945A1B46DA2031AA567CE.description: Use informal arguments to establish facts about the angle sum and exterior angle of triangles, about the angles created when parallel lines are cut by a transversal, and the angle-angle criterion for similarity of triangles.

DB13A12AB8DB42368A7B0D3DF8943BB4.description: Understand that a two-dimensional figure is similar to another if the second can be obtained from the first by a sequence of rotations, reflections, translations, and dilations; given two similar two-dimensional figures, describe a sequence that exhibits the similarity between them.

10DD981550AC4152A4C358B928DE9DC4.description: Describe the effect of dilations, translations, rotations, and reflections on two-dimensional figures using coordinates.

626E6CC8B54447C19B62A60EF5AC54C2.description: Understand that a two-dimensional figure is congruent to another if the second can be obtained from the first by a sequence of rotations, reflections, and translations; given two congruent figures, describe a sequence that exhibits the congruence between them.

E7A8E992FDCA4E649D2DB07ACEEDC2E6.description: Parallel lines are taken to parallel lines.

1F6F45246003496DBF505A5A61C16769.description: Angles are taken to angles of the same measure.

DDE581CB2FB74C88A940EE882921D9EF.description: Lines are taken to lines, and line segments to line segments of the same length.

C485F3C0D94640ABA60C6A722817C429.description: Verify experimentally the properties of rotations, reflections, and translations:

38CCD54D828A4901BE96A9BDA6524D98.description: Analyze decisions and strategies using probability concepts (e.g., balancing expected gains and risk, medical product testing, choosing an investment option, deciding when to kick an extra point vs. two point conversion after a touchdown in football).

F86C0A2FEF7242A7AB2F6894314F7362.description: Use probabilities to make fair decisions (e.g., drawing for a party door prize where attendees earn one entry to the drawing for each activity they complete, using an electronic spinner to pick a team spokesperson at random from a group, flip a coin to decide which of two friends gets to choose the movie, using a random number generator to select people to include in a sample for an experiment).

29009A7FAF8749539D46224AACB194E5.description: Evaluate and compare strategies on the basis of expected values.

582B088650CF4162AA4D37173EEF3766.description: Use probability to evaluate outcomes of decisions

B2D6FD1A5F924C6D961AB87B072C7D83.description: (+) Develop a probability distribution for a random variable defined for a sample space in which theoretical probabilities can be calculated; find the expected value.

58301FD57EBC4FF198292A8B1B766790.description: (+) Define a random variable for a quantity of interest by assigning a numerical value to each event in a sample space; graph the corresponding probability distribution using the same graphical displays as for data distributions.

B43677D3063F4BADB57E8A8051B97521.description: Use a representation such as a two-way table or venn diagram to apply the Addition Rule, P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) – P(A and B), and interpret the answer in terms of the model.

12141A12A41F4070AB10452B1571D856.description: Use a representation such as a two-way table or venn diagram to find the conditional probability of A given B as the fraction of B's outcomes that also belong to A, and interpret the answer in terms of the model.

F3FD74C1C9034C9AA5B7AA937814AE88.description: Use the rules of probability to compute probabilities of compound events in a uniform probability model.

B4E04A7213934662AC1238C6392AE9FC.description: Recognize and explain the concepts of conditional probability and independence in everyday language and everyday situations.

4C75DAC68D554EBD995DA042FC442DF5.description: Represent data from two categorical variables using two-way frequency tables and/or venn diagrams. Interpret the representation when two categories are associated with each object being classified. Use the representation as a sample space to decide if events are independent and to approximate conditional probabilities.

D9549E572BDA4A3BAFB39D3010306128.description: Understand that two events A and B are independent if the probability of A and B occurring together is the product of their probabilities, and use this characterization to determine if they are independent.

5557412076F144998B8E7AA50C352DE7.description: Describe events as subsets of a sample space (the set of outcomes) using characteristics (or categories) of the outcomes, or as unions, intersections, or complements of other events ("or," "and," "not").

5DCE69B7266B44C19B3741C332546F92.description: Conditional Probability and the Rules of Probability

1BE93F67FA5544D892BBECAB3EA89C0F.description: Use data from a sample survey to estimate a population mean or proportion; develop a margin of error through the use of simulation models for random sampling.

8D3F8F5D96F54F29A15FE72F9DF5F96A.description: Recognize the purposes of and differences among sample surveys, experiments, and observational studies; explain how randomization relates to each.

26BE09480C6E421FB29F97D7951C1C32.description: Understand and evaluate random processes underlying statistical experiments.

13686DA832DC49398C03495336300829.description: Justify that, given a system of two equations in two variables, replacing one equation by the sum of that equation and a multiple of the other produces a system with the same solutions.

339232C122BA4F92B9A45D9012A37B59.description: Solve quadratic equations by inspection (e.g., for x 2 = 49), taking square roots, completing the square, the quadratic formula, factoring, and graphing as appropriate to the initial form of the equation. Recognize when the quadratic formula gives complex solutions and write them as a ± bi for real numbers a and b.

D9E2FFCAAC1E48FCAE8993CF8F89A528.description: Solve linear equations and inequalities in one variable, including equations with coefficients represented by letters.

E4397A7E467B477F9B7E87C26A2D6727.description: Solve equations and inequalities in one variable.

AEEB53E7A153433BA638A014531F5EBA.description: Solve simple rational and radical equations in one variable, and give examples showing how extraneous solutions may arise.

686E5A8539474F93A9FC15D80C596372.description: Explain each step in solving a simple equation as following from the equality of numbers asserted at the previous step, starting from the assumption that the original equation has a solution. Construct a viable argument to justify a solution method.

07141DDD2DCD40CE9A2F96C7CC05E111.description: Understand solving equations as a process of reasoning and explain the reasoning.

9E85F447888345F1A906773A121BBC99.description: Rearrange formulas to highlight a quantity of interest, using the same reasoning as in solving equations.

D8F47152F4984BE684C67D6A27D0509A.description: Represent constraints by equations or inequalities, and by systems of equations and/or inequalities, and interpret solutions as viable or nonviable options in a modeling context.

01F8D91310374CB08CAA6367D060A492.description: Create equations in two or more variables to represent relationships between quantities; graph equations on coordinate axes with labels and scales.

3EC6B2136EFE49A8BB7490F01410823D.description: Create equations and inequalities in one variable and use them to solve problems. Include equations arising from linear and quadratic functions, and simple rational and exponential functions.

2A439396D36B47768DEB5F9A30F7C809.description: Create equations that describe numbers or relationships.

A86D68D65EBA43DEBEB4E28A6979AA43.description: Understand that rational expressions form a system analogous to the rational numbers, closed under addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division by a nonzero rational expression; add, subtract, multiply, and divide rational expressions.

0C829BF3645743D9BFD1F7BD99D23526.description: Rewrite simple rational expressions in different forms; write a(x)/b(x) in the form q(x) + r(x)/b(x), where a(x), b(x), q(x), and r(x) are polynomials with the degree of r(x) less than the degree of b(x), using inspection, long division, or, for the more complicated examples, a computer algebra system.

2616735B778E4652993F938AA5896C9F.description: (+) Know and apply the Binomial Theorem for the expansion of (x + y)n in powers of x and y for a positive integer n, where x and y are any numbers, with coefficients determined for example by Pascal's Triangle.

10B1C7AC7AF74C8EACC865DB90DD851C.description: Prove polynomial identities and use them to describe numerical relationships.

A37CE1B9EC3145649719485C351CCFFA.description: Use polynomial identities to solve problems.

06D24F3E076845519C8DB734101EC08A.description: Identify zeros of polynomials when suitable factorizations are available, and use the zeros to construct a rough graph of the function defined by the polynomial.

1A43E920E4EC44C8879EE9339B8D9A6C.description: Know and apply the Remainder Theorem: For a polynomial p(x) and a number a, the remainder on division by x – a is p(a), so p(a) = 0 if and only if (x – a) is a factor of p(x).

95A916788A76406F99CE40280B1466CF.description: Understand the relationship between zeros and factors of polynomials.

528FA2B66F8647C887AC048DDA9175DC.description: Understand that polynomials form a system analogous to the integers, namely, they are closed under the operations of addition, subtraction, and multiplication; add, subtract, and multiply polynomials.

F8A1D135BE164BCEAED9C8597DAB018B.description: Arithmetic with Polynomials and Rational Expressions

E53C4502442C4049BA28127087865FB2.description: Derive the formula for the sum of a finite geometric series (when the common ratio is not 1), and use the formula to solve problems.

6B43C5FAEA0342D6840D62C59173A16C.description: Use the properties of exponents to transform expressions for exponential functions.

D7DC625DCF2847449ED0F5D785722E0A.description: Complete the square in a quadratic expression to reveal the maximum or minimum value of the function it defines.

97F7E97CEFA641C288CF1B03B11C9A27.description: Factor a quadratic expression to reveal the zeros of the function it defines.

7C63D79A3BA84341B1EC116940D28A9F.description: Choose and produce an equivalent form of an expression to reveal and explain properties of the quantity represented by the expression.

D6D14218730142E0ACD2ECDAB6794EB3.description: Write expressions in equivalent forms to solve problems.

A86A5F0A17934F15AC350972BF94C7AE.description: Use the structure of an expression to identify ways to rewrite it.

483172EB59B74460A53A2EE3C719BAA2.description: Interpret complicated expressions by viewing one or more of their parts as a single entity.

8EB4F1B9022248C9BF04EBF88D2810EA.description: Interpret parts of an expression, such as terms, factors, and coefficients.

1A873759AB084541B45BC6EB7C1A4B9C.description: Interpret expressions that represent a quantity in terms of its context.

76A7D4184448436DB4EB04E7718C2D1E.description: (+) Work with 2 x 2 matrices as transformations of the plane, and interpret the absolute value of the determinant in terms of area.

901749FEEA2C47FA9957F01454474302.description: (+) Multiply a vector (regarded as a matrix with one column) by a matrix of suitable dimensions to produce another vector. Work with matrices as transformations of vectors.

F531F1D711D5435882D82CC0E574BF7C.description: (+) Understand that the zero and identity matrices play a role in matrix addition and multiplication similar to the role of 0 and 1 in the real numbers. The determinant of a square matrix is nonzero if and only if the matrix has a multiplicative inverse.

34FC0155A5CD420FB4EB77DFECE9CEDC.description: (+) Understand that, unlike multiplication of numbers, matrix multiplication for square matrices is not a commutative operation, but still satisfies the associative and distributive properties.

488C4640B3FE4072974430BBE359ED12.description: (+) Add, subtract, and multiply matrices of appropriate dimensions.

9D5CF8822CF34AF8A2330D97B9BAE0E7.description: (+) Multiply matrices by scalars to produce new matrices, e.g., as when all of the payoffs in a game are doubled.

11483E1E22F241E9B129D23EB22C715A.description: (+) Use matrices to represent and manipulate data, e.g., to represent payoffs or incidence relationships in a network.

3590BE91519A4A6783BC059FEFDE7FCF.description: Perform operations on matrices and use matrices in applications.

DF3FD56D27C6407EAD9A9F423532BBFD.description: Compute the magnitude of a scalar multiple cv using ||cv|| = |c|v. Compute the direction of cv knowing that when |c|v ≠ 0, the direction of cv is either along v (for c > 0) or against v (for c < 0).

69AA64234BE444BE80909730585AC06F.description: Represent scalar multiplication graphically by scaling vectors and possibly reversing their direction; perform scalar multiplication component-wise, e.g., as c(vx, vy) = (cvx, cvy).

1B070C55E2FF4153990AD4CE124DF826.description: (+) Multiply a vector by a scalar.

4446647D7A1F4AEBB3E6F897CC2F5BE2.description: Understand vector subtraction v - w as v + (-w), where -w is the additive inverse of w, with the same magnitude as w and pointing in the opposite direction. Represent vector subtraction graphically by connecting the tips in the appropriate order, and perform vector subtraction component-wise.

9263CD8AA1DD4A7EAE8C570C8056107D.description: Given two vectors in magnitude and direction form, determine the magnitude and direction of their sum.

ABD1BC7C325F48C29CE64C976F953CF7.description: Add vectors end-to-end, component-wise, and by the parallelogram rule. Understand that the magnitude of a sum of two vectors is typically not the sum of the magnitudes.

6AA0C611CD194AA9B1BE8B8E745EA32C.description: (+) Solve problems involving velocity and other quantities that can be represented by vectors.

B9E09D17FD2742B49FAE6B4AE34FF1E3.description: (+) Find the components of a vector by subtracting the coordinates of an initial point from the coordinates of a terminal point.

E3F4098910914935ACD415CAA422F875.description: (+) Recognize vector quantities as having both magnitude and direction. Represent vector quantities by directed line segments, and use appropriate symbols for vectors and their magnitudes (e.g., v, |v|, ||v||, v).

D580580BCB77477BAB452513CDF81B99.description: Represent and model with vector quantities.

5CB63C64252E4D9AB9C90ABE2D06D2CD.description: (+) Know the Fundamental Theorem of Algebra; show that it is true for quadratic polynomials.

174652BC4DF3450183219DCF23AC7FCD.description: (+) Extend polynomial identities to the complex numbers.

4EE2F82563C44500AA670657D77A6E77.description: Solve quadratic equations with real coefficients that have complex solutions. Recognize when the quadratic formula gives complex solutions and write them as a ± bi for real numbers a and b.

D4721DDF87D1485B80FF312144988B24.description: Use complex numbers in polynomial identities and equations.

B224C10ECC734CE68C6152D8B4712F48.description: (+) Calculate the distance between numbers in the complex plane as the modulus of the difference, and the midpoint of a segment as the average of the numbers at its endpoints.

096A37FC290E4842B38DF979C2C2FC6F.description: (+) Represent addition, subtraction, multiplication, and conjugation of complex numbers geometrically on the complex plane; use properties of this representation for computation.

7D97CEDECF244613A5590509D6C82E18.description: (+) Represent complex numbers on the complex plane in rectangular and polar form (including real and imaginary numbers), and explain why the rectangular and polar forms of a given complex number represent the same number.

A9853BBD9D03491DBBE4D8F93BEB588C.description: Represent complex numbers and their operations on the complex plane.

8D64AADBF7CC401CBA5E30EBE6DC2ADC.description: (+) Find the conjugate of a complex number; use conjugates to find moduli (absolute values) and quotients of complex numbers.

62CB7FE198624BDF88F8203B6BBD6F2F.description: (+) Use the relation i²= −1 and the commutative, associative, and distributive properties to add, subtract, and multiply complex numbers.

8D2BEAE31D46455594658EEB459EC935.description: Know there is a complex number i such that i²= −1, and every complex number has the form a + bi with a and b real. Understand why complex numbers exist.

C7E5067E22A445639FFEE909AEC5AC4A.description: Perform arithmetic operations with complex numbers.

C87D5B97DC984F79B57B1061080072CC.description: Choose a level of accuracy appropriate to limitations on measurement when reporting quantities.

C7217E8164694968BC61C18DEDE5AF01.description: Define appropriate quantities for the purpose of descriptive modeling.

A5CBBD516E56475486053ED77DDBC136.description: Use units as a way to understand problems and to guide the solution of multi-step problems; choose and interpret units consistently in formulas; choose and interpret the scale and the origin in graphs and data displays.

EDB3B94672A94E0AA306365140F155D3.description: Reason quantitatively and use units to solve problems.

75C6251B3AEA409CB4A6C73D83D6B14F.description: Explain why the sum or product of two rational numbers is rational; that the sum of a rational number and an irrational number is irrational; and that the product of a nonzero rational number and an irrational number is irrational.

2EF783B9B53945F781BDB7DCE177888F.description: Use properties of rational and irrational numbers.

EC0D6B08859E4171835798E2664B48F0.description: Rewrite expressions involving radicals and rational exponents using the properties of exponents.

6D64C295A5E04F3FAF65F2B47E4AA44D.description: Explain how the definition of the meaning of rational exponents follows from extending the properties of integer exponents.

11D6226961CE47C6ADBB97C202A7A8CD.description: Extend the properties of exponents to rational exponents.

4D77970265AA43D5BE7E0963E7B42901.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

9944EA9BD3334DEEB16B3A8E7222BF40.description: Look for and make use of structure.

096C81A4841F4B6AB6E8830272AA4BD2.description: Construct viable arguments, and appreciate and critique the reasoning of others.

F6E58CA04E9647E7A62EEC498E65B7B1.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.
